# Loqui UI/UX Plan 03 — Routes & Settings Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Revision 2.** This revision answers the independent Codex review (`.omc/research/ui-review/reviews/plan-03-codex.md`, verdict "needs rework": 2 Critical, 15 Important, 5 Minor). See "Review response" below.

**Revision 3.** This revision answers Codex's second review (`.omc/research/ui-review/reviews/plan-03-codex-r2.md`, pinned at `c912d19`, verdict "still needs rework": 3 Critical, 6 Important, 1 Minor). See "Round-2 review response" below. It is aligned with the spec at `7f31ece`.

**Goal:** Give Loqui one routing model and rebuild Settings on top of it:
- the route graph (contract §5.1), which answers "which task runs where, and is it usable?" for all 11 routes, using the same validation the executors use;
- a Patchbay switchboard that shows every route at once (SET-R1 B);
- one route planner, so preview, commit and Undo describe the same configuration. On-device moves are instant; any new off-device recipient or payload is staged behind Apply (SET-R3 B);
- cartridge model cards with real radio semantics (SET-R4 B);
- a main-owned credential authority and keyring with generation-bound verification health (SET-R5 C);
- a storage list whose counts and deletions come from the same main-owned predicates (SET-R7 A);
- settings search with live controls (SET-R2 A);
- 13 Settings quick wins.

**Architecture:**
- **Route graph.** `src/lib/routeGraph.ts` is a pure, Node-loadable resolver. `src/lib/routes.ts` re-exports it and adds the snapshot builder, `routeSnapshotFromSettings` and the React hooks.
- **Readiness facts.**
  - Facts come from `src/stores/routeFactsStore.ts` through network-free preload calls: model inventories, support models, main-confirmed credential presence and key health. No Codex start, discovery or verification ever happens there.
  - Unknown facts resolve to `unknown`, never `ready`.
  - Sealed state has one renderer authority, `src/stores/sealedStore.ts`.
- **Route changes.** Every provider, model, mode and endpoint change in Settings goes through `src/lib/routePlanner.ts`. It simulates the write on a copy of the settings, resolves all 11 routes before and after, and returns one patch and its Undo patch. `src/stores/routeDraftStore.ts` applies the patch when every change stays on the device or keeps the same recipient and payload; otherwise it stages the change behind the Apply bar, which lists every affected route.
- **Credentials.** `src/helpers/credentialAuthority.js` in main owns credential presence, acknowledged saves, change events, generations and undoable removal. The renderer never holds a secret, and readiness is only what main has confirmed. Authenticated model discovery and key verification happen only on an explicit button that names the receiving host.
- **Storage.** `src/helpers/storageOps.js` in main counts and deletes with the same predicates, and returns typed outcomes.

**Tech Stack:** React 19, TypeScript, zustand, Tailwind CSS 4, Radix Dialog, react-i18next, Electron IPC (`preload.js`, `src/helpers/ipcHandlers.js`), better-sqlite3, Node `node:test` with `tsx`, and Vite SSR (`test/lib/rendererTestHarness.js`) for renderer modules that import the settings store.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-15-loqui-uiux-overhaul.md` (at `7f31ece`; contracts consolidated at `091d198`): the Plan 03 row in §3, decisions D1, D4 and D6, constraints §4, contracts §5.1 (owned here), §5.3, §5.4 and §5.6 (consumed). Visual acceptance is the picked variant cards in `design-explorations/loqui-uiux-review.html#ch-settings`. Their source is `design-explorations/loqui-uiux-review/parts/05-settings.html`:

## PR #50 review follow-up

The two findings in the [GitHub review](https://github.com/snowopsdev/loqui/pull/50#issuecomment-6196856244) are addressed in this implementation plan:

- **Credential reset (Task 2).** The authority fences new mutations, invalidates queued work and Undo, and drains active writes before erasure. The module-wide `.env` queue uses the same reset boundary for independent writers. Reset waits for every erase operation even when one fails; overlapping resets cannot lower another reset's fence. Deferred tests cover active and queued saves, multi-field Undo, independent plaintext writes, overlapping resets and erase failure.
- **Storage snapshot identity (Task 14).** Audio and history previews carry main-produced identity digests. The confirm returns its reviewed digests, and main compares them before deletion; equal counts cannot authorize deletion of replacement items. Tests replace transcripts and recordings while preserving counts, including a recording replaced at the same filename. A stale confirmation requires a fresh review.

These are executable planning changes; app implementation remains outside this PR revision.

## Round-2 review response

This answers Codex's second review (`plan-03-codex-r2.md`, pinned at `c912d19`). Every finding is fixed in the task steps and the test code. Where a finding asked for production wiring, the tests go through the registered IPC handlers, the real `IPCHandlers` constructor, or the real `EnvironmentManager` persistence bodies over a fake filesystem. No finding is rejected. Five are partly disputed, and each partial dispute is in the last column, with its evidence.

| Finding | Status | How | Partial dispute (evidence) |
|---|---|---|---|

Vertex's explicit source is main-persisted and migrated once before renderer admission; later key presence cannot change it. Source edits stage/review/apply for all active Vertex routes; saving/removing/undoing a key changes readiness only. The executor uses that source, and `enterpriseVerifyTarget` preserves it. Task 1's graph derives hosts/readiness (Bedrock requires a complete static pair or profile); main facts expose only booleans/hosts. Task 3 syncs five getters and the source migration gate before enterprise facts are admitted. Unnamed enterprise edits stage and Apply stays blocked until facts are known. Tests run the real helper/SDK under injected environment variables, assert mounted Vertex secret save/remove/Undo never move the committed host, and exercise source changes only after Apply. A Task 18 guard covers every enterprise source setter. | Hosts remain derived in the pure graph so staged values can be previewed without IPC. |
| **R2-2/R3-2** (Critical) Reset must fence credential writes, Undo and the independent `.env` queue | Fixed in plan | **Task 2.** `credentials.reset(erase)` fences credential mutations, drops every Undo token, bumps generations and drains slot writes. `clearAllPersistedData()` then fences every module-wide `.env` writer, invalidates queued `envWriteQueue` jobs, drains an active write before erasing, and holds the fence through deletion. `saveAllKeysToEnvFile` refuses during the fence and skips `dotenv.config` if its write was invalidated. A deferred real `save-all-keys-to-env` race proves no plaintext `.env` or in-memory secret returns after reset. | none |
| **R2-3** (Critical) Two input interfaces cannot typecheck | Fixed | **Tasks 2, 8, 9.** One type, `AcknowledgedSecretSave = (value) => Promise<SecretSaveResult>`, exported from `ApiKeyInput.tsx`, is used by `ApiKeyInput.setApiKey`, `StagedCredentialInput.save` and `OpenAICompatiblePanel.saveApiKey`. The `() => {}` / `() => undefined` fallbacks become `unavailableSecretSave`. Task 2 fixes every caller that exists before Task 9. Each task's verification runs the real `npm run typecheck` (`package.json:63`). A test checks that the unavailable fallback resolves `{ ok: false, error: "unavailable" }`. | none |
| **R2-4** Main exposes uncommitted secrets and can bind health to the wrong value | Fixed | **Tasks 2, 11.** The authority keeps a committed snapshot while a write is pending. Verify tests the captured committed value at its generation, never `process.env`. Tests over the real persistence bodies: a pending first save is not listed and Verify waits; a replacement that commits during Verify gives `superseded`; a failed replacement tests and records the restored key. | none |

The empty-save fallback is deleted, and a Task 18 guard keeps it gone. Mounted tests: OpenRouter Remove → toast → Undo after the field unmounts, custom slots and pairs. | Two partial disputes. (1) **Test placement:** the mounted OpenRouter Undo test is in Task 12, not Task 9, because token removal lands in Task 12. Task 9 tests the identity flow (`credentialId === "openrouter"`). (2) **Bedrock session token:** under whole-pair removal, the optional `bedrockSessionToken` can no longer be removed alone. It uses `cortiTokenUrl` for Corti speech, `resolveProviderRequest` for the rest, and main's committed enterprise config plus `enterpriseRouteFacts(process.env)` for the enterprise identities. A Bedrock endpoint override names the override host; a Vertex env key names the express host with `environmentKey`. `KeyringPanel` drops `providerHosts` and `useMemo([])`, and re-describes on `keyring-changed`, `credentials-changed` and Corti region changes. The enterprise Test button labels its host from `describeVerify`. Tests: through a real `IPCHandlers`, the described host equals the host `net.fetch` received (Corti `eu` → `us`, groq, enterprise). For enterprise, it equals the real SDK request host across 9 injected environments. | **R2-8** An async route request can outlive close or a newer selection | Fixed | **Tasks 7, 8, 10.** The draft store gains a session `requestEpoch`, bumped only by `discard()` and `endSettingsSession()`, plus per-route `routeEpochs`, bumped by each request and by Undo for the routes it moves. ## Review response (round 1)

Every Critical and Important finding is closed. One finding is narrowed with evidence (I1, model-only changes). Nothing is rejected outright.

| Finding | Status | How |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** Authenticated discovery without explicit action | Closed | Task 9. `OpenAICompatiblePanel` loses mount, blur and auto-adopt discovery. URL edits are a local draft committed through the planner. The only path to `personalInference.models` is a "List models" button that names the receiving host and the credential slot it sends (or "no key"). The self-hosted Test uses a new unauthenticated probe that sends no headers. `CodexConnection` no longer checks status or quota on mount in Settings; that is an explicit "Check ChatGPT status" button. Mounted tests assert zero discovery calls on mount, tab browsing, typing and blur, and exactly one on the button. A repo-wide guard in Task 18 fails if any component writes a route-affecting setting outside the planner. |
| **C2** Counted history deletion deletes more | Closed | Task 14. `storageOps.js` in main owns preview and deletion with identical predicates. History deletion counts every transcript row (completed, discarded, soft-deleted) and every audio file, because the existing clear deletes all audio, and the confirmation names both. Tests use mixed rows and unlinked audio, and assert deleted == previewed. |
| **I1** Remote switching outside staged flow | Closed (narrowed) | Tasks 7–9. All four mode selectors, both pickers' commit paths, the custom base-URL field (no more automatic provider recognition), every self-hosted URL field, the editors' enable switches (cleanup, assistant, translation, screen context, vision model), the provider web-search toggle and the Corti region all go through the planner (`requestRouteChange` / `requestRoutePatch`). Turning a switch off is instant; turning one on stages when the route would send off the device. The policy-reconcile write is removed; invalid selections are preserved and shown as non-ready. On-device effective results (including loopback endpoints) are instant. New off-device recipients are staged. **Narrowing:** a model-only change at the same provider and host, with no growth in payload, applies instantly with a named toast and Undo. Evidence: spec §4 and SET-R3 B constrain moving work toward remote and silent provider switches, and such a change adds no recipient and no payload. It still runs through the planner, so the effective-recipient check is applied, not assumed. |
| **I2** Route facts start Codex network activity | Closed | Tasks 2–3. Codex presence is `fs.stat` of `<userData>/codex/auth.json` in main (no read, no process, no network). The facts loader never calls `codexStatus`, discovery or verification. A test fails if any of those are invoked. Facts publish independently. |
| **I3** Key readiness is optimistic renderer state | Closed | Task 2. Secret setters are acknowledged saves: the raw value never enters zustand, and the store holds only the `"__stored__"`/`""` sentinel set after main's ack. Main broadcasts `credentials-changed` after persistence. `flushSecretSaves()` is awaited by Apply and Verify. `ApiKeyInput` clears its draft after a save and shows a failed save. Readiness reads only main's `credentials.list`. |
| **I4** Undo-remove missing | Closed | Tasks 2 and 12. `credentials.remove` returns an opaque token, and the removed value lives only in main memory for 8 s. `undoRemove` is bound to the credential generation and expiry, and reset invalidates it. Tests confirm no IPC result contains secret material. |
| **I5** Preview, commit and Undo differ | Closed | Task 6. One simulated patch (with provider memory, explicit-model override, upload model, mode-validity clearing and vision flags) drives preview, commit and the exact raw Undo patch. The store's own provider-switch actions use the same extracted planners. |
| **I6** One-route draft changes other routes | Closed | Tasks 6 and 8. The planner resolves all 11 routes before and after. The Apply bar lists every changed route, marking coupled ones (meeting or upload inheriting dictation, vision following the assistant) with destination, host and payload. Undo restores inheritance blanks. |
| **I7** Patchbay destination identity | Closed | Tasks 1 and 10. Additive `ResolvedRoute.host`. Destinations use `route.providerId`, with one network destination per effective host. Tests cover a stale vision override, two LAN hosts and an inactive loopback URL. |
| **I8** Ready not constrained by executors | Closed | Task 1. Speech readiness runs the real `resolveTranscriptionRoute`. Meeting uses the streaming-provider table and rejects self-hosted. LLM endpoints use `isSecureHttpEndpoint` plus hosted-host rejection before any loopback decision. Unsupported configurations are `unreachable/unsupported`, not silently rewritten. |
| **I9** Failed inventory yields Ready | Closed | Tasks 1 and 3. Per-family facts are retained across errors, and the additive `RouteState` `{ status: "unknown" }` replaces optimistic ready (applied in spec §5.1, 091d198). |
| **I10** Corti identities | Closed | Tasks 1, 2, 8 and 11. `corti:text` (API key) and `corti:speech` (client id and secret) are separate identities for presence, health and rejection. The staged panel shows the speech credential fields. |
| **I11** Stale verification overwrites replacement | Closed | Task 11. Verify captures the credential generation and records only if it is unchanged. Concurrent Verify per identity is coalesced. Deferred-promise tests cover replacement, removal, out-of-order verifications and interrupted Verify all. |
| **I12** Storage/reset failures reported as success | Closed | Task 14. Main returns typed `{ ok, deleted, remaining, errors }`. Unreadable counts are errors, never zero. The dialog keeps the reviewed snapshot. Reset checks `success`, keeps errors visible and resets the credential authority. |

A conservative per-route payload-parts table built from request-builder evidence (selected text, history, notes and calendar look-ups, dictionary and snippet triggers, Corti meeting key terms, attendees, screenshot, web search), composed from the same snapshot inputs the request paths use. Agreement tests run against `resolveMeetingTranscriptionOptions`, `getDictionaryHintWords` and `isProviderSearchEnabled`, plus labelled source guards. |

## Contract change requests

**Status (spec commit 091d198).** Every request below is resolved in the consolidated spec. Where the spec's wording differs from what was asked, the spec governs and the plan follows it.

**§5.1, route graph (owned here).** **Applied in spec §5.1 (091d198).** Spec §5.1 now records the exact shape this plan codes against:
- `RouteState` includes `{ status: "unknown" }` and types `unreachable.detail` as the literal union `"sealed" | "retired" | "unsupported"`;
- `ResolvedRoute` includes `providerId` and `host`;
- `routeGraph.ts` is the pure resolver and `routes.ts` re-exports it;
- `buildRouteSnapshot` and `routeSnapshotFromSettings` are published. `routeSnapshotFromSettings` reads current facts, `sealedStore` and i18n, with no subscriptions and no IPC (Task 3). Plan 07 withdrew its request for it, but it stays published.

Consumer impact (also in §5.1 rule 1): Plans 04, 05 and 06 render `unknown` as a neutral "Checking…" state and never as ready, and Plan 05's Ready step waits for `ready`. `sends` is a composed list, so consumers that only display it are unaffected.

**Clarifications.** All are applied in spec §5.1 (091d198).

| # | Clarification | Status |
|---|---|---|

Plan 07 replaces the internals, adds `getSealedSnapshot()` and `subscribeSealed(cb)` to the same module, and migrates this store (not `routeFactsStore`) in its Task 13. - `readable` and `failed` are kept end to end;
- the unavailable state is kept;
- an unreadable zero is never shown as "cleared";

**§5.3, notices (owned by Plan 04).** Plan 03 merges before Plan 04 (spec §3), so it keeps the existing toast API and calls no `notify()`.

## Open questions for the owner

Each question has a default, and the plan implements that default unless the owner says otherwise.

1. **Codex and enterprise setup.** Codex, Bedrock, Azure and Vertex are set up inside the staged panel before Apply: Connect ChatGPT, or the endpoint, region, project, location, credentials and deployment. Nothing is committed and nothing is sent until Apply. Apply stays disabled until the route is Ready ("Sign in to X first", "Enter a valid server address", "Choose a model first"), as in SET-R3 B (`05-settings.html:867,878`). This replaces the round-1 default, which allowed Apply before credentials existed. Default: require readiness. The only question left for the owner is whether to keep an escape hatch, and the plan has none.
2. **History deletion also deletes all audio.** That is today's behaviour (`db-clear-transcriptions`), and the confirmation now says so and counts it. Should history deletion keep audio instead? Default: keep today's behaviour, disclosed.
3. **Transcript export.** There is no export IPC today. Default: ship without it.
4. **Curated model tiers.** The pips are size-derived estimates until `speedTier` and `qualityTier` are curated. Should they be curated before release?
5. **Main-process provider names.** Native reminder notifications use a small `PROVIDER_NAMES` map in main that mirrors `locality.ts`. Default: accept it.
6. **Incidental finding, out of scope.** `src/helpers/audioManager.js:3254` and `:3593` reference `usesKeywords`/`dictionary`, which are declared only inside `processWithOpenAIAPI` (`:2924-2925`). This is a possible ReferenceError on streaming dictation, not verified by running. Track it separately?
7. **Codex status in onboarding.** Settings no longer starts Codex on mount. `OnboardingFlow.tsx:546` keeps today's mount-time status check through an opt-in prop, so onboarding behaviour is unchanged. Default: Plan 05 decides whether onboarding keeps it.

## Global Constraints

- **Owner rules for this revision:**
  1. Authenticated discovery or verification never sends a stored credential without an explicit user action whose label names the host and the credential slot.
  2. Every history or audio deletion deletes exactly what its confirmation counts.
  3. Provider, model and endpoint changes never bypass the planner. New off-device recipients or payloads are staged.
  4. Route-fact loading makes no automatic network calls.
  5. Key readiness comes only from persistence that main has confirmed.
- Electron main owns SQLite, credentials, native runtimes, provider requests and updates. Renderers talk only through typed preload IPC (CLAUDE.md). No IPC result in this plan contains secret material, and the renderer never stores a raw secret.
- Local and remote choices stay explicit. Nothing silently switches provider or moves work off the device. Content is preserved on every failure. No provider or model change happens as a side effect. Invalid persisted selections are preserved and shown as non-ready.
- Unknown providers resolve to `remote` (fail toward disclosure). Use Plan 01's `resolveLocality`/`isLoopbackUrl`, and do not re-implement them.
- Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 and non-text UI at least 3:1, in light and Plum Night, measured on the real composited surfaces. Locality is always shape or glyph plus words.
- Motion uses the shared `--motion-*` tokens only, with no literal durations. Every loop is gated to its active state. Reduced motion keeps opacity and colour feedback and drops transforms.
- Orange means live voice (D1). In Settings, the default `Button` (the ink capsule) is the primary action. Orange appears only as the focus ring, the selected-card border and the active-nav marker.
- Every visible string goes through i18n in all 11 locales (`ar de en es fr it ja pt ru zh-CN zh-TW`), with the CLDR plural categories `npm run i18n:check` enforces. Provider and model names are not translated, and payload descriptions are.
- Use logical properties for RTL. Arrow-key navigation in grids flips Left and Right in RTL.
- **Tests:**
  - Use `node:test` through `npm test`. Run `npm run native:node` once, and `npm run native:electron` before launching the app. Never use personal profiles.
  - Load pure modules directly. Load store-importing renderer modules through `createRendererServer`. Mock `react-i18next` only through `withI18nMock` (`test/lib/i18nTestMock.js`, Task 3).
  - Mounted behaviour tests use the repo's probe pattern (`test/components/personalWorkspace.test.js:18-41`): call the component inside a probe that returns null, and invoke handler props under `React.act`.
  - Each test is labelled **change-driving** or **baseline guard**.
- `src/tsconfig.json` is not strict: narrow unions with explicit comparisons (`x.ok === false`).
- Before every commit, run `npx prettier --write` on the touched files and `npm run lint`. Before the PR, run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run i18n:check` and `npm run format:check`.
- `DESIGN.md` is the source of truth (D10). It is updated in Task 18.
- Node: `~/.nvm/versions/node/v24.21.0/bin`.

**i18n workflow used by every task.** Task 3 adds `scripts/merge-locale-keys.js`. For each task:
1. Write `/tmp/loqui-i18n-task-N.json` shaped `{ "en": {…}, "ar": {…}, …, "zh-TW": {…} }`, using the task's `en` block verbatim and real translations for the others.
2. Run `node scripts/merge-locale-keys.js /tmp/loqui-i18n-task-N.json && npm run i18n:check`.

## Review Focus

1. **A stored key reaching a host the user did not choose.** Opening a provider tab, typing or blurring an endpoint, or browsing OpenRouter must make zero authenticated requests. Only "List models" and "Verify" send a key, and only to the host they name. Pinned in Task 9 (mounted zero-call tests) and Task 11 (Verify).
2. **A confirmation that undercounts.** History with discarded and soft-deleted rows plus unlinked audio must delete exactly the counted totals, and a failed recount is an error, not success. Pinned in Task 14.
3. **A remote move without Apply.** Picker commits, endpoint fields, Undo of a local move and inherited (coupled) routes must all stage. Only on-device or same-recipient, same-payload results apply instantly. Pinned in Tasks 6, 7 and 9.
4. **Cold start, IPC failure or a key save in flight.** Routes must read "Checking…", not Ready. Apply and Verify must wait for pending saves. Pinned in Tasks 1, 2 and 3.
5. **A key replaced while Verify is running.** The old verdict must not land on the new key. Pinned in Task 11.

### Task 1: Route graph core: pure resolver with executor validation (§5.1)

Closes **I8** (a route is `ready` only when the real executor would run it), **I9** resolver side (per-family `unknown`, never `ready` from unknown facts), **I10** (credential identity `corti:text` vs `corti:speech`; rejection keyed by identity), **I7** (new `host` field), **I15** resolver side (`routePayloadParts` and composed `sends`, agreement test 1) and **M5** (a Node-loadable pure module plus a reusable complete fixture). Round 2 adds the graph half of **R2-1**: a non-secret `enterprise` snapshot slice and main-confirmed credential field presence, plus a main fact (`enterpriseMain`: main's environment overrides as hosts and booleans, from the new main-side `src/helpers/enterpriseRouteFacts.js`). From them every Bedrock, Azure and Vertex route derives its effective `host` and its readiness exactly as `src/helpers/enterpriseAiProviders.js` and the AI SDK packages it calls would, pinned by an agreement test against the real helper and SDK under injected environment overrides. Until Task 3 has synced the slice from main, every enterprise route is `unknown`. This is the data half of SET-R1/SET-R3 (the route state machine) and fixes SET-04 ("Active" means selected, not usable). The §5.1 hooks, `buildRouteSnapshot`, `routeSnapshotFromSettings`, the translated `RouteCopy` and `src/lib/routes.ts` are Task 3; nothing here reads the store, i18n or IPC.

What changes from v1 (old Task 1), and why:
- The resolver moves to `src/lib/routeGraph.ts` with exactly three imports, so tests and Plan 07 `import()` it directly under `node --import tsx` (M5). v1's `routes.ts` imported the store and the registry and needed Vite.
- Speech readiness comes from `resolveTranscriptionRoute` itself, with the meeting and text-endpoint rules mirrored from their executors (I8). v1 called any non-empty custom URL `ready` and decided loopback before validating.
- Facts are per model family and per credential identity; a family or credential map that main has not confirmed resolves to `{ status: "unknown" }` (I9, I10). v1's "unknown facts never downgrade a route" test asserted `ready`; it is replaced by the opposite assertion.
- Every route carries `host` (I7) and `sends` is composed from `PayloadPart`s (I15) instead of one fixed string per route.
- Round 2/3 (R2-1/R3-1/R3-3): enterprise routes no longer read `capabilities.providerHosts` or count as `ready` on credential presence alone. Azure requires a usable endpoint; Bedrock requires a complete static pair or supported profile; Vertex host selection follows the once-migrated `vertexAuthSource`, never secret presence. Missing `apiKey` source is `needsKey` without ADC fallback; ADC ignores stored and ambient API keys and requires a project.

  Snapshot conventions Task 3's builder must follow: `facts.installed.<family>` holds raw model ids (`"base"`, `"parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3"`, `"qwen3.5-2b-q4_k_m"`), `null` when that family's list call has never succeeded; `facts.credentials` holds only main-confirmed presence keyed by `CredentialId`, `null` until `credentials.list` first resolves; `facts.rejected` is keyed by `CredentialId`; `models` keys are `"whisper:<id>"`, `"sherpa:<id>"`, `"llm:<id>"` and `"cloud:<providerId>:<modelId>"`; `capabilities.providerHosts` values are bare `host[:port]`, keyed by raw provider id, plus one extra key `"corti:text"` for the Corti text host (`providerHosts.corti` is the Corti speech host for the selected region). A missing key gives `host: null`; the resolver never falls back from `"corti:text"` to `corti`. Enterprise providers have no `providerHosts` entry: their host comes only from `snapshot.enterprise` through `enterpriseRequestHost`. `snapshot.enterprise` holds the authoritative values (`bedrockRegion`, `azureEndpoint`, `vertexProject`, `vertexLocation`, `vertexAuthSource`); main's one-time source migration and getter sync complete before the renderer is admitted. `facts.credentialFields` holds main's per-field presence for each `CredentialId` (Vertex: `{ key }`, Bedrock: `{ accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken }`), loaded and nulled together with `facts.credentials`. `facts.enterpriseMain` is `null` until Task 3's loader has reconciled the enterprise settings from main and main answered `enterprise-route-facts`; while it is `null`, every enterprise route is `unknown`.

  Enterprise resolution (any mode whose provider is `bedrock`, `azure` or `vertex`, so the provider-only vision override is covered too): locality `remote`, `providerId` the enterprise id. `facts.enterpriseMain` `null` → `unknown`, `host: null`, before anything else. Otherwise the host comes from `enterpriseRequestHost` using committed route settings and main's environment facts; credential presence never changes it. An invalid endpoint or region/location yields `needsUrl`. If the needed credential facts have not loaded, apiKey-mode Vertex and profile-less Bedrock are `unknown` while retaining their already-known host. Bedrock is ready only with a supported profile or a complete committed static pair (`accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey`); a partial pair is `needsKey`, even when the authority's historical presence marker would have been true. Profile authentication takes precedence exactly as the executor does. Vertex's host is selected only by persisted `vertexAuthSource`: `apiKey` uses the express host and is `ready` only with a committed stored key or the supported `GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY` fallback, unless that credential is rejected; `adc` ignores both API-key sources and uses the configured location host, requiring a nonblank project. A missing API key in `apiKey` mode is `needsKey` and never falls back to ADC. Saving/removing/undoing a key changes readiness only. Then the usual `needsModel` for an empty model (an empty Azure deployment name).

  Resolution order per route: destination (locality, providerId, host, model, state) → `off` if the route's enable flag is off → `unreachable "sealed"` if `snapshot.sealed` and the locality is not `device` → otherwise the destination state. `sends` is `copy.list(parts.map((p) => copy.parts[p]))` unless the route is off or on the device. `provider` is `providerDisplayName(providerId)` or `null`; a configured endpoint keeps its host even when locality is `device`; built-in engines return `host: null`.

```js
function isPlainObject(value) {
  return (
    value !== null && typeof value === "object" && Object.getPrototypeOf(value) === Object.prototype
  );
}

// Plain objects merge key by key; anything else (Set, Map, array, function,
// null, primitive) replaces the default outright.
function deepMerge(base, overrides) {
  if (!isPlainObject(base) || !isPlainObject(overrides)) return overrides;
  const out = { ...base };
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(overrides)) {
    if (value === undefined) continue;
    out[key] =
      isPlainObject(value) && isPlainObject(base[key]) ? deepMerge(base[key], value) : value;
  }
  return out;
}

/**
 * A complete RouteSettingsSnapshot: every route local and installed, every
 * enable flag on except the vision override, every fact known, no credential
 * present, not sealed. Overrides deep-merge (plain objects only).
 * @param {object} [overrides]
 */
function makeSnapshot(overrides = {}) {
  return deepMerge(baseSnapshot(), overrides);
}

/**
 * A complete ResolvedRoute (default: the all-local dictation route).
 * `kind` and `settingsPath` follow `overrides.id` unless given explicitly.
 * @param {object} [overrides]
 */
function makeRoute(overrides = {}) {
  const id = overrides.id ?? "dictationStt";
  return {
    id,
    kind: KIND[id],
    locality: "device",
    provider: null,
    providerId: null,
    host: null,
    model: "Base",
    state: { status: "ready" },
    sends: null,
    settingsPath: SETTINGS_PATH[id],
    ...overrides,
  };
}

module.exports = { makeSnapshot, makeRoute };
```

```js
test("Corti speech and text authenticate with different credentials, and rejection is keyed by identity", async () => {
  const { routeCredentialId } = await load();
  assert.equal(routeCredentialId("dictationStt", "corti"), "corti:speech");
  assert.equal(routeCredentialId("noteRecordingStt", "corti"), "corti:speech");
  assert.equal(routeCredentialId("chat", "corti"), "corti:text");
  assert.equal(routeCredentialId("chat", "custom"), null);
  assert.equal(routeCredentialId("dictationStt", "openai"), "openai");
  const corti = {
    stt: {
      dictation: { mode: "providers", cloudProvider: "corti", cloudModel: "corti-transcribe" },
      meeting: { mode: "providers", cloudProvider: "corti" },
    },
    llm: { chatIntelligence: { mode: "providers", provider: "corti", model: "corti-chat" } },
  };
  const pairOnly = await routesOf({ ...corti, facts: { credentials: keys("corti:speech") } });
  assert.deepEqual(pairOnly.dictationStt.state, { status: "ready" });
  assert.deepEqual(pairOnly.noteRecordingStt.state, { status: "ready" });
  assert.deepEqual(pairOnly.chat.state, { status: "needsKey", provider: "Corti" });
  const keyOnly = await routesOf({ ...corti, facts: { credentials: keys("corti:text") } });
  assert.deepEqual(keyOnly.dictationStt.state, { status: "needsKey", provider: "Corti" });
  assert.deepEqual(keyOnly.chat.state, { status: "ready" });
  const mixed = await routesOf({
    ...corti,
    facts: { credentials: keys("corti:speech", "corti:text"), rejected: new Set(["corti:text"]) },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(
    mixed.dictationStt.state,
    { status: "ready" },
    "a rejected text key does not pause speech"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(mixed.chat.state, { status: "needsKey", provider: "Corti" });
  // Speech goes to the region's host; text always goes to the API-key host
  // (personalInference.js:78), read from providerHosts["corti:text"].
  assert.equal(keyOnly.dictationStt.host, "api.us.corti.app");
  assert.equal(keyOnly.noteRecordingStt.host, "api.us.corti.app");
  assert.equal(keyOnly.chat.host, "ai.eu.corti.app");
  const euSpeech = await routesOf({
    ...corti,
    facts: { credentials: keys("corti:speech", "corti:text") },
    capabilities: { providerHosts: { corti: "api.eu.corti.app" } },
  });
  assert.equal(euSpeech.dictationStt.host, "api.eu.corti.app", "the speech host follows the region");
  assert.equal(euSpeech.chat.host, "ai.eu.corti.app", "the text host does not");
  const { resolveRoute } = await load();
  const noTextHost = makeSnapshot({ ...corti, facts: { credentials: keys("corti:text") } });
  delete noTextHost.capabilities.providerHosts["corti:text"];
  assert.equal(resolveRoute(noTextHost, "chat").host, null, "never falls back to the speech host");
});

test("speech readiness agrees with the batch executor for custom endpoints", async () => {
  const { resolveTranscriptionRoute } = await import("../../src/helpers/transcriptionRoute.ts");
  const providers = makeSnapshot().capabilities.transcriptionProviderBaseUrls;
  const cases = [
    ["", "needsUrl"],
    ["not a url", "needsUrl"],
    ["http://stt.example.com/v1", "needsUrl"], // public HTTP
    ["https://api.openwhispr.com/v1", "needsUrl"], // retired hosted service
    ["https://inference.tinfoil.sh/v1", "needsUrl"], // Tinfoil only through the attested proxy
    ["https://api.openai.com/v1", "needsUrl"], // the untouched store default
    ["ws://localhost:9000/v1", "needsUrl"], // loopback, but not HTTP
    ["http://localhost:9000/v1", "ready"],
    ["https://stt.example.com/v1", "ready"],
  ];
  for (const [url, expected] of cases) {
    const input = {
      mode: "providers",
      cloudProvider: "custom",
      cloudModel: "whisper-1",
      cloudBaseUrl: url,
    };
    const executor = resolveTranscriptionRoute({
      settings: {
        transcriptionMode: "providers",
        cloudTranscriptionProvider: "custom",
        cloudTranscriptionModel: "whisper-1",
        cloudTranscriptionBaseUrl: url,
      },
      providers,
    });
    assert.equal(executor.transport === "error", expected !== "ready", `executor: ${url}`);
    const route = (await routesOf({ stt: { dictation: input } })).dictationStt;
    assert.equal(route.state.status, expected, url);
    if (expected === "needsUrl") {
      assert.equal(route.locality, "remote", `an invalid URL is never the device: ${url}`);
      assert.equal(route.host, null, url);
    }
  }
  const loopback = (
    await routesOf({
      stt: {
        dictation: {
          mode: "providers",
          cloudProvider: "custom",
          cloudBaseUrl: "http://localhost:9000/v1",
        },
      },
    })
  ).dictationStt;
  assert.equal(loopback.locality, "device");
  assert.equal(loopback.providerId, null);
  const hosted = (
    await routesOf({
      stt: {
        upload: {
          mode: "providers",
          cloudProvider: "custom",
          cloudBaseUrl: "https://stt.example.com/v1",
        },
      },
    })
  ).uploadStt;
  assert.equal(hosted.providerId, "custom");
  assert.equal(hosted.provider, "Custom endpoint");
  assert.equal(hosted.host, "stt.example.com");
});

  // is unreachable/unsupported (Plan 05 CCR 5).
  const groq = await routesOf({
    stt: { meeting: { mode: "providers", cloudProvider: "groq" } },
    facts: { credentials: keys("groq") },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(
    groq.noteRecordingStt.state,
    { status: "unreachable", detail: "unsupported" },
    "inherited Groq dictation cannot record notes"
  );
  assert.equal(groq.noteRecordingStt.providerId, "groq");
  const selfHosted = await routesOf({
    stt: { meeting: { mode: "self-hosted", remoteUrl: "http://192.168.1.20:9000/v1" } },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(selfHosted.noteRecordingStt.state, {
    status: "unreachable",
    detail: "unsupported",
  });
  assert.equal(selfHosted.noteRecordingStt.locality, "network");
  const openai = await routesOf({
    stt: { meeting: { mode: "providers", cloudProvider: "openai" } },
    facts: { credentials: keys("openai") },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(openai.noteRecordingStt.state, { status: "ready" });
  assert.equal(openai.noteRecordingStt.sends, "meeting audio from your microphone and the call");
});

test("text endpoints use the executor's rule before the loopback decision", async () => {
  const custom = async (cloudBaseUrl) =>
    (
      await routesOf({
        llm: {
          dictationCleanup: { mode: "providers", provider: "custom", model: "m", cloudBaseUrl },
        },
      })
    ).dictationCleanup;
  const selfHosted = async (remoteUrl) =>
    (
      await routesOf({
        llm: { dictationTranslation: { mode: "self-hosted", remoteUrl, model: "llama3.1:8b" } },
      })
    ).translation;
  const invalid = [
    "",
    "not a url",
    "http://llm.example.com/v1", // public HTTP
    "https://api.openwhispr.com/v1", // retired hosted service
    "https://user:secret@llm.example.com/v1", // embedded credentials
    "ws://localhost:1234/v1", // loopback, but not HTTP
    "http://lmstudio.localhost/v1", // loopback name, but not a private host for plain HTTP
  ];
  for (const url of invalid) {
    const c = await custom(url);
    assert.deepEqual(c.state, { status: "needsUrl" }, `custom ${url}`);
    assert.equal(c.locality, "remote", `custom ${url}`);
    assert.equal(c.providerId, "custom", `custom ${url}`);
    assert.equal(c.host, null, `custom ${url}`);
    const sh = await selfHosted(url);
    assert.deepEqual(sh.state, { status: "needsUrl" }, `self-hosted ${url}`);
    assert.equal(sh.locality, "network", `self-hosted ${url}`);
  }
  for (const url of [
    "http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1",
    "http://localhost:1234/v1",
    "http://[::1]:1234/v1",
    "https://lmstudio.localhost/v1",
  ]) {
    const c = await custom(url);
    assert.equal(c.locality, "device", url);
    assert.equal(c.providerId, null, url);
    assert.equal(c.host, new URL(url).host, "preserve a configured loopback endpoint host");
    assert.equal(c.sends, null, url);
    assert.deepEqual(c.state, { status: "ready" }, url);
  }
  const builtin = (await routesOf({})).dictationStt;
  assert.equal(builtin.locality, "device");
  assert.equal(builtin.host, null, "only a built-in engine has device locality and no host");
  const remote = await custom("https://llm.example.com:8443/v1");
  assert.equal(remote.locality, "remote");
  assert.equal(remote.host, "llm.example.com:8443");
  assert.equal(remote.sends, "your transcript text");
  const lan = await selfHosted("http://192.168.1.20:11434/v1");
  assert.equal(lan.locality, "network");
  assert.equal(lan.host, "192.168.1.20:11434");
  assert.equal(lan.providerId, null);
  assert.deepEqual(lan.state, { status: "ready" });
});

test("plain-HTTP *.localhost is loopback but refused by the executors, so it needs a URL (§5.1 rule 10)", async () => {
  const { isLoopbackUrl } = await import("../../src/lib/locality.ts");
  const url = "http://lmstudio.localhost/v1";
  // §5 Locality row (Plan 07 CCR-5, pinned by Plan 07's test/fixtures/loopbackCases.json): *.localhost IS loopback.
  assert.equal(isLoopbackUrl(url), true, "*.localhost is loopback");
  // §5.1 rule 10: whether an endpoint is valid is the executors' question, and they refuse plain-HTTP
  // *.localhost. Loopback-but-refused therefore resolves needsUrl, never device and never ready.
  const custom = (
    await routesOf({
      llm: { dictationCleanup: { mode: "providers", provider: "custom", model: "m", cloudBaseUrl: url } },
    })
  ).dictationCleanup;
  assert.deepEqual(custom.state, { status: "needsUrl" });
  assert.notEqual(custom.locality, "device");
  const speech = (
    await routesOf({
      stt: { dictation: { mode: "providers", cloudProvider: "custom", cloudModel: "whisper-1", cloudBaseUrl: url } },
    })
  ).dictationStt;
  assert.deepEqual(speech.state, { status: "needsUrl" });
  assert.notEqual(speech.locality, "device");
  const selfHosted = (
    await routesOf({ llm: { dictationTranslation: { mode: "self-hosted", remoteUrl: url, model: "llama3.1:8b" } } })
  ).translation;
  assert.deepEqual(selfHosted.state, { status: "needsUrl" });
  assert.equal(selfHosted.locality, "network");
});

test("Azure: a saved key never makes a missing or refused endpoint ready, and the host is the endpoint's", async () => {
  const { providerDisplayName } = await import("../../src/lib/locality.ts");
  const azure = async (azureEndpoint, credentials = keys("azure")) =>
    (await routesOf(enterpriseChat("azure", "gpt-4o-deploy", { enterprise: { azureEndpoint }, facts: { credentials } })))
      .chat;
  // createAzureModel refuses each of these (enterpriseAiProviders.js:73-77).
  for (const url of [
    "",
    "   ",
    "not a url",
    "http://myres.openai.azure.com/openai",
    "https://user:secret@myres.openai.azure.com/openai",
  ]) {
    const route = await azure(url);
    assert.deepEqual(route.state, { status: "needsUrl" }, `a saved key does not make ${JSON.stringify(url)} ready`);
    assert.equal(route.host, null, url);
    assert.equal(route.locality, "remote", url);
    assert.equal(route.providerId, "azure", url);
  }
  const first = await azure("https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai");
  assert.deepEqual(first.state, { status: "ready" });
  assert.equal(first.host, "myres.openai.azure.com");
  assert.equal(first.sends, "your messages, recent conversation, and notes and calendar details it looks up");
  const moved = await azure("https://Proxy.Example.com:8443/openai/");
  assert.equal(moved.host, "proxy.example.com:8443", "an endpoint host change changes route.host");
  assert.notEqual(moved.host, first.host);
  assert.deepEqual((await azure("https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai", keys())).state, {
    status: "needsKey",
    provider: providerDisplayName("azure"),
  });
  assert.deepEqual((await azure("https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai", null)).state, { status: "unknown" });
  assert.deepEqual((await azure("", null)).state, { status: "needsUrl" }, "a missing endpoint is a settings fact");
  const noDeployment = (
    await routesOf(enterpriseChat("azure", "", {
      enterprise: { azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" },
      facts: { credentials: keys("azure") },
    }))
  ).chat;
  assert.deepEqual(noDeployment.state, { status: "needsModel" }, "an empty deployment name");
});

test("Bedrock: the host follows the region through the SDK's partition table", async () => {
  const fields = (accessKeyId, secretAccessKey) =>
    new Map([["bedrock", { accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken: false }]]);
  const noOverrides = {
    bedrockEndpoint: { set: false, host: null },
    bedrockProfile: false,
    vertexApiKeyEnv: false,
    vertexProjectEnv: false,
  };
  const bedrock = async (bedrockRegion, options = {}) =>
    (
      await routesOf(
        enterpriseChat("bedrock", "us.anthropic.claude-fable-5", {
          enterprise: { bedrockRegion },
          facts: {
            credentials: options.credentials ?? keys("bedrock"),
            credentialFields: options.credentialFields ?? fields(true, true),
            enterpriseMain: { ...noOverrides, ...options.enterpriseMain },
          },
        })
      )
    ).chat;
  for (const [region, host] of [
    ["us-east-1", "bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com"],
    ["eu-west-1", "bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com"],
    ["cn-north-1", "bedrock-runtime.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com.cn"],
    ["", "bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com"], // enterpriseAiProviders.js:26 default
  ]) {
    const route = await bedrock(region);
    assert.equal(route.host, host, region);
    assert.deepEqual(route.state, { status: "ready" }, region);
  }
  const unusable = await bedrock("us east");
  assert.deepEqual(unusable.state, { status: "needsUrl" }, "no request URL can be built");
  assert.equal(unusable.host, null);
  const noCredentials = await bedrock("eu-west-1", { credentials: keys(), credentialFields: fields(false, false) });
  assert.equal(noCredentials.state.status, "needsKey");
  assert.equal(noCredentials.host, "bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com", "the destination is known before sign-in");
  for (const partial of [fields(true, false), fields(false, true)]) {
    const incomplete = await bedrock("eu-west-1", { credentialFields: partial });
    assert.equal(incomplete.state.status, "needsKey", "neither half of static credentials can enable Apply");
    assert.equal(incomplete.host, "bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com");
  }
  const profile = await bedrock("eu-west-1", {
    credentials: keys(),
    credentialFields: fields(false, false),
    enterpriseMain: { bedrockProfile: true },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(profile.state, { status: "ready" }, "a supported profile is an independent source");
  // The provider-only vision override reaches Bedrock in "providers" mode; same host rule.
  const vision = (
    await routesOf({
      enabled: { visionOverride: true },
      enterprise: { bedrockRegion: "ap-southeast-2" },
      facts: { credentials: keys("bedrock") },
      llm: { dictationAgentVision: { mode: "providers", provider: "bedrock", model: "apac.anthropic.claude-fable-5" } },
    })
  ).assistantVision;
  assert.equal(vision.host, "bedrock-runtime.ap-southeast-2.amazonaws.com");
});

test("Bedrock graph readiness matches the real SDK factory for static pairs and profile auth", async (t) => {
  const { getEnterpriseAIModel } = require("../../src/helpers/enterpriseAiProviders.js");
  const helperPath = require.resolve("../../src/helpers/enterpriseAiProviders.js");
  const originalLoad = Module._load;
  const profileCalls = [];
  Module._load = function loadBedrockProfile(request, parent, isMain) {
    if (request === "@aws-sdk/credential-providers" && parent?.filename === helperPath) {
      return {
        fromNodeProviderChain: ({ profile }) => async () => {
          profileCalls.push(profile);
          return { accessKeyId: "AKIAFIXTURE", secretAccessKey: "fixture-profile-secret" };
        },
      };
    }
    return originalLoad.call(this, request, parent, isMain);
  };
  t.after(() => { Module._load = originalLoad; });

  const bedrock = (fields) => getEnterpriseAIModel("bedrock", "fixture-model", "", {
    bedrockRegion: "us-east-1",
    ...fields,
  });
  await assert.rejects(
    bedrock({ bedrockAccessKeyId: "AKIAFIXTURE", bedrockSecretAccessKey: "" }),
    { name: "CredentialsProviderError" },
    "access-key-ID-only is refused by the executor"
  );
  await assert.rejects(
    bedrock({ bedrockAccessKeyId: "", bedrockSecretAccessKey: "fixture-secret" }),
    { name: "CredentialsProviderError" },
    "secret-only is refused by the executor"
  );
  assert.ok(await bedrock({ bedrockAccessKeyId: "AKIAFIXTURE", bedrockSecretAccessKey: "fixture-secret" }));
  assert.ok(await bedrock({ bedrockProfile: "fixture-profile", bedrockAccessKeyId: "partial" }));
  assert.deepEqual(profileCalls, ["fixture-profile"], "supported profile authentication wins over a partial static pair");
});

test("Vertex: the persisted auth source selects the host independently of saved or ambient key presence", async () => {
  const { providerDisplayName } = await import("../../src/lib/locality.ts");
  const fields = (key) => new Map([["vertex", { key }]]);
  const vertex = async (enterprise, facts) =>
    (await routesOf(enterpriseChat("vertex", "gemini-2.5-flash", { enterprise, facts }))).chat;
  const adc = {
    credentials: keys(),
    credentialFields: fields(false),
    enterpriseMain: { bedrockEndpoint: { set: false, host: null }, bedrockProfile: false, vertexApiKeyEnv: false, vertexProjectEnv: false },
  };
  for (const [vertexLocation, host] of [
    ["europe-west4", "europe-west4-aiplatform.googleapis.com"],
    ["", "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com"], // enterpriseAiProviders.js:92 default
    ["global", "aiplatform.googleapis.com"],
    ["eu", "aiplatform.eu.rep.googleapis.com"],
  ]) {
    const route = await vertex({ vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation, vertexAuthSource: "adc" }, adc);
    assert.equal(route.host, host, vertexLocation);
    assert.deepEqual(route.state, { status: "ready" }, vertexLocation);
  }
  const adcIgnoresKeys = await vertex(
    { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "adc" },
    {
      credentials: keys("vertex"),
      credentialFields: fields(true),
      enterpriseMain: { ...adc.enterpriseMain, vertexApiKeyEnv: true },
    }
  );
  assert.equal(adcIgnoresKeys.host, "europe-west4-aiplatform.googleapis.com");
  assert.deepEqual(adcIgnoresKeys.state, { status: "ready" }, "ADC ignores stored and legacy environment keys");
  const adcMissingProject = await vertex(
    { vertexProject: "  ", vertexLocation: "us-central1", vertexAuthSource: "adc" },
    {
      credentials: keys("vertex"),
      credentialFields: fields(true),
      enterpriseMain: { ...adc.enterpriseMain, vertexApiKeyEnv: true },
    }
  );
  assert.equal(adcMissingProject.host, "us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com");
  assert.deepEqual(adcMissingProject.state, {
    status: "needsKey",
    provider: providerDisplayName("vertex"),
  });
  const express = await vertex(
    { vertexProject: "", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" },
    { credentials: keys("vertex"), credentialFields: fields(true), enterpriseMain: adc.enterpriseMain }
  );
  assert.equal(express.host, "aiplatform.googleapis.com", "the API key ignores project and location");
  assert.deepEqual(express.state, { status: "ready" });
  const envFallback = await vertex(
    { vertexProject: "", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" },
    { credentials: keys(), credentialFields: fields(false), enterpriseMain: { ...adc.enterpriseMain, vertexApiKeyEnv: true } }
  );
  assert.equal(envFallback.host, "aiplatform.googleapis.com");
  assert.deepEqual(envFallback.state, { status: "ready" }, "the supported legacy key fallback is used only by apiKey mode");
  const noKey = await vertex(
    { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" },
    { credentials: keys(), credentialFields: fields(false), enterpriseMain: adc.enterpriseMain }
  );
  assert.equal(noKey.host, "aiplatform.googleapis.com");
  assert.deepEqual(noKey.state, { status: "needsKey", provider: providerDisplayName("vertex") }, "apiKey never falls back to ADC");
  const badLocation = await vertex(
    { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "bad location", vertexAuthSource: "adc" },
    adc
  );
  assert.deepEqual(badLocation.state, { status: "needsUrl" });
  assert.equal(badLocation.host, null);
  const unknownApiKey = await vertex(
    { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" },
    { credentials: null, credentialFields: null, enterpriseMain: adc.enterpriseMain }
  );
  assert.deepEqual(unknownApiKey.state, { status: "unknown" });
  assert.equal(unknownApiKey.host, "aiplatform.googleapis.com", "auth source determines the host before key listing");
});

test("main facts: environment overrides move enterprise hosts, and an unsynced slice is unknown", async () => {
  const unsynced = await routesOf({
    ...enterpriseChat("azure", "gpt-4o-deploy", {

  for (const provider of ["bedrock", "vertex"]) {
    const r = await routesOf(
      enterpriseChat(provider, "m", { facts: { credentials: keys(provider), enterpriseMain: null } })
    );
    assert.deepEqual(r.chat.state, { status: "unknown" }, provider);
    assert.equal(r.chat.host, null, provider);

  const main = (over) => ({

              "bedrock",
              { accessKeyId: true, secretAccessKey: true },

          },
        })
      )
    ).chat;
  const proxied = await bedrock(main({ bedrockEndpoint: { set: true, host: "bedrock-proxy.corp.example:8443" } }));
  assert.equal(proxied.host, "bedrock-proxy.corp.example:8443", "the override host, not the region's");

  const unusable = await bedrock(main({ bedrockEndpoint: { set: true, host: null } }));
  assert.deepEqual(unusable.state, { status: "needsUrl" });
  assert.equal(unusable.host, null);
  const vertexEnvKey = (
    await routesOf(
      enterpriseChat("vertex", "gemini-2.5-flash", {

        facts: { credentials: keys(), enterpriseMain: main({ vertexApiKeyEnv: true }) },
      })
    )
  ).chat;
  assert.equal(vertexEnvKey.host, "aiplatform.googleapis.com", "express mode through main's environment key");
  assert.deepEqual(vertexEnvKey.state, { status: "ready" }, "runs without a stored key or project");
  const envProjectOnly = (
    await routesOf(
      enterpriseChat("vertex", "gemini-2.5-flash", {
        enterprise: { vertexProject: "", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "adc" },
        facts: { credentials: keys("vertex"), enterpriseMain: main({ vertexProjectEnv: true }) },
      })
    )
  ).chat;
  assert.equal(envProjectOnly.state.status, "needsKey", "the helper passes the blank project, never GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT");
  const adcEnvKey = (
    await routesOf(
      enterpriseChat("vertex", "gemini-2.5-flash", {
        enterprise: { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "adc" },
        facts: { credentials: keys(), credentialFields: new Map(), enterpriseMain: main({ vertexApiKeyEnv: true }) },
      })
    )
  ).chat;
  assert.equal(adcEnvKey.host, "europe-west4-aiplatform.googleapis.com");
  assert.deepEqual(adcEnvKey.state, { status: "ready" }, "legacy env fallback cannot override the persisted ADC source");
});

test("agreement: enterprise hosts and refusals match enterpriseAiProviders.js and the request the AI SDK sends, with main's environment overrides", async (t) => {
  const { enterpriseRequestHost } = await load();
  const { getEnterpriseAIModel } = require("../../src/helpers/enterpriseAiProviders.js");
  // The real main-side reader Task 3 registers as the enterprise-route-facts IPC.
  const { enterpriseRouteFacts } = require("../../src/helpers/enterpriseRouteFacts.js");
  const ENV = [
    "AWS_ENDPOINT_URL",
    "AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME",
    "AWS_REGION",
    "AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK",
    "GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY",
    "GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT",
    "GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION",
  ];
  const savedEnv = new Map(ENV.map((name) => [name, process.env[name]]));
  const originalFetch = global.fetch;
  t.after(() => {
    global.fetch = originalFetch;
    for (const [name, value] of savedEnv) {
      if (value === undefined) delete process.env[name];
      else process.env[name] = value;
    }
  });
  const prompt = [{ role: "user", content: [{ type: "text", text: "Hello" }] }];
  // Fixture AWS keys only let Bedrock sign locally; the stubbed fetch answers every request.
  const AWS = { bedrockAccessKeyId: "AKIAFIXTURE", bedrockSecretAccessKey: "fixture-secret" };

  // The host the real executor's request goes to; null when it refuses the
  // configuration or no request can be made (the stub constructs a Request
  // first, so it refuses relative and credential-bearing URLs like fetch does).
  async function executorHost(provider, enterprise, apiKey) {
    let model;
    try {
      model = await getEnterpriseAIModel(provider, "fixture-model", apiKey, { ...AWS, ...enterprise });
    } catch {
      return null; // refused before any request (enterpriseAiProviders.js:73-77)
    }
    if (provider === "vertex" && enterprise.vertexAuthSource === "adc") {
      // ADC would first ask Google for a token (a real network call), so read the
      // base URL the SDK will call instead (@ai-sdk/google-vertex loadBaseURL).
      // The source implementation must pass apiKey: "" so ambient env cannot
      // silently switch this request to Express mode.
      assert.equal(typeof model.config?.baseURL, "string", "re-read @ai-sdk/google-vertex loadBaseURL");
      try {
        return new URL(model.config.baseURL).host;
      } catch {
        return null;
      }
    }
    let requested = null;
    global.fetch = async (url) => {
      new Request(String(url));
      requested = String(url);
      return new Response('{"error":{"message":"stub"}}', {
        status: 400,
        headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
      });
    };
    try {
      await model.doGenerate({ prompt });
    } catch {
      // The stub fails every request; an unusable URL fails before or inside fetch.
    } finally {
      global.fetch = originalFetch;
    }
    if (requested === null) return null;
    try {
      return new URL(requested).host;
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }

  // Injected environments only; never the developer's own.
  const scenarios = [
    {},
    { AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME: "https://bedrock-proxy.corp.example:8443/" },
    { AWS_ENDPOINT_URL: "https://aws-gateway.corp.example" },
    { AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME: "https://runtime.corp.example", AWS_ENDPOINT_URL: "https://ignored.corp.example" },
    { AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME: "" }, // set, so it wins, and no request URL can be built
    { AWS_ENDPOINT_URL: "https://user:pw@aws-gateway.corp.example" }, // fetch refuses credentials
    { GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY: "fixture-env-key" },
    { GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY: "" },
    { GOOGLE_VERTEX_PROJECT: "env-project", GOOGLE_VERTEX_LOCATION: "asia-east1", AWS_REGION: "ap-south-1" }, // never used
  ];
  const base = makeSnapshot().enterprise;
  const cases = [
    ["azure", { azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" }, "fixture-key"],
    ["azure", { azureEndpoint: "https://Proxy.Example.com:8443/x/" }, "fixture-key"],
    ["azure", { azureEndpoint: "" }, "fixture-key"],
    ["azure", { azureEndpoint: "not a url" }, "fixture-key"],
    ["azure", { azureEndpoint: "http://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" }, "fixture-key"],
    ["azure", { azureEndpoint: "https://u:p@myres.openai.azure.com/openai" }, "fixture-key"],
    ["bedrock", { bedrockRegion: "us-east-1" }, ""],
    ["bedrock", { bedrockRegion: "eu-central-1" }, ""],
    ["bedrock", { bedrockRegion: "cn-northwest-1" }, ""],
    ["bedrock", { bedrockRegion: "us-isob-east-1" }, ""],
    ["bedrock", { bedrockRegion: "" }, ""],
    ["bedrock", { bedrockRegion: "us east" }, ""],
    ["bedrock", { bedrockRegion: "evil.example/x" }, ""], // the SDK really contacts bedrock-runtime.evil.example
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "adc" }, ""],
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "", vertexAuthSource: "adc" }, ""],
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "global", vertexAuthSource: "adc" }, ""],
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "us", vertexAuthSource: "adc" }, ""],
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "bad location", vertexAuthSource: "adc" }, ""],
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "adc" }, ""],
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" }, "fixture-key"],
    ["vertex", { vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" }, ""], // committed stored key absent: uses injected legacy fallback or refuses
  ];
  for (const scenario of scenarios) {
    for (const name of ENV) delete process.env[name];
    Object.assign(process.env, scenario);
    const main = enterpriseRouteFacts(process.env);
    assert.equal(
      JSON.stringify(main).includes("fixture-env-key") || JSON.stringify(main).includes("user:pw"),
      false,
      "main's facts carry no value"
    );
    for (const [provider, overrides, apiKey] of cases) {
      const enterprise = { ...base, ...overrides };
      const graphHost = enterpriseRequestHost(provider, enterprise, main);
      const sdkHost = await executorHost(provider, enterprise, apiKey);
      const missingVertexKey =
        provider === "vertex" &&
        enterprise.vertexAuthSource === "apiKey" &&
        !(apiKey || process.env.GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY);
      if (missingVertexKey) {
        assert.equal(sdkHost, null, "the selected apiKey mode refuses without either committed key source");
        assert.equal(graphHost, "aiplatform.googleapis.com", "the configured recipient remains known while readiness is needsKey");
      } else {
        assert.equal(
          graphHost,
          sdkHost,
          `${JSON.stringify(scenario)} ${provider} ${JSON.stringify(overrides)}`
        );
      }
    }
  }
  for (const name of ENV) delete process.env[name];
  // Without its key Azure and Vertex apiKey mode are refused; neither may silently select ADC.
  assert.equal(
    await executorHost("azure", { ...base, azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" }, ""),
    null
  );
  for (const name of ENV) delete process.env[name];
  assert.equal(
    await executorHost("vertex", { ...base, vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" }, ""),
    null,
    "missing apiKey-mode credential is refused, not redirected to ADC"
  );
});

test("assistant vision follows the assistant unless overridden, and is off without screen context", async () => {

    dictationAgent: OPENAI_CHAT,

  };

    status: "off",
  });
  assert.deepEqual((await routesOf({ enabled: { voiceAssistant: false } })).assistantVision.state, {
    status: "off",
  });
});

test("sealed mode makes every route that leaves the device unreachable, LAN included", async () => {
  const { isSealedLocality } = await load();
  const r = await routesOf({
    sealed: true,
    enabled: { translation: false },
    facts: { credentials: null },
    stt: { dictation: OPENAI_STT },
    llm: {
      noteFormatting: {
        mode: "self-hosted",
        remoteUrl: "http://192.168.1.20:11434/v1",
        model: "llama3.1:8b",
      },
      dictationTranslation: OPENAI_CHAT,
    },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(
    r.dictationStt.state,
    { status: "unreachable", detail: "sealed" },
    "sealed wins over unknown"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(
    r.noteFormatting.state,
    { status: "unreachable", detail: "sealed" },
    "a LAN server is another machine"
  );
  assert.equal(r.noteFormatting.locality, "network");
  assert.deepEqual(r.chat.state, { status: "ready" });
  assert.deepEqual(r.translation.state, { status: "off" });
  assert.equal(isSealedLocality("remote"), true);
  assert.equal(isSealedLocality("network"), true);
  assert.equal(isSealedLocality("device"), false);
});

test("payload parts follow Appendix B per route and condition", async () => {
  const { routePayloadParts } = await load();
  const s = makeSnapshot({
    dictionaryInUse: true,
    llm: { dictationAgent: { providerSearch: true }, chatIntelligence: { providerSearch: true } },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("dictationStt", s), ["audio", "dictionary"]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("noteRecordingStt", s), ["meetingAudio"]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("uploadStt", s), ["audioFile"]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("dictationCleanup", s), ["transcript", "dictionary"]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("translation", s), ["transcript", "dictionary"]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("voiceAssistant", s), [
    "request",
    "selectedText",
    "history",
    "lookups",
    "dictionary",
    "screenshot",
    "webSearch",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("assistantVision", s), [
    "request",
    "selectedText",
    "history",
    "lookups",
    "dictionary",
    "screenshot",
    "webSearch",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("noteFormatting", s), [
    "noteText",
    "meetingTranscript",
    "participants",
    "dictionaryWords",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("chat", s), [
    "messages",
    "history",
    "lookups",
    "dictionary",
    "webSearch",
  ]);
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("speakerId", s), []);
  const override = makeSnapshot({
    enabled: { visionOverride: true },
    llm: { dictationAgent: { providerSearch: true } },
  });
  assert.deepEqual(
    routePayloadParts("voiceAssistant", override),
    ["request", "selectedText", "history", "lookups", "webSearch"],
    "the screenshot goes to the vision provider"
  );
  assert.deepEqual(
    routePayloadParts("assistantVision", override),
    ["request", "selectedText", "history", "lookups", "screenshot"],
    "search follows the vision scope"
  );
  const noScreen = makeSnapshot({ enabled: { screenContext: false } });
  assert.deepEqual(routePayloadParts("voiceAssistant", noScreen), [
    "request",
    "selectedText",
    "history",
    "lookups",
  ]);
  const remoteChat = (
    await routesOf({
      dictionaryInUse: true,
      llm: { chatIntelligence: { ...OPENAI_CHAT, providerSearch: true } },
      facts: { credentials: keys("openai") },
    })
  ).chat;
  assert.equal(
    remoteChat.sends,
    "your messages, recent conversation, notes and calendar details it looks up, your dictionary words and snippet triggers, and permission for the provider to search the web"
  );
});

});
```

```ts
// The route graph (spec §5.1): which task runs where, and can it run right now?
// One pure resolver answers for Settings, the pill, onboarding and Plan 07.
//
// Node-loadable on purpose (tests and Plan 07 import it directly under
// `node --import tsx`): erasable TypeScript only, explicit import extensions,
// and no imports beyond these three modules. No React, no store, no registry
// JSON: everything the resolver needs arrives in the snapshot.
//
// "Ready" means the real executor would run the request. Speech routes ask the
// batch executor itself (resolveTranscriptionRoute); note recording mirrors
// resolveMeetingTranscriptionOptions; text endpoints use the main process's
// endpoint rule (personalInference.js validateRequest). Unknown facts resolve to
// "unknown", never "ready".
import { isLoopbackUrl, providerDisplayName, type Locality } from "./locality.ts";
import { resolveTranscriptionRoute } from "../helpers/transcriptionRoute.ts";
import { isSecureHttpEndpoint } from "../utils/urlUtils.ts";

export type RouteId =
  | "dictationStt"
  | "noteRecordingStt"
  | "uploadStt"
  | "dictationCleanup"
  | "voiceAssistant"
  | "assistantVision"
  | "translation"
  | "noteFormatting"
  | "chat"
  | "speakerId"
  | "semanticSearch";

export type RouteKind = "speech" | "text" | "support";

export type RouteState =
  | { status: "ready" }
  | { status: "off" }
  | { status: "unknown" }
  | { status: "needsModel"; sizeBytes?: number }
  | { status: "needsKey"; provider: string }
  | { status: "needsUrl" }
  | { status: "unreachable"; detail?: "sealed" | "retired" | "unsupported" }; // spec §5.1: literal union, not string

export interface ResolvedRoute {
  id: RouteId;
  kind: RouteKind;
  locality: Locality;
  provider: string | null; // English providerDisplayName, logs only; UI uses providerDisplayLabel(providerId, t)
  providerId: string | null; // raw id ("openai", "custom"); null for device and network
  host: string | null; // effective endpoint host:port; configured loopback keeps its host; null for built-in engines or unknown/invalid hosts
  model: string | null;
  state: RouteState;
  sends: string | null; // translated payload list; null when device or off
  settingsPath: string;
}

export type SttContext = "dictation" | "meeting" | "upload";
export type LlmRouteScope =
  | "dictationCleanup"
  | "dictationAgent"
  | "dictationAgentVision"
  | "dictationTranslation"
  | "noteFormatting"
  | "chatIntelligence";
export type CredentialId =
  | "openai"
  | "anthropic"
  | "gemini"
  | "groq"
  | "xai"
  | "mistral"
  | "openrouter"
  | "tinfoil"
  | "deepgram"
  | "assemblyai"
  | "corti:text"
  | "corti:speech"
  | "codex"
  | "bedrock"
  | "azure"
  | "vertex";

export interface SttRouteInput {
  mode: string;
  localProvider: string;
  localModel: string;
  cloudProvider: string;
  cloudModel: string;
  cloudBaseUrl: string;
  remoteUrl: string;
  remoteModel: string;
}

export interface LlmRouteInput {
  mode: string;
  provider: string;
  model: string;
  remoteUrl: string;
  cloudBaseUrl: string;
  providerSearch: boolean;
}

export interface ModelInfo {
  name: string;
  sizeBytes?: number;
}

export interface RouteFacts {
  // Raw model ids per family; null = this family's inventory is not known.
  installed: {
    whisper: ReadonlySet<string> | null;
    sherpa: ReadonlySet<string> | null;
    llm: ReadonlySet<string> | null;
  };
  credentials: ReadonlyMap<CredentialId, boolean> | null; // main-confirmed presence; null = not loaded
  // Main-confirmed presence per credential field (Task 2's list rows' `fields`),
  // loaded and nulled together with `credentials`. Vertex's `key` decides its host.
  credentialFields: ReadonlyMap<CredentialId, Readonly<Record<string, boolean>>> | null;
  // Main's own environment overrides for the enterprise SDKs (Task 3's
  // enterprise-route-facts). null until Task 3 has also reconciled the four
  // enterprise settings to main's values: until then every enterprise route is unknown.
  enterpriseMain: EnterpriseMainFacts | null;
  rejected: ReadonlySet<CredentialId>;
  speakerIdModelsReady: boolean | null;
  searchModelReady: boolean | null;
}

export interface RouteCapabilities {
  meetingProviders: readonly string[];
  transcriptionProviderBaseUrls: readonly { id: string; baseUrl: string }[];
  // Raw provider id → bare host[:port]. "corti" is the Corti speech host for the
  // selected region; "corti:text" is the Corti text host (one fixed host).
  providerHosts: Readonly<Record<string, string>>;
}

export type PayloadPart =
  | "audio"
  | "audioFile"
  | "meetingAudio"
  | "dictionary"
  | "dictionaryWords"
  | "transcript"
  | "request"
  | "selectedText"
  | "history"
  | "lookups"
  | "noteText"
  | "meetingTranscript"
  | "participants"
  | "screenshot"
  | "webSearch"
  | "messages";

export const PAYLOAD_PARTS = [
  "audio",
  "audioFile",
  "meetingAudio",
  "dictionary",
  "dictionaryWords",
  "transcript",
  "request",
  "selectedText",
  "history",
  "lookups",
  "noteText",
  "meetingTranscript",
  "participants",
  "screenshot",
  "webSearch",
  "messages",
] as const satisfies readonly PayloadPart[];

export interface RouteCopy {
  parts: Readonly<Record<PayloadPart, string>>;
  list: (items: string[]) => string;
}

export type EnterpriseProviderId = "bedrock" | "azure" | "vertex";

// The non-secret enterprise settings that decide where an enterprise request
// goes. Raw store strings: main hands the same values, untrimmed, to
// enterpriseAiProviders.js (main.js:447-457).
export interface EnterpriseRouteSettings {
  bedrockRegion: string;
  azureEndpoint: string;
  vertexProject: string;
  vertexLocation: string;
  vertexAuthSource: "adc" | "apiKey";
}

// Hosts and booleans only; produced by src/helpers/enterpriseRouteFacts.js in main.
export interface EnterpriseMainFacts {
  // AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_BEDROCK_RUNTIME, else AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. host null = set but unusable.
  bedrockEndpoint: { set: boolean; host: string | null };
  bedrockProfile: boolean; // non-empty BEDROCK_PROFILE; profile value never leaves main
  vertexApiKeyEnv: boolean; // non-empty GOOGLE_VERTEX_API_KEY, only a fallback in apiKey mode
  vertexProjectEnv: boolean; // reported only: the helper always passes a string project
}

export interface RouteSettingsSnapshot {
  stt: Record<SttContext, SttRouteInput>;
  llm: Record<LlmRouteScope, LlmRouteInput>;
  enterprise: EnterpriseRouteSettings;
  enabled: {
    cleanup: boolean;
    voiceAssistant: boolean;
    screenContext: boolean;
    visionOverride: boolean;
    translation: boolean;
    speakerId: boolean;
  };
  dictionaryInUse: boolean;
  facts: RouteFacts;
  // Keys: "whisper:<id>", "sherpa:<id>", "llm:<id>", "cloud:<providerId>:<modelId>".
  models: Readonly<Record<string, ModelInfo>>;
  capabilities: RouteCapabilities;
  sealed: boolean;
  copy: RouteCopy;
}

export const ROUTE_IDS = [
  "dictationStt",
  "noteRecordingStt",
  "uploadStt",
  "dictationCleanup",
  "voiceAssistant",
  "assistantVision",
  "translation",
  "noteFormatting",

  "semanticSearch",
] as const satisfies readonly RouteId[];

  dictationStt: "speech",
  noteRecordingStt: "speech",
  uploadStt: "speech",
  dictationCleanup: "text",
  voiceAssistant: "text",
  assistantVision: "text",
  translation: "text",

export const ROUTE_SETTINGS_PATH: Readonly<Record<RouteId, string>> = {
  dictationStt: "stt/dictation",
  noteRecordingStt: "stt/noteRecording",
  uploadStt: "stt/upload",
  dictationCleanup: "llms/dictationCleanup",

  dictation: "dictationStt",

export const SCOPE_ROUTE: Readonly<Record<LlmRouteScope, RouteId>> = {

  dictationAgent: "voiceAssistant",
  dictationAgentVision: "assistantVision",
  dictationTranslation: "translation",
```
