2. Create `scripts/merge-locale-keys.js`:

   ```js
   #!/usr/bin/env node
   // Deep-merges a per-locale fragment into every src/locales/<lang>/translation.json.
   // Usage: node scripts/merge-locale-keys.js <fragment.json> [localesRoot]
   // The fragment is { "en": {...}, "de": {...}, ... } and must cover every locale,
   // so a new key can never land in English only.
   const fs = require("node:fs");
   const path = require("node:path");

   const [fragmentPath, rootArg] = process.argv.slice(2);
   if (!fragmentPath) {
     console.error("Usage: node scripts/merge-locale-keys.js <fragment.json> [localesRoot]");
     process.exit(2);
   }
   const root = rootArg ?? path.join(__dirname, "..", "src", "locales");
   const fragment = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(fragmentPath, "utf8"));
   const langs = fs
     .readdirSync(root)
     .filter((d) => fs.existsSync(path.join(root, d, "translation.json")));
   const missing = langs.filter((lang) => !fragment[lang]);
   if (missing.length) {
     console.error(`Missing locales in fragment: ${missing.join(", ")}`);
     process.exit(1);
   }

   const isObject = (v) => v !== null && typeof v === "object" && !Array.isArray(v);
   function merge(target, source) {
     for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(source)) {
       target[key] = isObject(value) ? merge(isObject(target[key]) ? target[key] : {}, value) : value;
     }
     return target;
   }

   for (const lang of langs) {
     const file = path.join(root, lang, "translation.json");
     const json = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, "utf8"));
     fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(merge(json, fragment[lang]), null, 2) + "\n");
   }
   console.log(`Merged ${path.basename(fragmentPath)} into ${langs.length} locales.`);
   ```

4. Create `src/stores/sealedStore.ts`:

   ```ts
   import { create } from "zustand";

   // The one renderer authority for sealed mode (spec §5.4). Route hooks, the
   // imperative route snapshot, the Apply bar and the Keyring all read this
   // store and nothing else; no other renderer module calls privacy.getSealed or
   // privacy.onSealedChange (Task 18 guards it). Keep the internals small and
   // swappable: Plan 07 (its Task 13) replaces them (attestation, staleness,
   // fail-closed reads), adds getSealedSnapshot() and subscribeSealed(cb) to this
   // same module, and keeps useSealedStore/getSealed/ensureSealedSubscribed exactly.
   // `known` is false until main has answered. Route snapshots map unknown
   // (known: false) to sealed = false, because main enforces the seal either way.

   export const useSealedStore = create<{ sealed: boolean; known: boolean }>()(() => ({
     sealed: false,
     known: false,
   }));

   export function getSealed(): boolean {
     return useSealedStore.getState().sealed;
   }

   let subscribed = false;
   // Bumped by every seal event. The first fetch applies only if no event
   // arrived after it started, so a slow fetch can never undo a newer event.
   let eventVersion = 0;

   export function ensureSealedSubscribed(): void {
     if (subscribed || typeof window === "undefined") return;
     subscribed = true;
     const privacy = window.electronAPI?.privacy;
     if (!privacy?.getSealed && !privacy?.onSealedChange) {
       // This build has no sealed mode, so nothing can be sealed.
       useSealedStore.setState({ sealed: false, known: true });
       return;
     }
     privacy.onSealedChange?.((sealed) => {
       eventVersion += 1;
       useSealedStore.setState({ sealed: sealed === true, known: true });
     });
     const startedAt = eventVersion;
     Promise.resolve()
       .then(() => privacy.getSealed?.())
       .then(
         (sealed) => {
           if (typeof sealed !== "boolean" || eventVersion !== startedAt) return;
           useSealedStore.setState({ sealed, known: true });
         },
         () => {
           // Unknown stays unknown; the next event settles it.
         }
       );
   }
   ```

5. Create `src/stores/routeFactsStore.ts`:

   ```ts
   import { create } from "zustand";
   import type { CredentialId, EnterpriseMainFacts, EnterpriseRouteSettings, RouteFacts } from "../lib/routeGraph";
   import { enterpriseLocalWriteCount, reconcileEnterpriseSettingsFromMain } from "./settingsStore";

   // Facts the route resolver needs that the settings store does not hold.
   // Every call here is local to this machine: model inventories on disk, main's
   // credential presence (Codex = a file stat in main) and keyring health. Never
   // codexStatus, model discovery or key verification (spec rule: route-fact
   // loading makes no automatic network calls).
   //
   // Each fact is loaded and published on its own. A failed or malformed answer
   // keeps the previous value; a fact is null only until main first answers.
   // Per-key generations stop an older response from overwriting a newer one.

   export type RouteFactKey =
     | "whisper"
     | "sherpa"
     | "llm"
     | "speakerId"
     | "search"
     | "credentials"
     | "rejected"
     | "enterprise";

   export const ROUTE_FACT_KEYS: readonly RouteFactKey[] = [
     "whisper",
     "sherpa",
     "llm",
     "speakerId",
     "search",
     "credentials",
     "rejected",
     "enterprise",
   ];

   interface ModelListResult {
     success?: boolean;
     models?: { model: string; downloaded: boolean }[];
   }
   interface CredentialRow {
     id: CredentialId;
     present: boolean;
     generation: number;
     // Per-field presence, never values (Task 2). Vertex's `key` changes readiness only.
     fields?: Record<string, boolean>;
   }

   export interface RouteFactsApi {
     listWhisperModels?: () => Promise<ModelListResult>;
     listParakeetModels?: () => Promise<ModelListResult>;
     modelGetAll?: () => Promise<{ id: string; isDownloaded?: boolean }[]>;
     getDiarizationModelStatus?: () => Promise<{ modelsDownloaded?: boolean }>;
     getSearchModelStatus?: () => Promise<{ downloaded?: boolean }>;
     credentials?: {
       list?: () => Promise<CredentialRow[]>;
       onChanged?: (callback: (event: CredentialRow) => void) => (() => void) | void;
     };
     keyring?: {
       list?: () => Promise<{ id: CredentialId; status: string }[]>;
       onChanged?: (callback: () => void) => (() => void) | void;
     };
     // R2-1/R3-1: main's enterprise settings (including migrated Vertex source) and its
     // environment overrides (enterprise-route-facts). All local reads.
     getBedrockRegion?: () => Promise<string | null>;
     getAzureEndpoint?: () => Promise<string | null>;
     getVertexProject?: () => Promise<string | null>;
     getVertexLocation?: () => Promise<string | null>;
     getVertexAuthSource?: () => Promise<"adc" | "apiKey">;
     enterpriseRouteFacts?: () => Promise<EnterpriseMainFacts>;
   }

   export const EMPTY_ROUTE_FACTS: RouteFacts = {
     installed: { whisper: null, sherpa: null, llm: null },
     credentials: null,
     credentialFields: null,
     enterpriseMain: null,
     rejected: new Set<CredentialId>(),
     speakerIdModelsReady: null,
     searchModelReady: null,
   };

   export const useRouteFactsStore = create<{ facts: RouteFacts }>()(() => ({
     facts: EMPTY_ROUTE_FACTS,
   }));

   const requested: Partial<Record<RouteFactKey, number>> = {};
   const published: Partial<Record<RouteFactKey, number>> = {};

   async function track<T, V>(
     key: RouteFactKey,
     call: () => Promise<T> | undefined,
     read: (raw: T) => V | undefined,
     apply: (facts: RouteFacts, value: V) => RouteFacts
   ): Promise<void> {
     const generation = (requested[key] = (requested[key] ?? 0) + 1);
     let value: V | undefined;
     try {
       const pending = call();
       if (!pending) return; // this build has no such call; the fact stays as it is
       value = read(await pending);
     } catch {
       return; // transient failure: keep the last known value
     }
     if (value === undefined || generation <= (published[key] ?? 0)) return;
     published[key] = generation;
     useRouteFactsStore.setState((s) => ({ facts: apply(s.facts, value) }));
   }

   function downloadedIds(result: ModelListResult | undefined): Set<string> | undefined {
     if (!result || result.success === false || !Array.isArray(result.models)) return undefined;
     return new Set(result.models.filter((m) => m.downloaded).map((m) => m.model));
   }

   function withInstalled(
     facts: RouteFacts,
     family: "whisper" | "sherpa" | "llm",
     ids: ReadonlySet<string>
   ): RouteFacts {
     return { ...facts, installed: { ...facts.installed, [family]: ids } };
   }

   // Main's per-credential generation orders presence updates, so a list read
   // before a save can never undo the save's event.
   const credentialGenerations = new Map<CredentialId, number>();

   // Only booleans survive: a row can never smuggle a value into renderer state.
   function presentFields(fields: unknown): Record<string, boolean> {
     if (!fields || typeof fields !== "object") return {};
     return Object.fromEntries(
       Object.entries(fields as Record<string, unknown>).map(([name, present]) => [name, present === true])
     );
   }

   const sameFields = (a: Readonly<Record<string, boolean>> | undefined, b: Record<string, boolean>) =>
     a !== undefined && JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b);

   // Presence and field presence move together under one generation, so the
   // graph never sees a Vertex key field from a different moment than its presence.
   function mergeCredentials(facts: RouteFacts, rows: readonly CredentialRow[]): RouteFacts {
     const next = new Map(facts.credentials ?? []);
     const nextFields = new Map(facts.credentialFields ?? []);
     let changed = facts.credentials === null || facts.credentialFields === null;
     for (const row of rows) {
       if (!row || typeof row.id !== "string") continue;
       const generation = typeof row.generation === "number" ? row.generation : 0;
       if (generation < (credentialGenerations.get(row.id) ?? -1)) continue;
       credentialGenerations.set(row.id, generation);
       if (next.get(row.id) !== (row.present === true)) changed = true;
       next.set(row.id, row.present === true);
       const fields = presentFields(row.fields);
       if (!sameFields(nextFields.get(row.id), fields)) changed = true;
       nextFields.set(row.id, fields);
     }
     return changed ? { ...facts, credentials: next, credentialFields: nextFields } : facts;
   }

   // R2-1/R3-1: main is the source of truth for where an enterprise request goes.
   // Once per window, the settings store's five enterprise fields are
   // reconciled to main's values (main wins, unless a local write went to main
   // after the read began); every load then re-reads main's environment
   // overrides. facts.enterpriseMain publishes only after both, so until the
   // sync lands every enterprise route resolves unknown (Task 1).
   let enterpriseSynced = false;

   const asText = (value: unknown): string => (typeof value === "string" ? value : "");

   function enterpriseMainFacts(raw: unknown): EnterpriseMainFacts | undefined {
     const r = raw as Partial<EnterpriseMainFacts> | null | undefined;
     const endpoint = r?.bedrockEndpoint;
     if (
       !r ||
       !endpoint ||
       typeof endpoint.set !== "boolean" ||
       !(endpoint.host === null || typeof endpoint.host === "string") ||
       typeof r.bedrockProfile !== "boolean" ||
       typeof r.vertexApiKeyEnv !== "boolean" ||
       typeof r.vertexProjectEnv !== "boolean"
     ) {
       return undefined; // malformed: not a fact
     }
     return {
       bedrockEndpoint: { set: endpoint.set, host: endpoint.set ? endpoint.host : null },
       bedrockProfile: r.bedrockProfile,
       vertexApiKeyEnv: r.vertexApiKeyEnv,
       vertexProjectEnv: r.vertexProjectEnv,
     };
   }

   async function loadEnterpriseMain(api: RouteFactsApi): Promise<EnterpriseMainFacts | undefined> {
     const { getBedrockRegion, getAzureEndpoint, getVertexProject, getVertexLocation, getVertexAuthSource, enterpriseRouteFacts } = api;
     // A build that cannot confirm main's configuration stays unknown.
     if (!getBedrockRegion || !getAzureEndpoint || !getVertexProject || !getVertexLocation || !getVertexAuthSource || !enterpriseRouteFacts) {
       return undefined;
     }
     if (!enterpriseSynced) {
       const since = enterpriseLocalWriteCount();
       const [bedrockRegion, azureEndpoint, vertexProject, vertexLocation, vertexAuthSource] = await Promise.all([
         getBedrockRegion(),
         getAzureEndpoint(),
         getVertexProject(),
         getVertexLocation(),
         getVertexAuthSource(),
       ]);
       if (vertexAuthSource !== "adc" && vertexAuthSource !== "apiKey") return undefined;
       const main: EnterpriseRouteSettings = {
         bedrockRegion: asText(bedrockRegion),
         azureEndpoint: asText(azureEndpoint),
         vertexProject: asText(vertexProject),
         vertexLocation: asText(vertexLocation),
         vertexAuthSource,
       };
       reconcileEnterpriseSettingsFromMain(main, since);
       enterpriseSynced = true;
     }
     return enterpriseMainFacts(await enterpriseRouteFacts());
   }

   const LOADERS: Record<RouteFactKey, (api: RouteFactsApi) => Promise<void>> = {
     whisper: (api) =>
       track("whisper", () => api.listWhisperModels?.(), downloadedIds, (f, ids) =>
         withInstalled(f, "whisper", ids)
       ),
     sherpa: (api) =>
       track("sherpa", () => api.listParakeetModels?.(), downloadedIds, (f, ids) =>
         withInstalled(f, "sherpa", ids)
       ),
     llm: (api) =>
       track(
         "llm",
         () => api.modelGetAll?.(),
         (rows) =>
           Array.isArray(rows) ? new Set(rows.filter((m) => m.isDownloaded).map((m) => m.id)) : undefined,
         (f, ids) => withInstalled(f, "llm", ids)
       ),
     speakerId: (api) =>
       track(
         "speakerId",
         () => api.getDiarizationModelStatus?.(),
         (r) => (typeof r?.modelsDownloaded === "boolean" ? r.modelsDownloaded : undefined),
         (f, ready) => ({ ...f, speakerIdModelsReady: ready })
       ),
     search: (api) =>
       track(
         "search",
         () => api.getSearchModelStatus?.(),
         (r) => (typeof r?.downloaded === "boolean" ? r.downloaded : undefined),
         (f, ready) => ({ ...f, searchModelReady: ready })
       ),
     credentials: (api) =>
       track(
         "credentials",
         () => api.credentials?.list?.(),
         (rows) => (Array.isArray(rows) ? rows : undefined),
         mergeCredentials
       ),
     rejected: (api) =>
       track(
         "rejected",
         () => api.keyring?.list?.(),
         (rows) =>
           Array.isArray(rows)
             ? new Set(rows.filter((r) => r.status === "rejected").map((r) => r.id))
             : undefined,
         (f, rejected) => ({ ...f, rejected })
       ),
     enterprise: (api) =>
       track(
         "enterprise",
         () => loadEnterpriseMain(api),
         (value) => value,
         (f, enterpriseMain) => ({ ...f, enterpriseMain })
       ),
   };

   export async function loadRouteFacts(
     api: RouteFactsApi | undefined,
     keys: readonly RouteFactKey[] = ROUTE_FACT_KEYS
   ): Promise<void> {
     if (!api) return;
     await Promise.all(keys.map((key) => LOADERS[key](api)));
   }

   const currentApi = (): RouteFactsApi | undefined =>
     typeof window === "undefined" ? undefined : (window.electronAPI as unknown as RouteFactsApi);

   export function refreshRouteFacts(keys: readonly RouteFactKey[] = ROUTE_FACT_KEYS): Promise<void> {
     return loadRouteFacts(currentApi(), keys);
   }

   function applyCredentialChange(event: CredentialRow): void {
     if (useRouteFactsStore.getState().facts.credentials === null) {
       // Main has not listed presence yet: read the full list rather than
       // assume anything about the credentials this event does not name.
       void refreshRouteFacts(["credentials"]);
     } else {
       useRouteFactsStore.setState((s) => ({ facts: mergeCredentials(s.facts, [event]) }));
     }
     // Main resets a key's health on save and remove; re-read the verdict.
     void refreshRouteFacts(["rejected"]);
   }

   // Facts change on focus, after model downloads or deletes anywhere
   // (LOCAL_MODELS_CHANGED_EVENT, src/hooks/useModelDownload.ts:21; the cache
   // clear, src/components/SettingsPage.tsx:1478), and when main reports a
   // credential or keyring change.
   const REFRESH_EVENTS = ["focus", "openwhispr-models-cleared", "openwhispr-local-models-changed"];

   let subscribed = false;
   export function ensureRouteFactsSubscribed(): void {
     if (subscribed || typeof window === "undefined") return;
     subscribed = true;
     const api = currentApi();
     void refreshRouteFacts();
     api?.credentials?.onChanged?.(applyCredentialChange);
     api?.keyring?.onChanged?.(() => void refreshRouteFacts(["rejected"]));
     for (const event of REFRESH_EVENTS) {
       window.addEventListener(event, () => void refreshRouteFacts());
     }
   }
   ```

   This file imports only types from `routeGraph`, so it adds no runtime import cycle with `routes.ts`. Its one runtime import, `settingsStore` (R2-1 reconciliation), does not import this file, `routes.ts` or `routeGraph.ts` (`src/stores/settingsStore.ts:1-46`; Task 6 adds only `providerSwitchPlans` and `providerSearch`).

     ```ts
     // R2-1/R3-1: main's environment is what the enterprise executor reads
     // (main.js:447-457), so main wins over localStorage. A local write sends
     // the new value to main as well, so a write after the read began is newer
     // than that read and is kept.
     const ENTERPRISE_ROUTE_FIELDS = ["bedrockRegion", "azureEndpoint", "vertexProject", "vertexLocation", "vertexAuthSource"] as const;
     let enterpriseLocalWrites = 0;

     export function noteEnterpriseLocalWrite(): void {
       enterpriseLocalWrites += 1;
     }

     export function enterpriseLocalWriteCount(): number {
       return enterpriseLocalWrites;
     }

     export function reconcileEnterpriseSettingsFromMain(
       main: Record<"bedrockRegion" | "azureEndpoint" | "vertexProject" | "vertexLocation", string> & { vertexAuthSource: "adc" | "apiKey" },
       since: number
     ): boolean {
       if (enterpriseLocalWrites !== since) return false;
       const state = useSettingsStore.getState();
       const changed: Partial<SettingsState> = {};
       for (const key of ENTERPRISE_ROUTE_FIELDS) {
         if (state[key] === main[key]) continue;
         changed[key] = main[key];
         if (isBrowser) localStorage.setItem(key, main[key]);
       }
       // Renderer-only: nothing is written back to main.
       if (Object.keys(changed).length > 0) useSettingsStore.setState(changed);
       return true;
     }
     ```

     Main's `""` replaces the renderer's `"us-east-1"`/`"us-central1"` defaults when main has no value; the executor applies the same defaults (`enterpriseAiProviders.js:26,92`), so Task 1 resolves the same host.

7. Create `src/lib/routes.ts`:

   ```ts
   import { useEffect, useMemo, useSyncExternalStore } from "react";
   import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next";
   import i18n from "../i18n";
   import { API_ENDPOINTS } from "../config/constants";
   import { MEETING_STREAMING_PROVIDER_IDS } from "../helpers/meetingTranscriptionRouting";
   import {
     getCloudModel,
     getLocalModel,
     getParakeetModelInfo,
     getTranscriptionModels,
     getTranscriptionProviders,
     getWhisperModelInfo,
   } from "../models/ModelRegistry";
   import {
     selectResolvedLLMConfig,
     selectResolvedMeetingTranscription,
     selectResolvedUploadTranscription,
     useSettingsStore,
     type SettingsState,
   } from "../stores/settingsStore";
   import { ensureRouteFactsSubscribed, useRouteFactsStore } from "../stores/routeFactsStore";
   import { ensureSealedSubscribed, getSealed, useSealedStore } from "../stores/sealedStore";
   import { getDictionaryHintWords } from "../utils/snippets";
   import { isProviderSearchEnabled, PROVIDER_SEARCH_CHANGED_EVENT } from "../utils/providerSearch";
   import {
     localSttModelKey,
     resolveRoutes,
     type LlmRouteInput,
     type LlmRouteScope,
     type ModelInfo,
     type PayloadPart,
     type ResolvedRoute,
     type RouteCapabilities,
     type RouteCopy,
     type RouteFacts,
     type RouteId,
     type RouteSettingsSnapshot,
     type SttContext,
     type SttRouteInput,
   } from "./routeGraph.ts";

   // §5.1 contract module. The pure graph (types, resolver, payload composition)
   // lives in routeGraph.ts, which stays Node-loadable, and is re-exported
   // unchanged. This file adds what needs the renderer: the snapshot builder over
   // the settings store, translated route copy, the imperative snapshot and the
   // React hooks.
   export * from "./routeGraph.ts";

   const LLM_SCOPES: readonly LlmRouteScope[] = [
     "dictationCleanup",
     "dictationAgent",
     "dictationAgentVision",
     "dictationTranslation",
     "noteFormatting",
     "chatIntelligence",
   ];

   interface SttSource {
     transcriptionMode: string;
     localTranscriptionProvider: string;
     whisperModel: string;
     parakeetModel: string;
     cohereModel: string;
     cloudTranscriptionProvider: string;
     cloudTranscriptionModel: string;
     cloudTranscriptionBaseUrl?: string;
   }

   function sttInput(src: SttSource, remoteUrl: string, remoteModel: string): SttRouteInput {
     const localModel =
       src.localTranscriptionProvider === "whisper"
         ? src.whisperModel
         : src.localTranscriptionProvider === "cohere"
           ? src.cohereModel
           : src.parakeetModel;
     return {
       mode: src.transcriptionMode,
       localProvider: src.localTranscriptionProvider,
       localModel,
       cloudProvider: src.cloudTranscriptionProvider,
       cloudModel: src.cloudTranscriptionModel,
       cloudBaseUrl: src.cloudTranscriptionBaseUrl ?? "",
       remoteUrl,
       remoteModel,
     };
   }

   // Keys: localSttModelKey(provider, id) for local speech, "llm:<id>" for local
   // text, "cloud:<provider>:<id>" for cloud models (read by routeGraph.ts).
   function describeModels(
     stt: Record<SttContext, SttRouteInput>,
     llm: Record<LlmRouteScope, LlmRouteInput>
   ): Record<string, ModelInfo> {
     const models: Record<string, ModelInfo> = {};
     for (const input of Object.values(stt)) {
       if (input.localModel) {
         const key = localSttModelKey(input.localProvider, input.localModel);
         if (input.localProvider === "whisper") {
           const info = getWhisperModelInfo(input.localModel);
           if (info) models[key] = { name: info.name, sizeBytes: info.sizeMb * 1_000_000 };
         } else {
           const info = getParakeetModelInfo(input.localModel);
           if (info) models[key] = { name: info.name, sizeBytes: info.expectedSizeBytes ?? info.sizeMb * 1_000_000 };
         }
       }
       if (input.cloudProvider && input.cloudModel) {
         const info = getTranscriptionModels(input.cloudProvider).find((m) => m.id === input.cloudModel);
         if (info) models[`cloud:${input.cloudProvider}:${input.cloudModel}`] = { name: info.name };
       }
     }
     for (const input of Object.values(llm)) {
       if (!input.model) continue;
       const local = getLocalModel(input.model);
       if (local) models[`llm:${input.model}`] = { name: local.name, sizeBytes: local.sizeBytes };
       const cloud = input.provider ? getCloudModel(input.model, input.provider) : undefined;
       if (cloud) models[`cloud:${input.provider}:${input.model}`] = { name: cloud.name };
     }
     return models;
   }

   function hostOf(url: string): string | null {
     try {
       return new URL(url).host || null;
     } catch {
       return null;
     }
   }

   let capabilities: RouteCapabilities | null = null;

   // Static registry data, passed in so routeGraph.ts stays JSON-free.
   function routeCapabilities(): RouteCapabilities {
     if (capabilities) return capabilities;
     const transcriptionProviders = getTranscriptionProviders();
     const providerHosts: Record<string, string> = {};
     const add = (id: string, url: string) => {
       const host = hostOf(url);
       if (host) providerHosts[id] = host;
     };
     for (const provider of transcriptionProviders) add(provider.id, provider.baseUrl);
     add("openai", API_ENDPOINTS.OPENAI_BASE);
     add("anthropic", API_ENDPOINTS.ANTHROPIC);
     add("gemini", API_ENDPOINTS.GEMINI);
     add("groq", API_ENDPOINTS.GROQ_BASE);
     add("openrouter", API_ENDPOINTS.OPENROUTER_BASE);
     // Corti text uses the API key against one fixed host (constants.ts:123,
     // personalInference.js:78), unlike Corti speech, whose host follows the
     // region (capabilitiesFor below). Task 1 reads this key for Corti text routes.
     add("corti:text", API_ENDPOINTS.CORTI_MODELS_BASE);
     // Codex requests go through the ChatGPT account it signs in to
     // (auth hosts checked at src/helpers/personalInference.js:258).
     add("codex", "https://chatgpt.com");
     // Bedrock, Azure and Vertex deliberately get no entry (R2-1): their host
     // follows settings (region, endpoint, project/location) and the Vertex key,
     // so Task 1 derives it from snapshot.enterprise + facts.credentialFields with
     // enterpriseRequestHost, never from this static table.
     capabilities = {
       meetingProviders: [...MEETING_STREAMING_PROVIDER_IDS],
       transcriptionProviderBaseUrls: transcriptionProviders.map(({ id, baseUrl }) => ({ id, baseUrl })),
       providerHosts,
     };
     return capabilities;
   }

   // Corti speech connects to api.<region>.corti.app (cortiTranscription.js:39,
   // cortiStreaming.js:48); the registry baseUrl names only the US host. An empty
   // region means US (transcriptionRoute.ts:305). Only a bare label becomes part
   // of a host name.
   function cortiHost(environment: string): string {
     const region = /^[a-z0-9-]+$/i.test(environment ?? "") ? environment.toLowerCase() : "us";
     return `api.${region}.corti.app`;
   }

   // The static capabilities plus the hosts that follow settings. A new object
   // only when the Corti host differs from the cached one.
   function capabilitiesFor(settings: SettingsState): RouteCapabilities {
     const statics = routeCapabilities();
     const corti = cortiHost(settings.cortiEnvironment);
     return statics.providerHosts.corti === corti
       ? statics
       : { ...statics, providerHosts: { ...statics.providerHosts, corti } };
   }

   export function buildRouteSnapshot(
     settings: SettingsState,
     facts: RouteFacts,
     copy: RouteCopy,
     sealed: boolean
   ): RouteSettingsSnapshot {
     const meeting = selectResolvedMeetingTranscription(settings);
     const upload = selectResolvedUploadTranscription(settings);
     const stt: Record<SttContext, SttRouteInput> = {
       dictation: sttInput(settings, settings.remoteTranscriptionUrl, settings.remoteTranscriptionModel),
       // Note recording has no self-hosted model field of its own.
       meeting: sttInput(meeting, meeting.remoteTranscriptionUrl, settings.remoteTranscriptionModel),
       // Upload has no self-hosted fields: UploadSettings.tsx binds SelfHostedPanel
       // to the dictation server URL.
       upload: sttInput(upload, settings.remoteTranscriptionUrl, settings.remoteTranscriptionModel),
     };

     const llm = {} as Record<LlmRouteScope, LlmRouteInput>;
     for (const scope of LLM_SCOPES) {
       const cfg = selectResolvedLLMConfig(settings, scope);
       llm[scope] = {
         mode: cfg.mode,
         provider: cfg.provider,
         model: cfg.model,
         remoteUrl: cfg.remoteUrl ?? "",
         cloudBaseUrl: cfg.cloudBaseUrl ?? "",
         // The same function the request path uses (useChatStreaming.ts:392).
         providerSearch: isProviderSearchEnabled(scope, cfg.provider, cfg.mode),
       };
     }

     return {
       stt,
       llm,
       // R2-1: the non-secret settings main hands enterpriseAiProviders.js
       // (main.js:447-457; the setters write both sides, settingsStore.ts:2033-2097).
       // Raw strings, untrimmed, because the executor uses them untrimmed. No
       // secret, profile or API version: none of them changes the host.
       enterprise: {
         bedrockRegion: settings.bedrockRegion ?? "",
         azureEndpoint: settings.azureEndpoint ?? "",
         vertexProject: settings.vertexProject ?? "",
         vertexLocation: settings.vertexLocation ?? "",
       },
       enabled: {
         cleanup: settings.useCleanupModel,
         voiceAssistant: settings.useDictationAgent,
         screenContext: settings.voiceAgentScreenContext,
         visionOverride: settings.useDictationAgentVisionModel,
         translation: settings.useDictationTranslation,
         speakerId: settings.speakerDiarizationEnabled,
       },
       // The same hint list the STT prompt, cleanup suffix and chat request use.
       dictionaryInUse: getDictionaryHintWords(settings).length > 0,
       facts,
       models: describeModels(stt, llm),
       capabilities: capabilitiesFor(settings),
       sealed,
       copy,
     };
   }

   function listFormat(language: string): Intl.ListFormat {
     try {
       return new Intl.ListFormat(language || "en", { style: "long", type: "conjunction" });
     } catch {
       return new Intl.ListFormat("en", { style: "long", type: "conjunction" });
     }
   }

   export function routeCopy(t: (key: string) => string, language: string): RouteCopy {
     const parts: Record<PayloadPart, string> = {
       audio: t("routes.payload.audio"),
       audioFile: t("routes.payload.audioFile"),
       meetingAudio: t("routes.payload.meetingAudio"),
       dictionary: t("routes.payload.dictionary"),
       dictionaryWords: t("routes.payload.dictionaryWords"),
       transcript: t("routes.payload.transcript"),
       request: t("routes.payload.request"),
       selectedText: t("routes.payload.selectedText"),
       history: t("routes.payload.history"),
       lookups: t("routes.payload.lookups"),
       noteText: t("routes.payload.noteText"),
       meetingTranscript: t("routes.payload.meetingTranscript"),
       participants: t("routes.payload.participants"),
       screenshot: t("routes.payload.screenshot"),
       webSearch: t("routes.payload.webSearch"),
       messages: t("routes.payload.messages"),
     };
     const format = listFormat(language);
     return { parts, list: (items) => format.format(items) };
   }

   export function currentRouteCopy(): RouteCopy {
     return routeCopy((key) => String(i18n.t(key)), i18n.language || "en");
   }

   // Non-React reader for click-time decisions (Apply, Undo, Keyring). Reads the
   // current facts, the sealed store and the app's i18n; subscribes to nothing
   // and calls no IPC. Unloaded facts stay unknown, which never reads as ready.
   export function routeSnapshotFromSettings(settings: SettingsState): RouteSettingsSnapshot {
     return buildRouteSnapshot(
       settings,
       useRouteFactsStore.getState().facts,
       currentRouteCopy(),
       getSealed()
     );
   }

   // --- React hooks (§5.1) ---

   // providerSearch lives in localStorage, outside every store; this version
   // re-runs the builder when a toggle changes here or in another window.
   let providerSearchVersion = 0;
   function subscribeProviderSearch(onChange: () => void): () => void {
     if (typeof window === "undefined") return () => {};
     const bump = () => {
       providerSearchVersion += 1;
       onChange();
     };
     window.addEventListener(PROVIDER_SEARCH_CHANGED_EVENT, bump);
     window.addEventListener("storage", bump);
     return () => {
       window.removeEventListener(PROVIDER_SEARCH_CHANGED_EVENT, bump);
       window.removeEventListener("storage", bump);
     };
   }
   const readProviderSearchVersion = () => providerSearchVersion;

   export function useRouteCopy(): RouteCopy {
     const { t, i18n: instance } = useTranslation();
     const language = instance?.language || "en";
     return useMemo(() => routeCopy(t, language), [t, language]);
   }

   export function useResolvedRoutes(): ResolvedRoute[] {
     const settings = useSettingsStore();
     const facts = useRouteFactsStore((s) => s.facts);
     const sealed = useSealedStore((s) => s.sealed);
     const copy = useRouteCopy();
     const searchVersion = useSyncExternalStore(
       subscribeProviderSearch,
       readProviderSearchVersion,
       readProviderSearchVersion
     );
     useEffect(() => {
       ensureRouteFactsSubscribed();
       ensureSealedSubscribed();
     }, []);
     return useMemo(
       () => resolveRoutes(buildRouteSnapshot(settings, facts, copy, sealed)),
       // searchVersion is not read here: it re-runs the builder, which reads localStorage.
       // eslint-disable-next-line react-hooks/exhaustive-deps
       [settings, facts, copy, sealed, searchVersion]
     );
   }

   export function useResolvedRoute(id: RouteId): ResolvedRoute {
     const routes = useResolvedRoutes();
     return routes.find((route) => route.id === id) as ResolvedRoute;
   }
   ```

   `useSettingsStore()` without a selector returns the state object, whose identity changes only when a setting changes, so the memo recomputes once per change and consumers get a stable array in between. If `npm run typecheck` reports that a registry field differs from the access above (`sizeMb`, `expectedSizeBytes`, `sizeBytes`), read `src/models/ModelRegistry.ts:7-127` and adapt only the field access.

### Task 4: Settings paths, in-modal navigation and the support-models tab (SET-Q17)

Closes I13 for the support-model rows (the "Downloaded" status uses the locality role, never `text-success`, which measures 3.30:1 on white) and the Review Focus item "nothing flashes Download before facts load". It also delivers SET-Q17 and the navigation plumbing every later task uses.

Every `ResolvedRoute.settingsPath` (`"stt/dictation"`, `"llms/supportModels"`, …) must open Settings at that exact place, both from outside the modal (`ControlPanel`'s `onOpenSettings(section?: string)` feeds `SettingsModal`'s `initialSection`, `src/components/ControlPanel.tsx:669`) and from inside it (Patchbay rows in Task 10, search results in Task 16). SET-Q17 moves speaker identification and semantic search out of Privacy & Data into a Language Models sub-tab, with their sizes. Once a support model is downloaded, the route facts are refreshed (Task 3), so the `speakerId` and `semanticSearch` chips leave "Download" without waiting for a focus event.

Scope notes:
- `parseSettingsPath` and the alias maps are the v1 design, moved out of `SettingsModal.tsx`. The `stt` section prefix is included here because every `ROUTE_SETTINGS_PATH` value for speech routes starts with it. The `routing` section id and its `routes` alias are added by Task 10, not here.
- Sub-tab ids for `speechToText` and `llms` become exported constants that `SettingsPage` derives its tab unions from, so a route path can never name a tab that does not exist (guarded by a test against the real `ROUTE_SETTINGS_PATH`).
- `ProviderTabs` still renders the `llms` sub-tabs. Its tablist/tab roles and arrow keys come from Plan 02 and are a hard preflight owned by Task 18; this task adds one more tab to it and does not touch its markup.

const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const test = require("node:test");
const React = require("react");
const { createRoot } = require("react-dom/client");
const {
  createRendererServer,
  installBrowserGlobals,
  installHookDom,
} = require("../lib/rendererTestHarness");
const { withI18nMock } = require("../lib/i18nTestMock");

function walk(node, visit) {
  if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.forEach((child) => walk(child, visit));
  if (!node || typeof node !== "object") return;
  visit(node);
  walk(node.props?.children, visit);
}
const findAll = (tree, predicate) => {
  const out = [];
  walk(tree, (node) => predicate(node) && out.push(node));
  return out;
};
const textOf = (tree) => {
  const parts = [];
  const collect = (node) => {
    if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.forEach(collect);
    if (typeof node === "string") return parts.push(node);
    if (node && typeof node === "object") collect(node.props?.children);
  };
  collect(tree);
  return parts.join("|");
};
const settle = () => React.act(async () => new Promise((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve)));

async function mount(t, api) {
  let root;
  t.after(async () => {
    if (root) await React.act(async () => root.unmount());
    delete globalThis.__routeFactsRefreshes;
  });
  globalThis.__routeFactsRefreshes = 0;
  installBrowserGlobals(t, { window: { electronAPI: api } });
  const container = installHookDom(t);
  const vite = await createRendererServer(
    t,
    withI18nMock(
      {
        cachePrefix: "loqui-support-models-test-",
        mockModules: {
          "/stores/routeFactsStore":
            "export function refreshRouteFacts() { globalThis.__routeFactsRefreshes += 1; return Promise.resolve(); }",
        },
      },
      { withOptions: true }
    )
  );
  const Component = (await vite.ssrLoadModule("/components/settings/LocalSupportModels.tsx")).default;
  let tree;
  function Probe() {
    tree = Component();
    return null;
  }
  root = createRoot(container);
  await React.act(async () => root.render(React.createElement(Probe)));
  const row = (kind) => findAll(tree, (n) => n.props?.label === `personal.supportModels.${kind}`)[0];
  const button = (kind) => findAll(row(kind), (n) => typeof n.props?.onClick === "function")[0];
  return { tree: () => tree, row, button };
}

});

test("support models", async (t) => {

   ```ts
   import type { SettingsSectionType } from "../components/SettingsPage";

   // Settings locations are "<section>" or "<section>/<subTab>". Route
   // settingsPaths (src/lib/routeGraph.ts) and every legacy deep link resolve
   // here, and anything unknown falls back to Preferences rather than a blank pane.

   export interface SettingsLocation {
     section: SettingsSectionType;
     subTab?: string;
   }

   export const SETTINGS_SECTIONS: readonly SettingsSectionType[] = [
     "general",
     "hotkeys",
     "speechToText",
     "llms",
     "privacyData",
     "system",
   ];

   // Sub-tab ids, in tab order. SettingsPage builds its tab unions from these so a
   // route path can never name a tab that does not exist.
   export const SPEECH_SUB_TABS = ["dictation", "noteRecording", "upload"] as const;
   export const LLM_SUB_TABS = [
     "dictationCleanup",
     "dictationAgent",
     "dictationTranslation",
     "noteFormatting",
     "chatIntelligence",
     "supportModels",
   ] as const;

   const SUB_TABS: Partial<Record<SettingsSectionType, readonly string[]>> = {
     speechToText: SPEECH_SUB_TABS,
     llms: LLM_SUB_TABS,
   };

   // The old AI Models sidebar had four items (transcription, meetings,
   // intelligence, agentMode) — they now collapse into two: speechToText + llms.
   // Legacy deep-links land on the matching sub-tab via LEGACY_SUB_TAB.
   // "dictationAgent" is a live deep-link (the Home GPU banner), not a legacy alias.
   // "stt" is the section prefix route paths use ("stt/dictation").
   export const SECTION_ALIASES: Record<string, SettingsSectionType> = {
     aiModels: "llms",
     agentConfig: "llms",
     agentMode: "llms",
     dictationAgent: "llms",
     intelligence: "llms",
     meetings: "llms",
     prompts: "llms",
     transcription: "speechToText",
     uploadTranscription: "speechToText",
     stt: "speechToText",
     softwareUpdates: "system",
     privacy: "privacyData",
     permissions: "privacyData",
     developer: "system",
   };

   export const LEGACY_SUB_TAB: Record<string, string> = {
     transcription: "dictation",
     uploadTranscription: "upload",
     dictationAgent: "dictationAgent",
     meetings: "noteFormatting",
     intelligence: "dictationCleanup",
     agentMode: "chatIntelligence",
     agentConfig: "chatIntelligence",
     aiModels: "dictationCleanup",
     prompts: "dictationCleanup",
   };

   export function parseSettingsPath(path: string | null | undefined): SettingsLocation {
     if (!path) return { section: "general" };
     const [head, sub] = path.split("/", 2);
     const section = (SETTINGS_SECTIONS as readonly string[]).includes(head)
       ? (head as SettingsSectionType)
       : SECTION_ALIASES[head];
     if (!section) return { section: "general" };
     const subTab = sub || LEGACY_SUB_TAB[head];
     const known = SUB_TABS[section];
     return subTab && (!known || known.includes(subTab)) ? { section, subTab } : { section };
   }
   ```

   Sections without a registered sub-tab list pass a sub-tab through unchanged, so later tasks that add sub-tabs elsewhere only register them in `SUB_TABS`.

4. Add `formatDecimalBytes` to `src/utils/formatBytes.ts`. Model hosts publish decimal sizes ("34.8 MB", "91 MB"), and the existing `formatBytes` is 1024-based:

   ```ts
   // Decimal (1000-based) units, matching the sizes model hosts publish.
   export function formatDecimalBytes(bytes: number, decimals = 1): string {
     if (!Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes <= 0) return "0 MB";
     const units = ["B", "KB", "MB", "GB", "TB"];
     const i = Math.min(units.length - 1, Math.floor(Math.log10(bytes) / 3));
     return `${parseFloat((bytes / 1000 ** i).toFixed(decimals))} ${units[i]}`;
   }
   ```

5. Replace the whole of `src/components/settings/LocalSupportModels.tsx`. The status reads and `download()` keep their behaviour; what changes is that readiness starts unknown (no Download flash), sizes and the device ring show, "Downloaded" uses the locality role, and a finished download refreshes route facts.

   ```tsx
   import { useEffect, useState } from "react";
   import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next";
   import modelRegistryData from "../../models/modelRegistryData.json";
   import { refreshRouteFacts } from "../../stores/routeFactsStore";
   import { formatDecimalBytes } from "../../utils/formatBytes";
   import { Button } from "../ui/button";
   import { LocalityRing } from "../ui/LocalityRing";
   import { SectionHeader, SettingsPanel, SettingsPanelRow, SettingsRow } from "../ui/SettingsSection";

   type ModelKind = "meeting" | "search";

   // Sizes shown before download. Diarization is the sum of the registry entries;
   // the embedding model (all-MiniLM-L6-v2 ONNX plus tokenizer) is fetched by
   // scripts/download-minilm.js and is about 91 MB.
   const SUPPORT_MODEL_BYTES: Record<ModelKind, number> = {
     meeting: Object.values(modelRegistryData.diarizationModels).reduce(
       (sum, model) => sum + model.sizeMb * 1_000_000,
       0
     ),
     search: 91_000_000,
   };

   export default function LocalSupportModels() {
     const { t } = useTranslation();
     // null = not read yet. Nothing says "Download" until main has answered.
     const [ready, setReady] = useState<Record<ModelKind, boolean | null>>({
       meeting: null,
       search: null,
     });
     const [checking, setChecking] = useState(true);
     const [busy, setBusy] = useState<ModelKind | null>(null);
     const [error, setError] = useState("");

     useEffect(() => {
       let mounted = true;
       const api = window.electronAPI;
       void Promise.all([api.getDiarizationModelStatus?.(), api.getSearchModelStatus?.()])
         .then(([meeting, search]) => {
           if (mounted)
             setReady({ meeting: !!meeting?.modelsDownloaded, search: !!search?.downloaded });
         })
         .catch((error) => {
           if (mounted) setError(String(error));
         })
         .finally(() => {
           if (mounted) setChecking(false);
         });
       return () => {
         mounted = false;
       };
     }, []);

     const download = async (kind: ModelKind) => {
       setBusy(kind);
       setError("");
       try {
         const result =
           kind === "meeting"
             ? await window.electronAPI.downloadDiarizationModels?.()
             : await window.electronAPI.downloadSearchModel?.();
         if (!result?.success) throw new Error(result?.error || t("personal.supportDownloadFailed"));
         setReady((previous) => ({ ...previous, [kind]: true }));
         // The route graph reads these two as route facts (speakerId, semanticSearch).
         void refreshRouteFacts();
       } catch (error) {
         setError(String(error));
       } finally {
         setBusy(null);
       }
     };

     return (
       <div className="space-y-3">
         <SectionHeader
           title={t("settingsPage.llms.supportModels.title")}
           description={t("settingsPage.llms.supportModels.description")}
         />
         <SettingsPanel>
           {(["meeting", "search"] as const).map((kind) => (
             <SettingsPanelRow key={kind}>
               <SettingsRow
                 label={t(`personal.supportModels.${kind}`)}
                 description={t(`personal.supportModels.${kind}Description`)}
               >
                 <div className="flex items-center gap-2">
                   <LocalityRing locality="device" label={t("locality.device")} size={18} />
                   {checking ? (
                     <span className="text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground">
                       {t("settingsPage.llms.supportModels.checking")}
                     </span>
                   ) : ready[kind] ? (
                     <span className="text-xs font-medium text-locality-device">
                       {t("settingsPage.llms.supportModels.downloaded")}
                     </span>
                   ) : (
                     <Button
                       size="sm"
                       variant="outline"
                       disabled={!!busy}
                       onClick={() => void download(kind)}
                     >
                       {busy === kind
                         ? t("personal.downloading")
                         : t("settingsPage.llms.supportModels.download", {
                             size: formatDecimalBytes(SUPPORT_MODEL_BYTES[kind]),
                           })}
                     </Button>
                   )}
                 </div>
               </SettingsRow>
             </SettingsPanelRow>
           ))}
         </SettingsPanel>
         {error && (
           <p role="alert" className="text-xs text-destructive">
             {error}
           </p>
         )}
       </div>
     );
   }
   ```

   Contrast (measured with Plan 01's `contrastRatio` over the shipped tokens): `text-locality-device` is 5.35:1 on the white panel and 4.91:1 on `muted`/`secondary`/`surface-3` in light, and above 9:1 in Plum Night. `text-success` is 3.30:1 on white and is not used. The `role="alert"` error text sits on the page background, outside the panel (4.83:1 light, 6.61:1 dark).

### Task 5: Route chips, an honest mode selector and contrast (SET-Q4)

Closes I13 for the mode selector, the chips and the cloud model list (contrast measured with opacity compositing over the real Settings surfaces, in both themes, and the light focus ring token), and M1 for the mode selector (focus and selection are exercised through handler props, not only SSR role counts). It also adds the `unknown` ("Checking…") chip state and the `retired` and `unsupported` details that the v2 route graph introduces.

"Active" means "mode selected", not "usable" (SET-04). This task does four things:
- It replaces "Active" with "Current" plus the route's real state chip, including the three new cases: `unknown` reads "Checking…", and `unreachable` has the details `sealed`, `retired` and `unsupported`.
- It makes the mode selector a real radio group: `role="radiogroup"`/`radio`, `aria-checked`, a roving tab stop, arrow keys that move focus (Enter and Space choose, because choosing a mode changes a route).
- It ships the two chip primitives every later screen uses.
- It fixes the contrast of everything it touches and pins the Settings surfaces with composited tests in both themes (Plum Night extension included).

Design decisions worth reviewing:
- **Arrows move focus; Enter or Space choose.** A radio group normally selects on arrow keys, but here a selection is a route change: instant with an Undo toast on device, a staged draft otherwise (Tasks 7 and 8). Arrowing through Cloud on the way to Local would stage and then replace drafts. The model cartridge grid (Task 13) follows the same rule.
- **Chip words never use `text-destructive`.** It is 4.43:1 on the muted, secondary and surface-3 fills (`#dc2626` on `#f5f5f5`). Chip text is foreground, muted-foreground or the device role; the destructive hue is carried by the glyph (a non-text mark, 3:1 minimum, measured 4.06:1 at worst).
- **The selected mark is the ring token, not solid `primary`.** Solid `#ff5a1f` is 2.94:1 on a hovered row. The ring token (`#E84E16` light) is 3.19:1 or better on every Settings surface, and orange stays within the D1 allowance (focus ring, selected-card border, active-nav marker).
- **Descriptions are full-strength `text-muted-foreground`.** At `/80` it is 4.46:1 on a hovered row in light.

  // src/components/settings/routing/RouteChips.tsx
  export function routeStateLabel(state: RouteState, t: TFunction | ((key: string, options?: object) => string)): string;
  export function RouteStateChip(props: { state: RouteState; className?: string }): JSX.Element;
  export function RouteDestinationChip(props: { route: Pick<ResolvedRoute, "locality" | "providerId" | "model">; className?: string }): JSX.Element;
  // src/components/ui/rovingNav.ts
  export type NavKey = "ArrowUp" | "ArrowDown" | "ArrowLeft" | "ArrowRight" | "Home" | "End";
  export function stepLinear(index: number, key: string, disabled: readonly boolean[], rtl?: boolean): number; // index unchanged for other keys
  // InferenceModeSelector gains props:
  //   label: string                    (radiogroup accessible name)
  //   routeState?: RouteState          (state of the applied mode's route; shown beside "Current")
  //   stagedMode?: InferenceMode|null  (Task 8; the staged mode is the checked radio and shows "Staged, not active")
  ```

  The two chip signatures are exactly the published components of spec §5.1 (Plan 08 CCR-6): no other props, required or optional. Plan 08 consumes them, and §5.1 requires every surface that discloses a route (Plans 04–08 included) to use these two chips rather than build its own. Changing either signature is a §5.1 contract change.

- i18n keys owned here: `routes.runsOn`, `routes.place.chooseProvider`, `routes.selection.{current,selected,staged}`, `routes.state.*`. Task 3 owns `routes.names.*`.

    assert.equal(chips.routeStateLabel({ status: "unreachable" }, tr), "routes.state.cantReach");

    assert.equal(chips.routeStateLabel({ status: "unreachable", detail: "something-new" }, tr), "routes.state.cantReach");

    assert.match(html, /routes\.state\.checking/);
    assert.doesNotMatch(html, /routes\.state\.ready/);

  await t.test("chip text never uses a low-contrast role (I13, change-driving)", () => {

```js
const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const test = require("node:test");
const React = require("react");
const { createRoot } = require("react-dom/client");
const { renderToStaticMarkup } = require("react-dom/server");
const {
  createRendererServer,
  installBrowserGlobals,
  installHookDom,
} = require("../lib/rendererTestHarness");
const { withI18nMock } = require("../lib/i18nTestMock");

// Mounted-behaviour pattern from personalWorkspace.test.js: the selector is called
// as a function inside a probe that returns null; handler props are invoked under
// React.act. In React 19 a host element's ref is a prop, so the test hands each
// radio a fake element whose focus() is recorded, which is what makes arrow-key
// focus observable without a DOM.
function walk(node, visit) {
  if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.forEach((child) => walk(child, visit));
  if (!node || typeof node !== "object") return;
  visit(node);
  walk(node.props?.children, visit);
}
const findAll = (tree, predicate) => {
  const out = [];
  walk(tree, (node) => predicate(node) && out.push(node));
  return out;
};
const textOf = (tree) => {
  const parts = [];
  const collect = (node) => {
    if (Array.isArray(node)) return node.forEach(collect);
    if (typeof node === "string") return parts.push(node);
    if (node && typeof node === "object") collect(node.props?.children);
  };
  collect(tree);
  return parts.join("|");
};

const modes = [
  { id: "providers", label: "Cloud", description: "Send audio to a provider", icon: null },
  { id: "local", label: "Local", description: "Stay on this device", icon: null },
  { id: "self-hosted", label: "Self-hosted", description: "Your server", icon: null, disabled: true, badge: "Soon" },
  { id: "enterprise", label: "Enterprise", description: "Your cloud account", icon: null },
];

async function mount(t, getProps) {
  let root;
  t.after(async () => {
    if (root) await React.act(async () => root.unmount());
  });
  installBrowserGlobals(t);
  const container = installHookDom(t);
  const vite = await createRendererServer(t, withI18nMock({ cachePrefix: "loqui-mode-selector-test-" }));
  const { InferenceModeSelector } = await vite.ssrLoadModule("/components/ui/SettingsSection.tsx");
  let tree;
  function Probe() {
    tree = InferenceModeSelector(getProps());
    return null;
  }
  root = createRoot(container);
  await React.act(async () => root.render(React.createElement(Probe)));
  const focused = [];
  const group = () => findAll(tree, (n) => n.props?.role === "radiogroup")[0];
  const radios = () => findAll(tree, (n) => n.props?.role === "radio");
  const attach = () =>
    radios().forEach((radio, i) =>
      radio.props.ref({ focus: () => focused.push(modes[i].id) })
    );
  attach();
  const press = async (index, key) => {
    let prevented = false;
    await React.act(async () => radios()[index].props.onKeyDown({ key, preventDefault: () => (prevented = true) }));
    attach();
    return prevented;
  };
  const tabStops = () => radios().map((r, i) => (r.props.tabIndex === 0 ? modes[i].id : null)).filter(Boolean);
  return { tree: () => tree, group, radios, press, focused, tabStops };
}

test("mode selector", async (t) => {
  await t.test("it is a radio group named for the task, with one tab stop on the checked radio (change-driving)", async (t) => {
    const h = await mount(t, () => ({ label: "Dictation runs on", modes, activeMode: "local", onSelect() {} }));
    assert.equal(h.group().props["aria-label"], "Dictation runs on");
    assert.equal(h.radios().length, 4);

    assert.deepEqual(h.tabStops(), ["local"]);

    assert.deepEqual(h.tabStops(), ["enterprise"], "the tab stop follows focus");
    await h.press(3, "ArrowDown");

    await h.press(0, "End");
    assert.equal(h.focused.at(-1), "enterprise");

  });

  await t.test("markup carries the radio semantics server-side too (change-driving)", async (t) => {
    installBrowserGlobals(t);
    const vite = await createRendererServer(t, withI18nMock({ cachePrefix: "loqui-mode-selector-ssr-" }));
    const { InferenceModeSelector } = await vite.ssrLoadModule("/components/ui/SettingsSection.tsx");
    const html = renderToStaticMarkup(
      React.createElement(InferenceModeSelector, { label: "Dictation runs on", modes, activeMode: "local", onSelect() {} })
    );
    assert.match(html, /role="radiogroup"[^>]*aria-label="Dictation runs on"/);
    assert.equal((html.match(/role="radio"/g) ?? []).length, 4);
    assert.equal((html.match(/tabindex="0"/g) ?? []).length, 1);
  });
});
```

All are **change-driving**: today the selector has no `role`, no `label` prop, no roving tab stop and no key handler, and it renders "Active". The `a click chooses…` subtest also pins that a disabled mode cannot be chosen.

Create `test/components/settingsContrast.test.js`. It uses Plan 01's real helpers (`src/utils/contrast.ts`, `test/helpers/harness/cssTokens.js`) and blends the translucent Settings fills before scoring:

```js
const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const fs = require("node:fs");
const path = require("node:path");
const test = require("node:test");
const { resolveTokens } = require("../helpers/harness/cssTokens");

const css = fs.readFileSync(path.join(__dirname, "../..", "src/index.css"), "utf8");
const load = () => import("../../src/utils/contrast.ts");

// Settings surfaces, composited the way the shipped classes composite them.
// Plan 01's colorRoles/plumNight tests score tokens against opaque surfaces;
// Settings also draws on translucent fills, so those are blended here
// (alpha-over, per channel) before scoring.
//   content pane     bg-background | dark:bg-surface-1            (SidebarModal.tsx:243)
//   SettingsPanel    bg-card/50    | dark:bg-surface-2/50         (SettingsSection.tsx SettingsPanel)
//   hovered row      hover:bg-foreground/3 | dark:hover:bg-white/3 (InferenceModeSelector row)
//   icon tile        bg-primary/10 | dark:bg-primary/15, over the hovered row
//   outline button   bg-muted/70 hover:bg-muted | dark:bg-surface-raised/90 dark:hover:bg-surface-raised
const PLAIN = [
  "--color-popover",
  "--color-muted",
  "--color-secondary",
  "--color-surface-1",
  "--color-surface-2",
  "--color-surface-3",
];

async function surfaces(tokens, theme) {
  const { parseHexColor } = await load();
  const hex = ({ r, g, b }) =>
    "#" + [r, g, b].map((v) => Math.round(v).toString(16).padStart(2, "0")).join("");
  const over = (fg, alpha, bg) => {
    const f = parseHexColor(fg);
    const b = parseHexColor(bg);
    return hex({
      r: f.r * alpha + b.r * (1 - alpha),
      g: f.g * alpha + b.g * (1 - alpha),
      b: f.b * alpha + b.b * (1 - alpha),
    });
  };
  const dark = theme === "dark";
  const pane = dark ? tokens["--color-surface-1"] : tokens["--color-background"];
  const panel = dark ? over(tokens["--color-surface-2"], 0.5, pane) : over(tokens["--color-card"], 0.5, pane);
  const hoverRow = dark ? over("#ffffff", 0.03, panel) : over(tokens["--color-foreground"], 0.03, panel);
  const tile = over(tokens["--color-primary"], dark ? 0.15 : 0.1, hoverRow);
  const outlineRest = dark
    ? over(tokens["--color-surface-raised"], 0.9, panel)
    : over(tokens["--color-muted"], 0.7, panel);
  const outlineHover = dark ? tokens["--color-surface-raised"] : tokens["--color-muted"];
  const out = { pane, panel, hoverRow, tile, outlineRest, outlineHover };
  for (const token of PLAIN) out[token.replace("--color-", "")] = tokens[token];
  return out;
}

const THEMES = [
  ["light", (t) => t.light],
  ["dark", (t) => t.dark],
];
const TEXT_ROLES = [
  "--color-foreground",
  "--color-muted-foreground",
  "--color-link",
  "--color-locality-device",
  "--color-locality-network",
  "--color-locality-remote",
];
// The icon tile only ever hosts the mode icon (foreground) and nothing else.
const TILE_TEXT_ROLES = ["--color-foreground", "--color-muted-foreground"];
const MARK_ROLES = [
  "--color-ring",
  "--color-locality-device",
  "--color-locality-network",
  "--color-locality-remote",
  "--color-destructive",
];

test("text roles meet 4.5:1 on every composited Settings surface in both themes", async () => {
  const { contrastRatio } = await load();
  const tokens = resolveTokens(css);
  for (const [theme, pick] of THEMES) {
    const t = pick(tokens);
    const s = await surfaces(t, theme);
    for (const [name, surface] of Object.entries(s)) {
      const roles = name === "tile" ? TILE_TEXT_ROLES : TEXT_ROLES;
      for (const role of roles) {
        const ratio = contrastRatio(t[role], surface);
        assert.ok(ratio >= 4.5, `${theme}: ${role} on ${name} (${surface}) is ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1`);
      }
    }
  }
});

test("ring, locality and status marks meet 3:1 on every composited Settings surface in both themes", async () => {
  const { contrastRatio } = await load();
  const tokens = resolveTokens(css);
  for (const [theme, pick] of THEMES) {
    const t = pick(tokens);
    const s = await surfaces(t, theme);
    for (const [name, surface] of Object.entries(s))
      for (const mark of MARK_ROLES) {
        const ratio = contrastRatio(t[mark], surface);
        assert.ok(ratio >= 3, `${theme}: ${mark} on ${name} (${surface}) is ${ratio.toFixed(2)}:1`);
      }
  }
});

// I13 token CCR: the light focus ring moves from the brand orange to its
// darker sibling. Plan 01 shipped this in f7d53e4; on an older Plan 01 base
// (172f9df) the ring is #ff5a1f and these assertions fail: that colour measures
// 2.86:1 on muted, 2.94:1 on the hovered row and 2.62:1 on the selected icon tile.
test("the light focus ring is the darker orange and Plum Night keeps its own", () => {
  const { light, dark } = resolveTokens(css);
  assert.equal(light["--color-ring"].toLowerCase(), "#e84e16");
  assert.equal(dark["--color-ring"].toLowerCase(), "#ff5a1f");
});

test("the old brand-orange ring would fail the Settings surfaces it was replaced for", async () => {
  const { contrastRatio } = await load();
  const t = resolveTokens(css).light;
  const s = await surfaces(t, "light");
  const failing = Object.entries(s).filter(([, surface]) => contrastRatio("#ff5a1f", surface) < 3);
  assert.ok(failing.length >= 4, `expected the old ring to fail several surfaces, failed ${failing.map(([n]) => n)}`);
});

test("status text roles that cannot clear 4.5:1 stay off Settings text", async () => {
  const { contrastRatio } = await load();
  const t = resolveTokens(css).light;
  const s = await surfaces(t, "light");
  // Why chips and the support-model row use foreground / locality roles for words.
  assert.ok(contrastRatio(t["--color-success"], s.panel) < 4.5, "success text is 3.30:1 on the panel");
  assert.ok(contrastRatio(t["--color-destructive"], s.muted) < 4.5, "destructive text is 4.43:1 on muted");
  assert.ok(contrastRatio(t["--color-destructive"], s.tile) < 4.5, "destructive text is 4.06:1 on the selected tile");
});

Against `f7d53e4` and later they are **baseline guards** that pin Settings-specific composites Plan 01 does not measure (hovered row, selected tile, outline buttons, half-opaque panel in both themes).

1. Create `src/components/ui/rovingNav.ts`:

   ```ts
   // Roving-tabindex arrow handling for radio groups and option grids.
   // Pure, so keyboard behaviour is testable without a DOM.

   export type NavKey = "ArrowUp" | "ArrowDown" | "ArrowLeft" | "ArrowRight" | "Home" | "End";

   // A vertical list moves with Up/Down; Left/Right are the secondary pair and
   // swap in right-to-left layouts. Returns `index` unchanged for any other key.
   export function stepLinear(
     index: number,
     key: string,
     disabled: readonly boolean[],
     rtl = false
   ): number {
     const n = disabled.length;
     if (n === 0 || disabled.every(Boolean)) return index;
     const scan = (from: number, dir: 1 | -1) => {
       let i = from;
       for (let step = 0; step < n; step++) {
         i = (i + dir + n) % n;
         if (!disabled[i]) return i;
       }
       return index;
     };
     const next = rtl ? "ArrowLeft" : "ArrowRight";
     const previous = rtl ? "ArrowRight" : "ArrowLeft";
     switch (key) {
       case "ArrowDown":
       case next:
         return scan(index, 1);
       case "ArrowUp":
       case previous:
         return scan(index, -1);
       case "Home":
         return scan(n - 1, 1);
       case "End":
         return scan(0, -1);
       default:
         return index;
     }
   }
   ```

   Up and Down always move; Left and Right are the secondary pair and swap when `rtl` is true. Task 13 adds `stepGrid` to this file.

3. Create `src/components/settings/routing/RouteChips.tsx`:

   ```tsx
   import type { TFunction } from "i18next";
   import { useTranslation } from "react-i18next";
   import { providerDisplayLabel } from "../../../lib/locality";
   import type { ResolvedRoute, RouteState } from "../../../lib/routeGraph";
   import { formatDecimalBytes } from "../../../utils/formatBytes";
   import { cn } from "../../lib/utils";
   import {
     CircleAlert,
     CircleCheck,
     Clock,
     Download,
     KeyRound,
     Lock,
     Minus,
     Server,
     WifiOff,
   } from "../../icons";
   import { LocalityRing } from "../../ui/LocalityRing";

   // Route chips (DESIGN.md "Settings · Routing"): a state is always glyph plus
   // words, and colour is a third, redundant cue. Chip text uses foreground,
   // muted-foreground or the device role only: text-destructive measures 4.43:1
   // on the muted, secondary and surface-3 fills, so the destructive hue lives on
   // the glyph (a non-text mark, 3:1) instead.

   // eslint-disable-next-line react-refresh/only-export-components -- pure label helper shared with the Patchbay and Apply bar
   export function routeStateLabel(
     state: RouteState,
     t: TFunction | ((key: string, options?: object) => string)
   ): string {
     switch (state.status) {
       case "ready":
         return t("routes.state.ready");
       case "off":
         return t("routes.state.off");
       case "unknown":
         return t("routes.state.checking");
       case "needsModel":
         return state.sizeBytes
           ? t("routes.state.download", { size: formatDecimalBytes(state.sizeBytes) })
           : t("routes.state.chooseModel");
       case "needsKey":
         return state.provider ? t("routes.state.addKey") : t("routes.state.chooseProvider");
       case "needsUrl":
         return t("routes.state.addUrl");
       case "unreachable":
         if (state.detail === "sealed") return t("routes.state.sealed");
         if (state.detail === "retired") return t("routes.state.retired");
         if (state.detail === "unsupported") return t("routes.state.unsupported");
         return t("routes.state.cantReach");
     }
   }

   const TEXT_STYLE: Record<RouteState["status"], string> = {
     ready: "text-locality-device",
     off: "text-muted-foreground",
     unknown: "text-muted-foreground",
     needsModel: "text-foreground",
     needsKey: "text-foreground",
     needsUrl: "text-foreground",
     unreachable: "text-foreground",
   };

   function glyphStyle(state: RouteState): string {
     switch (state.status) {
       case "ready":
         return "text-locality-device";
       case "off":
       case "unknown":
         return "text-muted-foreground";
       case "needsModel":
         return "text-foreground";
       case "needsKey":
       case "needsUrl":
         return "text-destructive";
       case "unreachable":
         return state.detail === "sealed" ? "text-muted-foreground" : "text-destructive";
     }
   }

   function StateGlyph({ state }: { state: RouteState }) {
     const cls = cn("h-3 w-3 shrink-0", glyphStyle(state));
     switch (state.status) {
       case "ready":
         return <CircleCheck className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
       case "off":
         return <Minus className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
       case "unknown":
         return <Clock className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
       case "needsModel":
         return <Download className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
       case "needsKey":
         return <KeyRound className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
       case "needsUrl":
         return <Server className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
       case "unreachable":
         if (state.detail === "sealed") return <Lock className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
         if (state.detail === "retired" || state.detail === "unsupported")
           return <CircleAlert className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
         return <WifiOff className={cls} aria-hidden="true" />;
     }
   }

   export function RouteStateChip({ state, className }: { state: RouteState; className?: string }) {
     const { t } = useTranslation();
     return (
       <span
         data-state={state.status}
         className={cn(
           "inline-flex h-6 items-center gap-1 rounded-full px-2 text-xs font-medium tabular-nums",
           TEXT_STYLE[state.status],
           className
         )}
       >
         <StateGlyph state={state} />
         {routeStateLabel(state, t)}
       </span>
     );
   }

   export function RouteDestinationChip({
     route,
     className,
   }: {
     route: Pick<ResolvedRoute, "locality" | "providerId" | "model">;
     className?: string;
   }) {
     const { t } = useTranslation();
     // Plan 01: provider names in UI go through providerDisplayLabel so
     // "Custom endpoint" and "Unknown provider" are localised.
     const providerName = route.providerId ? providerDisplayLabel(route.providerId, t) : null;
     const place =
       route.locality === "remote"
         ? (providerName ?? t("routes.place.chooseProvider"))
         : t(`locality.${route.locality}`);
     const ringLabel =
       route.locality === "remote"
         ? t("locality.remote", { provider: providerName ?? "" })
         : t(`locality.${route.locality}`);
     return (
       <span
         className={cn(
           "inline-flex h-6 min-w-0 max-w-[260px] items-center gap-1.5 text-xs font-medium text-foreground",
           className
         )}
       >
         <LocalityRing locality={route.locality} label={ringLabel} provider={providerName} size={16} />
         <span className="truncate" dir="auto">
           {route.model ? `${place} · ${route.model}` : place}
         </span>
       </span>
     );
   }
   ```

   `text-locality-device` exists because Plan 01 registers `--color-locality-device` in `@theme`; it measures 4.91:1 or better on every Settings text surface in light and above 9:1 in Plum Night (the icon tile hosts only the mode icon, so it is scored for foreground and muted-foreground only). Do not use `text-success` or `text-warning` for words (3.30:1 and 3.19:1 on white). The `unknown` state is a muted "Checking…" with a clock glyph and never shares a style with `ready`.

4. Rework `InferenceModeSelector` in `src/components/ui/SettingsSection.tsx` (`:111-197`). Keep `InferenceModeOption` as is. Add these imports below the existing `InferenceMode` import:

   ```tsx

   ```

   Replace the component with:

   ```tsx
   export function InferenceModeSelector({
     label,
     modes,
     activeMode,
     onSelect,
     routeState,
     stagedMode = null,
   }: {
     /** Accessible name of the radio group, e.g. "Dictation runs on". */
     label: string;
     modes: InferenceModeOption[];
     activeMode: InferenceMode | null;
     onSelect: (mode: InferenceMode) => void;
     /** State of the route the applied mode resolves to; shown next to "Current". */
     routeState?: RouteState;
     /** A mode staged behind Apply (Task 8). It is the checked radio; the applied one stays "Current". */
     stagedMode?: InferenceMode | null;
   }) {
     const { t, i18n } = useTranslation();
     const refs = React.useRef<(HTMLButtonElement | null)[]>([]);
     const [focusIndex, setFocusIndex] = React.useState<number | null>(null);
     const rtl = (i18n?.dir?.() ?? "ltr") === "rtl";
     const disabled = modes.map((mode) => !!mode.disabled);
     const checkedId = stagedMode ?? activeMode;
     const checkedIndex = modes.findIndex((mode) => mode.id === checkedId);
     const anchor = checkedIndex >= 0 ? checkedIndex : Math.max(0, disabled.indexOf(false));
     // One tab stop: the radio that has focus, otherwise the checked one.
     const tabStop =
       focusIndex !== null && focusIndex < modes.length && !disabled[focusIndex] ? focusIndex : anchor;

     // Arrow keys move focus only. Choosing a mode changes a route (instantly on
     // device, staged behind Apply otherwise), so it takes Enter or Space, which a
     // <button> turns into a click.
     const onKeyDown = (event: React.KeyboardEvent, index: number) => {
       const next = stepLinear(index, event.key, disabled, rtl);
       if (next === index) return;
       event.preventDefault();
       setFocusIndex(next);
       refs.current[next]?.focus();
     };

     return (
       <SettingsPanel className="overflow-hidden">
         <div
           role="radiogroup"
           aria-label={label}
           onBlur={(event) => {
             if (!event.currentTarget.contains(event.relatedTarget as Node | null))
               setFocusIndex(null);
           }}
         >
           {modes.map((mode, index) => {
             const isChecked = index === checkedIndex;
             const isCurrent = activeMode === mode.id;
             const isStaged = stagedMode === mode.id && stagedMode !== activeMode;
             const isDisabled = !!mode.disabled;
             return (
               <SettingsPanelRow
                 key={mode.id}
                 className={`transition-colors duration-[var(--motion-fast)] ${
                   isDisabled ? "" : "hover:bg-foreground/3 dark:hover:bg-white/3"
                 }`}
               >
                 <button
                   role="radio"
                   aria-checked={isChecked}
                   tabIndex={index === tabStop ? 0 : -1}
                   type="button"
                   aria-disabled={isDisabled || undefined}
                   ref={(el) => {
                     refs.current[index] = el;
                   }}
                   onClick={() => {
                     if (!isDisabled) onSelect(mode.id);
                   }}
                   onFocus={() => setFocusIndex(index)}
                   onKeyDown={(event) => onKeyDown(event, index)}
                   className={`group flex w-full cursor-pointer items-center gap-3 rounded-md text-start outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring ${
                     isDisabled ? "cursor-not-allowed opacity-60" : ""
                   }`}
                 >
                   <div
                     className={`flex h-8 w-8 shrink-0 items-center justify-center rounded-md transition-colors duration-[var(--motion-fast)] ${
                       isChecked
                         ? "bg-primary/10 dark:bg-primary/15"
                         : "bg-muted/60 group-hover:bg-muted dark:bg-surface-raised dark:group-hover:bg-surface-3"
                     }`}
                   >
                     <div
                       className={`transition-colors duration-[var(--motion-fast)] ${
                         isChecked ? "text-foreground" : "text-muted-foreground"
                       }`}
                     >
                       {mode.icon}
                     </div>
                   </div>
                   <div className="min-w-0 flex-1">
                     <div className="flex flex-wrap items-center gap-2">
                       <span className="text-xs font-medium text-foreground">{mode.label}</span>
                       {isCurrent && !isDisabled && (
                         <span className="rounded-sm bg-muted px-1.5 py-px text-xs font-medium text-foreground">
                           {t("routes.selection.current")}
                         </span>
                       )}
                       {isCurrent && routeState && (
                         <RouteStateChip state={routeState} className="h-5 px-0" />
                       )}
                       {isStaged && (
                         <span className="rounded-sm border border-dashed border-locality-remote px-1.5 py-px text-xs font-medium text-foreground">
                           {t("routes.selection.staged")}
                         </span>
                       )}
                       {isDisabled && mode.badge && (
                         <span className="rounded-sm bg-muted/80 px-1.5 py-px text-xs font-medium text-muted-foreground dark:bg-surface-3">
                           {mode.badge}
                         </span>
                       )}
                     </div>
                     <p className="mt-0.5 text-xs text-muted-foreground">{mode.description}</p>
                   </div>
                   <div
                     aria-hidden="true"
                     className={`h-4 w-4 shrink-0 rounded-full border-2 transition-colors duration-[var(--motion-fast)] ${
                       isChecked
                         ? "border-ring bg-ring"
                         : "border-border-hover dark:border-border-subtle"
                     }`}
                   >
                     {isChecked && (
                       <div className="flex h-full w-full items-center justify-center">
                         <div className="h-1.5 w-1.5 rounded-full bg-primary-foreground" />
                       </div>
                     )}
                   </div>
                 </button>
               </SettingsPanelRow>
             );
           })}
         </div>
       </SettingsPanel>
     );
   }
   ```

   Notes: the `onFocus` handler keeps the tab stop on whichever radio has focus, and the group's `onBlur` returns it to the checked radio when focus leaves. All transitions use `duration-[var(--motion-fast)]`, never a literal duration. The mode icon is `text-foreground` when checked, because brand-orange on its own tint is 2.62:1.
