### Task 6: Route planner: one patch for preview, commit and Undo

Closes **I5** (preview, commit and Undo describe different configurations) and **I6** (a one-route change silently changes inheriting routes). It also provides the classification (`kind`) and click-time blocker that Task 7 uses to close I1.

There is one computation, and nothing else may write a route:
- **Shared provider switches.** `src/lib/providerSwitchPlans.ts` holds the provider-switch logic, extracted from the store's `switchCloudTranscriptionProvider` and `switchReasoningProvider`, including the per-provider model memory. Both store actions now call these planners and then `applyRoutePatch`, so the store and the planner run the same implementation.
- **The planner.** `src/lib/routePlanner.ts` turns a target into the exact raw store writes (the patch). It simulates the patch on a copy of the state and resolves all 11 routes before and after. It lists every route whose destination, model, payload or state changes, including coupled ones: Note recording or Upload inheriting dictation, and assistant vision following the assistant. It also records the prior raw value of every written key (the Undo patch).
- **One patch for everything.** Preview is the after-resolution of that patch. Commit and Undo both await `applyRoutePatch(patch)`. A patch with enterprise recipient settings is sent once to main with the complete old enterprise tuple as its compare-and-set expectation. Main atomically persists the prospective `.env` snapshot before materializing any new enterprise values; only an acknowledged success lets the renderer write localStorage/store state or announce success. A conflict refreshes the canonical non-secret tuple and keeps the draft for review; a write failure leaves both main and renderer on the previous tuple.
- **Switches and options are planned too (I1 follow-up).** The enable switches (`useCleanupModel`, `useDictationTranslation`, `useDictationAgent`, `voiceAgentScreenContext`, `useDictationAgentVisionModel`), the Corti region and tenant (`cortiEnvironment`, `cortiTenant`) and the provider web-search preference (patch key `providerSearch:<scope>`, stored in localStorage as `personalWebSearch:<scope>`) are route-patch keys. Turning a route on counts as a new recipient when it ends off the device, so it stages. Switching a route off (or configuring a route that is off) sends nothing new, so it is instant. The vision override is the one switch that is not an on/off: either direction can move screenshots to another provider, and the planner stages that like any recipient change. A Corti region switch changes the speech host (`api.us.corti.app` ↔ `api.eu.corti.app`) and stages when a speech route uses Corti (Corti text always calls `ai.eu.corti.app`, Task 1's `providerHosts["corti:text"]`, so a text-only profile switches instantly); the tenant keeps the host and is instant. Web search on adds the `webSearch` payload part and stages; off is instant.
- **Enterprise recipient settings are planned too (R2-1/R3-1).** `bedrockRegion`, `azureEndpoint`, `vertexProject`, `vertexLocation` and `vertexAuthSource` (`ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS`) are route-patch keys. The persisted Vertex source is independent of secret presence: saving/removing/undoing a key changes readiness only, while a source change changes the express-vs-ADC recipient and stages across every active Vertex route, including inheriting scopes. `azureApiVersion` (query parameter only) and `bedrockProfile` (a credential source on the same host, refreshed through Task 2's presence) stay outside. `planPatch` adds coupled writes before diffing: a `bedrockRegion` write rewrites each Bedrock scope's geo-scoped model through `adjustBedrockModelForRegion`. `applyRoutePatch` sends the enterprise subset once through `saveEnterpriseRoutePatch({ patch, expected })`; `expected` is the complete old five-key non-secret tuple. Main compares it in the shared environment-write queue, atomically writes the prospective `.env` snapshot, then commits the in-memory tuple. A conflict returns the canonical tuple without writing, refreshes the renderer, and leaves the draft for re-review. The legacy single-field savers use the same serialized transaction path. When main facts are unknown, a changed active route still counts as a recipient change and Apply stays blocked until facts load.
- **Apply readiness (R2-9, ROUTE side).** `routeBlocker` blocks every changed, enabled, off-device route that is not `ready`: `needsKey` blocks for Codex and the enterprise clouds too, and `needsModel` blocks with or without a size. Device and off routes never block. `SETUP_AFTER_APPLY` stays exported for copy only (Task 8's "sign in here first"); it no longer unblocks Apply.

Create `test/helpers/enterpriseRoutePatch.test.js` against Task 2's `realCredentialEnv` harness. This executes the real transaction method with in-memory files and a held `.env` rename; it never loads a user profile or sends a request.

```js
const assert = require("node:assert/strict");
const test = require("node:test");
const { realCredentialEnv } = require("./harness/realCredentialEnv");

const initial = {
  BEDROCK_REGION: "us-east-1",
  AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT: "https://east.openai.azure.com/openai",
  VERTEX_PROJECT: "acme-prod",
  VERTEX_LOCATION: "us-central1",
  VERTEX_AUTH_SOURCE: "adc",
};
const tick = () => new Promise((resolve) => setImmediate(resolve));
const holdEnvRename = (fs) => fs.holdNext((op, name) => op === "rename" && name === ".env");

test("enterprise route patches are expected-tuple, atomic and reset-fenced", async (t) => {
  await t.test("the public transaction requires a complete expected tuple before any file write", async (t) => {
    const { env, fs } = realCredentialEnv(t, initial);
    const valid = env.getEnterpriseRouteSettings();
    for (const options of [undefined, {}, { expected: undefined }, { expected: null }, { expected: { ...valid, vertexProject: undefined } }]) {
      assert.throws(() => env.saveEnterpriseRoutePatch({ azureEndpoint: "https://west.openai.azure.com/openai" }, options), /expected/i);
    }
    assert.deepEqual(fs.log.filter((line) => line.includes(".env")), [], "invalid expectations produce no disk IO");
  });

  await t.test("one held multi-field rename keeps RAM and disk old until ACK, then commits the complete tuple", async (t) => {
    const { env, fs } = realCredentialEnv(t, initial);
    const { path: envPath } = await env.saveAllKeysToEnvFile();
    const beforeBytes = fs.files.get(envPath).toString("utf8");
    const before = env.getEnterpriseRouteSettings();
    holdEnvRename(fs);
    const pending = env.saveEnterpriseRoutePatch({
      azureEndpoint: "https://west.openai.azure.com/openai",
      vertexAuthSource: "apiKey",
    }, { expected: before });
    const rename = await fs.nextHold();
    assert.deepEqual(env.getEnterpriseRouteSettings(), before);
    assert.equal(fs.files.get(envPath).toString("utf8"), beforeBytes);
    rename.release();
    const ack = await pending;
    assert.deepEqual(ack, {
      success: true,
      current: { ...before, azureEndpoint: "https://west.openai.azure.com/openai", vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" },
    });
    assert.deepEqual(env.getEnterpriseRouteSettings(), ack.current);
    assert.match(fs.files.get(envPath).toString("utf8"), /AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT=https:\/\/west\.openai\.azure\.com\/openai/);
    assert.match(fs.files.get(envPath).toString("utf8"), /VERTEX_AUTH_SOURCE=apiKey/);
    assert.equal(fs.log.filter((line) => line === "rename .env").length, 2, "one seed write plus one patch rename");
  });

  await t.test("a stale expected tuple conflicts without writing and a failed rename restores the prior tuple", async (t) => {
    const { env, fs } = realCredentialEnv(t, initial);
    const { path: envPath } = await env.saveAllKeysToEnvFile();
    const before = env.getEnterpriseRouteSettings();
    const beforeBytes = fs.files.get(envPath).toString("utf8");
    const writesBefore = fs.log.filter((line) => line.startsWith("writeFile .env")).length;
    const conflict = await env.saveEnterpriseRoutePatch({ azureEndpoint: "https://west.openai.azure.com/openai" }, {
      expected: { ...before, azureEndpoint: "https://other.openai.azure.com/openai" },
    });
    assert.deepEqual(conflict, { success: false, conflict: true, current: before });
    assert.equal(fs.log.filter((line) => line.startsWith("writeFile .env")).length, writesBefore);

    holdEnvRename(fs);
    const failed = env.saveEnterpriseRoutePatch({ azureEndpoint: "https://west.openai.azure.com/openai" }, { expected: before });
    const rename = await fs.nextHold();
    rename.fail(new Error("disk unavailable"));
    await assert.rejects(failed, /disk unavailable/);
    assert.deepEqual(env.getEnterpriseRouteSettings(), before);
    assert.equal(fs.files.get(envPath).toString("utf8"), beforeBytes, "atomic rename failure leaves the old file intact");
  });

  await t.test("reset during a held rename rejects the patch and erases its late file", async (t) => {
    const { env, fs } = realCredentialEnv(t, initial);
    const { path: envPath } = await env.saveAllKeysToEnvFile();
    holdEnvRename(fs);
    const pending = env.saveEnterpriseRoutePatch({ azureEndpoint: "https://west.openai.azure.com/openai" }, {
      expected: env.getEnterpriseRouteSettings(),
    });
    const rename = await fs.nextHold();
    const reset = env.clearAllPersistedData();
    await tick();
    rename.release();
    await assert.rejects(pending, { code: "ENV_RESET" });
    await reset;
    assert.equal(fs.files.has(envPath), false);
    assert.equal(process.env.AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, undefined);
  });
});
```

```js
    [`${prefix}RemoteUrl`]: "",
  };
}

// Every key a route patch may write, at a known value. Every route is on the
// device and enabled, nothing inherits a custom value, and the dictionary is empty.
function routeBaseState() {

    meetingWhisperModel: "",
    meetingParakeetModel: "",
    meetingCohereModel: "",
    meetingCloudTranscriptionProvider: "",
    meetingCloudTranscriptionModel: "",
    meetingCloudTranscriptionBaseUrl: "",
    meetingRemoteTranscriptionUrl: "",
    uploadTranscriptionMode: "local",
    uploadUseLocalWhisper: true,
    uploadCloudTranscriptionMode: "",

    uploadWhisperModel: "",
    uploadParakeetModel: "",
    uploadCohereModel: "",
    uploadCloudTranscriptionProvider: "",
    uploadCloudTranscriptionModel: "",
    uploadCloudTranscriptionBaseUrl: "",

// Facts as main would report them: model inventories unknown (device routes
// never block), keys saved for openai, groq, anthropic and deepgram only.
function testFacts(overrides = {}) {
  return {
    installed: { whisper: null, sherpa: null, llm: null },
    credentials: new Map([
      ["openai", true],
      ["groq", true],
      ["anthropic", true],
      ["deepgram", true],

    // Task 2's per-field presence (R2-1); only Vertex's `key` changes a host.
    credentialFields: new Map([

    enterpriseMain: { bedrockEndpoint: { set: false, host: null }, bedrockProfile: false, vertexApiKeyEnv: false, vertexProjectEnv: false },

};

module.exports = { PAYLOAD_PART_IDS, TEST_COPY, QWEN, routeBaseState, testFacts, MIGRATED_STORAGE };
```

   ```ts
   import modelRegistryData from "../models/modelRegistryData.json";
   import { pickDefaultModelId, pickProviderDefaultModel } from "../models/providerDefaultModel";
   import { INFERENCE_SCOPES, type InferenceScope } from "../config/inferenceScopes";
   import type { SettingsState } from "../stores/settingsStore";
   import { adjustBedrockModelForRegion } from "../utils/bedrockRegions";
   import type { TranscriptionPolicyContext } from "../utils/providerSelection";

   // Provider-switch patches shared by the settings store's own switch actions
   // and the route planner (routePlanner.ts), so a previewed switch is the
   // committed switch. Pure: reads the state it is given and returns raw store
   // writes. It imports neither the store (the store imports this module) nor
   // ModelRegistry (which imports the store).

   const STT_ROUTE_KEYS = [
     "transcriptionMode",
     "useLocalWhisper",
     "cloudTranscriptionMode",
     "localTranscriptionProvider",
     "whisperModel",
     "parakeetModel",
     "cohereModel",
     "cloudTranscriptionProvider",
     "cloudTranscriptionModel",
     "cloudTranscriptionBaseUrl",
     "remoteTranscriptionUrl",
     "remoteTranscriptionModel",
     "meetingTranscriptionMode",
     "meetingUseLocalWhisper",
     "meetingCloudTranscriptionMode",
     "meetingLocalTranscriptionProvider",
     "meetingWhisperModel",
     "meetingParakeetModel",
     "meetingCohereModel",
     "meetingCloudTranscriptionProvider",
     "meetingCloudTranscriptionModel",
     "meetingCloudTranscriptionBaseUrl",
     "meetingRemoteTranscriptionUrl",
     "uploadTranscriptionMode",
     "uploadUseLocalWhisper",
     "uploadCloudTranscriptionMode",
     "uploadLocalTranscriptionProvider",
     "uploadWhisperModel",
     "uploadParakeetModel",
     "uploadCohereModel",
     "uploadCloudTranscriptionProvider",
     "uploadCloudTranscriptionModel",
     "uploadCloudTranscriptionBaseUrl",
   ] as const satisfies readonly (keyof SettingsState)[];

   // The vision scope's mode is deliberately absent. The override is
   // provider-only, and its mode is never persisted (settingsStore.ts:1757-1758),
   // so a patch that tries to write it is refused.
   const LLM_ROUTE_KEYS = [
     "cleanupMode",
     "cleanupProvider",
     "cleanupModel",
     "cleanupCloudMode",
     "cleanupCloudBaseUrl",
     "cleanupRemoteUrl",
     "dictationAgentMode",
     "dictationAgentProvider",
     "dictationAgentModel",
     "dictationAgentCloudMode",
     "dictationAgentCloudBaseUrl",
     "dictationAgentRemoteUrl",
     "dictationAgentVisionProvider",
     "dictationAgentVisionModel",
     "dictationAgentVisionCloudMode",
     "dictationAgentVisionCloudBaseUrl",
     "noteFormattingMode",
     "noteFormattingProvider",
     "noteFormattingModel",
     "noteFormattingCloudMode",
     "noteFormattingCloudBaseUrl",
     "noteFormattingRemoteUrl",
     "chatAgentMode",
     "chatAgentProvider",
     "chatAgentModel",
     "chatAgentCloudMode",
     "chatAgentCloudBaseUrl",
     "chatAgentRemoteUrl",
     "translationMode",
     "translationProvider",
     "translationModel",
     "translationCloudMode",
     "translationCloudBaseUrl",
     "translationRemoteUrl",
   ] as const satisfies readonly (keyof SettingsState)[];

   // Switches that turn a route on or off. Turning one on can add a recipient,
   // so the editors send them through the planner (Task 8), never a setter.
   export const ROUTE_SWITCH_KEYS = [
     "useCleanupModel",
     "useDictationTranslation",
     "useDictationAgent",
     "voiceAgentScreenContext",
     "useDictationAgentVisionModel",
   ] as const satisfies readonly (keyof SettingsState)[];
   export type RouteSwitchKey = (typeof ROUTE_SWITCH_KEYS)[number];

   // Options that decide the receiving host without being a provider field:
   // Corti's region picks api.<region>.corti.app (cortiTranscription.js:39,
   // cortiStreaming.js:48); the tenant picks the auth realm on the same host.
   export const ROUTE_OPTION_KEYS = ["cortiEnvironment", "cortiTenant"] as const satisfies readonly (keyof SettingsState)[];

   // Enterprise settings that pick the receiving host (R2-1/R3-1): the Bedrock region
   // (bedrock-runtime.<region>…), the Azure endpoint (its own host), and Vertex's
   // persisted auth source (express vs ADC), project and location (<location>-aiplatform…;
   // the project scopes the ADC request and decides readiness). Main hands them to enterpriseAiProviders.js
   // (main.js:447-457). azureApiVersion (a query parameter) and bedrockProfile (a
   // credential source on the same host) are deliberately not route keys.
   export const ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS = [
     "bedrockRegion",
     "azureEndpoint",
     "vertexProject",
     "vertexLocation",
     "vertexAuthSource",
   ] as const satisfies readonly (keyof SettingsState)[];
   export type RouteEnterpriseKey = (typeof ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS)[number];

   // The provider web-search preference lives in localStorage as
   // personalWebSearch:<scope> (src/utils/providerSearch.ts), not in the store.
   // A patch carries it as providerSearch:<scope>; only these scopes support it
   // (supportsProviderSearch, providerSearch.ts:2-8).
   export type ProviderSearchScope = "chatIntelligence" | "dictationAgent";
   export const PROVIDER_SEARCH_PATCH_KEYS = [
     "providerSearch:chatIntelligence",
     "providerSearch:dictationAgent",
   ] as const;
   export type ProviderSearchPatchKey = (typeof PROVIDER_SEARCH_PATCH_KEYS)[number];

   export function providerSearchScope(key: string): ProviderSearchScope | null {
     return (PROVIDER_SEARCH_PATCH_KEYS as readonly string[]).includes(key)
       ? (key.slice("providerSearch:".length) as ProviderSearchScope)
       : null;
   }

   // The only store fields a route patch may write. No secret is on this list,
   // so a patch can never carry key material (applyRoutePatch enforces it).
   export const ROUTE_PATCH_KEYS = [
     ...STT_ROUTE_KEYS,
     ...LLM_ROUTE_KEYS,
     "transcriptionModelByProvider",
     "reasoningModelByProvider",
     ...ROUTE_SWITCH_KEYS,
     ...ROUTE_OPTION_KEYS,
     ...ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS,
   ] as const;

   export type NonSecretKeys = (typeof ROUTE_PATCH_KEYS)[number];
   export type SettingsPatch = Partial<Pick<SettingsState, NonSecretKeys>> &
     Partial<Record<ProviderSearchPatchKey, boolean>>;
   export const ROUTE_PATCH_KEY_SET: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set<string>([
     ...ROUTE_PATCH_KEYS,
     ...PROVIDER_SEARCH_PATCH_KEYS,
   ]);

   // Independent task slots used only when the user changes a provider.
   export const TRANSCRIPTION_CONTEXT_KEYS = [
     {
       context: "dictation",
       provider: "cloudTranscriptionProvider",
       model: "cloudTranscriptionModel",
     },
     {
       context: "meeting",
       provider: "meetingCloudTranscriptionProvider",
       model: "meetingCloudTranscriptionModel",
     },
     {
       context: "upload",
       provider: "uploadCloudTranscriptionProvider",
       model: "uploadCloudTranscriptionModel",
     },
   ] as const;

   export const ENTERPRISE_PROVIDER_IDS: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["bedrock", "azure", "vertex"]);

   function transcriptionProviderModels(
     providerId: string,
     context: TranscriptionPolicyContext
   ): Array<{ id: string; streaming?: boolean }> {
     const models =
       modelRegistryData.transcriptionProviders.find((provider) => provider.id === providerId)
         ?.models ?? [];
     return context === "meeting" ? models.filter((model) => model.streaming) : models;
   }

   export function defaultTranscriptionModel(
     providerId: string,
     context: TranscriptionPolicyContext
   ): string {
     return transcriptionProviderModels(providerId, context)[0]?.id ?? "whisper-1";
   }

   function transcriptionModelBelongsToProvider(
     providerId: string,
     modelId: string,
     context: TranscriptionPolicyContext
   ): boolean {
     if (providerId === "custom") return Boolean(modelId);
     return transcriptionProviderModels(providerId, context).some((model) => model.id === modelId);
   }

   export function reasoningModelBelongsToProvider(providerId: string, modelId: string): boolean {
     if (!modelId) return false;
     // Custom and OpenRouter ids are free-form; any remembered id is valid.
     // Tinfoil's registry entry is refreshed in place from its live catalog.
     if (providerId === "custom" || providerId === "openrouter") return true;
     return (
       modelRegistryData.cloudProviders
         .find((provider) => provider.id === providerId)
         ?.models.some((model) => model.id === modelId) ?? false
     );
   }

   interface RegistryModel {
     id: string;
     supportsVision?: boolean;
   }
   interface RegistryProvider {
     id: string;
     defaultModel?: string;
     models?: RegistryModel[];
   }

   // The registry's default rule (providerDefaultModel.ts): a named default
   // wins, otherwise the first (best) model. Vision keeps only models flagged
   // supportsVision. Enterprise entries carry no vision flags, so all of their
   // models qualify. Codex, custom and OpenRouter have no registry list: "".
   export function defaultCloudModel(providerId: string, options: { vision?: boolean } = {}): string {
     const cloud = (modelRegistryData.cloudProviders as RegistryProvider[]).find(
       (provider) => provider.id === providerId
     );
     if (cloud) {
       const models = options.vision
         ? (cloud.models ?? []).filter((model) => model.supportsVision)
         : cloud.models;
       return pickProviderDefaultModel(models, cloud.defaultModel)?.id ?? "";
     }
     return pickDefaultModelId(
       (modelRegistryData.enterpriseProviders as RegistryProvider[]).find(
         (provider) => provider.id === providerId
       )
     );
   }

   // The same read as selectResolvedLLMConfig (settingsStore.ts:2629-2662):
   // the scope's own value, else its fallback scope's, else "".
   export function resolvedScopeField(
     state: SettingsState,
     scope: InferenceScope,
     field: "provider" | "model" | "cloudBaseUrl"
   ): string {
     const def = INFERENCE_SCOPES[scope] as {
       storeKeys: Partial<Record<string, keyof SettingsState>>;
       fallbackScope?: string;
     };
     const key = def.storeKeys[field];
     const own = key ? ((state[key] as string | undefined) ?? "") : "";
     if (own) return own;
     return def.fallbackScope
       ? resolvedScopeField(state, def.fallbackScope as InferenceScope, field)
       : "";
   }

   function write(patch: SettingsPatch, key: keyof SettingsState, value: unknown): void {
     (patch as Record<string, unknown>)[key as string] = value;
   }

   // Writes that must travel with `patch` so the routes it moves still run (R2-1).
   // Bedrock cross-region inference profile ids are geo-scoped (us./eu./apac.,
   // bedrockRegions.ts:1-3): a region in another geography needs the matching
   // prefix, which EnterpriseProviderConfig.tsx:115-118 wrote with the region.
   // Every scope that resolves to Bedrock and stores its own model is adjusted
   // (the old handler adjusted only the scope on screen); inheriting scopes
   // follow their parent. A model key the patch itself writes is kept verbatim:
   // that is the caller's explicit choice, and it makes a re-planned undoPatch
   // (Task 7's Undo) add nothing. Called by planPatch only; applyRoutePatch never
   // expands a patch.
   // The model keys a region change can rewrite in `state`: every scope that
   // resolves to Bedrock and stores its own model. The planner also pins these
   // in the undoPatch, so a re-planned Undo restores the region and rewrites no model.
   export function bedrockCoupledModelKeys(state: SettingsState): (keyof SettingsState)[] {
     const found: (keyof SettingsState)[] = [];
     for (const scope of Object.keys(INFERENCE_SCOPES) as InferenceScope[]) {
       const keys = INFERENCE_SCOPES[scope].storeKeys;
       // The vision scope's mode is never persisted (settingsStore.ts:1757-1758); it is provider-only.
       const mode = state[keys.mode] as string | undefined;
       if (scope !== "dictationAgentVision" && mode !== "enterprise" && mode !== "providers") continue;
       if (resolvedScopeField(state, scope, "provider") !== "bedrock") continue;
       if ((state[keys.model] as string | undefined) ?? "") found.push(keys.model);
     }
     return found;
   }

   export function planEnterpriseCoupling(state: SettingsState, patch: SettingsPatch): SettingsPatch {
     const coupled: SettingsPatch = {};
     const region = patch.bedrockRegion;
     // Only a real region change couples; re-typing the current region writes nothing.
     if (region === undefined || region === state.bedrockRegion) return coupled;
     const after = { ...state, ...patch } as SettingsState;
     for (const key of bedrockCoupledModelKeys(after)) {
       if (key in patch) continue;
       const own = after[key] as string;
       const adjusted = adjustBedrockModelForRegion(own, region);
       if (adjusted !== own) write(coupled, key, adjusted);
     }
     return coupled;
   }

   // Every provider shares one model slot per scope, so a plain provider write
   // destroys the outgoing provider's model (the "Parasail" wipe). This plan
   // remembers the outgoing model and restores the incoming provider's last one.
   export function planTranscriptionProviderSwitch(
     state: SettingsState,
     context: TranscriptionPolicyContext,
     providerId: string
   ): SettingsPatch {
     const patch: SettingsPatch = {};
     const keys = TRANSCRIPTION_CONTEXT_KEYS.find((entry) => entry.context === context);
     if (!keys) return patch;
     // Meeting/upload raw keys default to "" (inherit from dictation), so work
     // against resolved values. Restoring writes a concrete model — the scope
     // stops inheriting the dictation model from that point on.
     const outgoingProvider = (state[keys.provider] as string) || state.cloudTranscriptionProvider;
     if (outgoingProvider === providerId) {
       write(patch, keys.provider, providerId);
       return patch;
     }
     const outgoingModel = (state[keys.model] as string) || state.cloudTranscriptionModel;
     const memory = { ...state.transcriptionModelByProvider };
     if (outgoingProvider && outgoingModel) {
       memory[`${context}:${outgoingProvider}`] = outgoingModel;
       patch.transcriptionModelByProvider = memory;
     }
     const remembered = memory[`${context}:${providerId}`];
     write(patch, keys.provider, providerId);
     write(
       patch,
       keys.model,
       remembered && transcriptionModelBelongsToProvider(providerId, remembered, context)
         ? remembered
         : defaultTranscriptionModel(providerId, context)
     );
     return patch;
   }

   // LLM twin. The caller supplies the provider's default model because dynamic
   // catalogs (Tinfoil) live in the UI.
   export function planReasoningProviderSwitch(
     state: SettingsState,
     scope: InferenceScope,
     providerId: string,
     fallbackModel = ""
   ): SettingsPatch {
     const keys = INFERENCE_SCOPES[scope].storeKeys;
     const currentProvider = resolvedScopeField(state, scope, "provider");
     const currentModel = resolvedScopeField(state, scope, "model");
     const memory = { ...state.reasoningModelByProvider };
     const patch: SettingsPatch = {};
     // Only remember a model the outgoing provider actually owns — after a
     // local/cloud mode round-trip the shared slot can hold a foreign id.
     if (currentProvider && currentProvider !== providerId) {
       if (reasoningModelBelongsToProvider(currentProvider, currentModel)) {
         memory[`${scope}:${currentProvider}`] = currentModel;
         patch.reasoningModelByProvider = memory;
       }
     } else if (reasoningModelBelongsToProvider(providerId, currentModel)) {
       // Reselecting the current provider with a model it owns: keep it.
       write(patch, keys.provider, providerId);
       return patch;
     }
     const remembered = memory[`${scope}:${providerId}`];
     write(patch, keys.provider, providerId);
     write(
       patch,
       keys.model,
       remembered && reasoningModelBelongsToProvider(providerId, remembered)
         ? remembered
         : fallbackModel
     );
     return patch;
   }
   ```

   Add one queue for complete route patches. The planner is evaluated only when its operation reaches the queue head, and a staged plan passes the exact five-field tuple it reviewed. A stale plan therefore conflicts instead of silently adopting a newer base. `flushRoutePatchSaves` drains until no queued operation was added while waiting.

   ```ts
   let routePatchQueue: Promise<void> = Promise.resolve();

   type RoutePatchOptions = {
     expectedEnterprise?: EnterpriseRouteSettings;
     // Renderer-only admission predicate. Never crosses IPC. Task 7 uses it
     // to prevent a closed/replaced request from sending a patch while queued.
     canCommit?: () => boolean;
   };

   function assertRoutePatchAdmission(options?: RoutePatchOptions): void {
     if (options?.canCommit && !options.canCommit()) {
       throw Object.assign(new Error("Route request was superseded before commit"), {
         code: "ROUTE_PATCH_SUPERSEDED",
       });
     }
   }

   function enqueueRoutePatch<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {
     const queued = routePatchQueue.catch(() => {}).then(operation);
     routePatchQueue = queued.then(() => undefined, () => undefined);
     return queued;
   }

   export async function flushRoutePatchSaves(): Promise<void> {
     for (;;) {
       const pending = routePatchQueue;
       await pending;
       if (pending === routePatchQueue) return;
     }
   }

   function runRoutePatchAtHead(
     buildPatch: (state: SettingsState) => SettingsPatch,
     options?: RoutePatchOptions
   ): Promise<void> {
     return enqueueRoutePatch(async () => {
       // Check before planning and again immediately before the first write.
       // There is no await between the second check and starting IPC.
       assertRoutePatchAdmission(options);
       const state = useSettingsStore.getState();
       await applyRoutePatchNow(buildPatch(state), options);
     });
   }

   async function applyRoutePatchNow(
     patch: SettingsPatch,
     options?: RoutePatchOptions
   ): Promise<void> {
     const entries = Object.entries(patch).filter(([, value]) => value !== undefined);
     for (const [key] of entries) {
       if ((STALE_SECRET_LOCALSTORAGE_KEYS as readonly string[]).includes(key)) {
         throw new Error(`applyRoutePatch: ${key} is a secret and never part of a route patch`);
       }
       if (!ROUTE_PATCH_KEY_SET.has(key)) throw new Error(`applyRoutePatch: ${key} is not a route setting`);
     }
     if (entries.length === 0) return;
     const storeEntries = entries.filter(([key]) => providerSearchScope(key) === null);
     const enterpriseEntries = storeEntries.filter(([key]) => ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS.includes(key as RouteEnterpriseKey));
     // A queued stale request may fail closed here without contacting main or
     // writing local state. Once saveEnterpriseRoutePatch starts, however, an
     // ACK is durable and must be reflected even if the request later expires.
     assertRoutePatchAdmission(options);
     if (enterpriseEntries.length > 0 && isBrowser) {
       const save = window.electronAPI?.saveEnterpriseRoutePatch;
       if (!save) throw new Error("Enterprise route persistence is unavailable");
       const current = useSettingsStore.getState();
       const expected = options?.expectedEnterprise ?? Object.fromEntries(
         ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS.map((key) => [key, current[key]])
       ) as EnterpriseRouteSettings;
       const enterprisePatch = Object.fromEntries(enterpriseEntries) as Partial<EnterpriseRouteSettings>;
       const ack = await save({ patch: enterprisePatch, expected });
       if (!ack.success) {
         // The canonical tuple came from main after a competing window's
         // commit. Fence Task 3's older startup getter read before refreshing
         // renderer state, or that read could put the stale tuple back.
         noteEnterpriseLocalWrite();
         for (const key of ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS) localStorage.setItem(key, String(ack.current[key]));
         useSettingsStore.setState(ack.current);
         throw Object.assign(new Error("Enterprise route settings changed; review the draft again"), {
           code: "ENTERPRISE_ROUTE_CONFLICT",
           current: ack.current,
         });
       }
       // Task 3's startup sync must not overwrite this newly committed tuple.
       noteEnterpriseLocalWrite();
     }
     for (const [key, value] of storeEntries) {
       if (key === "transcriptionModelByProvider" || key === "reasoningModelByProvider") {
         writeModelMemoryStorage(key, value as Record<string, string>);
       } else if (isBrowser) {
         localStorage.setItem(key, String(value));
       }
     }
     if (storeEntries.length > 0) useSettingsStore.setState(Object.fromEntries(storeEntries) as Partial<SettingsState>);
     for (const [key, value] of entries) {
       const scope = providerSearchScope(key);
       if (scope && isBrowser) writeProviderSearchPreference(scope, value === true);
     }
   }
   ```

```js
  // Change-driving (I5): v1's local target carried no provider/model, so Undo cleared a working local setup.
  await t.test("local → remote → Undo restores the local selection exactly", async () => {

      assert.equal(back.kind, "instant", `${id}: moving back to this device is instant`);

  // Change-driving (I6): v1 resolved only the selected route.

  // Change-driving: blockers are computed over every changed off-device route.
  // R2-9 reversed two v2 exemptions: Codex/enterprise sign-in and the remote
  // model are chosen in the staged editor before Apply, so both now block.
  await t.test("blockers", () => {
    reset();
    const noOpenAiKey = { facts: { credentials: new Map([["openai", false]]) } };
    assert.equal(plan("dictationStt", { mode: "providers", provider: "openai" }, noOpenAiKey).blocker, "needsKey");
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "codex" }).blocker, "needsKey", "R2-9: Codex signs in before Apply");
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "bedrock" }).blocker, "needsKey", "R2-9: no enterprise exemption");
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "" }).blocker, "chooseProvider");
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "self-hosted", remoteUrl: "", model: "llama3" }).blocker, "needsUrl");
    assert.equal(plan("dictationStt", { mode: "providers", provider: "groq" }, { sealed: true }).blocker, "sealed");
    assert.equal(plan("dictationStt", { mode: "providers", provider: "groq" }, { facts: { credentials: null } }).blocker, "unknown");
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "openai", model: "" }).blocker, "needsModel", "R2-9: the model is chosen before Apply");
    const azureNoEndpoint = plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "azure", model: "gpt-4o-deploy" }, {
      facts: { credentials: new Map([["azure", true]]) },
    });
    assert.equal(azureNoEndpoint.blocker, "needsUrl", "R2-1: a saved Azure key without an endpoint cannot apply");
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "openai" }).blocker, null, "ready routes never block");
    reset(OPENAI_CHAT);
    const home = plan("chat", { mode: "local" }, { sealed: true });
    assert.equal(home.blocker, null, "moving onto the device is never blocked");
    assert.equal(home.kind, "instant");
  });

  await t.test("planPatch refuses keys outside the route settings", () => {
    reset();

  // R2-1: the enterprise fields were direct setter writes (EnterpriseProviderConfig.tsx:114-118,
  // 145-148,166-174) that settingsStore.ts:2060-2063 persisted to main at once.
  const AZURE = { mode: "enterprise", provider: "azure", model: "gpt-4o-deploy" };
  const azureScope = (prefix) => ({
    [`${prefix}Mode`]: AZURE.mode,
    [`${prefix}Provider`]: AZURE.provider,
    [`${prefix}Model`]: AZURE.model,
  });
  const azureKey = {
    facts: { credentials: new Map([["azure", true]]), credentialFields: new Map([["azure", { key: true }]]) },
  };

  // Change-driving (R2-1): v2's allowlist refused azureEndpoint and the graph gave Azure no host.
  await t.test("an Azure endpoint change on the active route is an off-device recipient change: it stages", async () => {
    reset({ ...azureScope("chatAgent"), azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    const p = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(azureKey), "chat", { azureEndpoint: "https://other.example.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(p.kind, "staged");
    assert.deepEqual(p.changes.map((c) => c.id), ["chat"]);
    assert.equal(change(p, "chat").before.host, "myres.openai.azure.com");
    assert.equal(change(p, "chat").after.host, "other.example.com");
    assert.equal(p.blocker, null, "the new endpoint is valid and the key is saved");
    assert.deepEqual(p.patch, { azureEndpoint: "https://other.example.com/openai" });
    assert.deepEqual(p.undoPatch, { azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(live().azureEndpoint, "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai", "planning commits nothing");

    const refused = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(azureKey), "chat", { azureEndpoint: "http://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(change(refused, "chat").after.host, null);
    assert.equal(refused.blocker, "needsUrl", "Apply waits for an endpoint the executor accepts");

    const samePlace = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(azureKey), "chat", { azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai/" });
    assert.equal(samePlace.kind, "instant", "a path-only edit keeps the recipient");
    assert.deepEqual(samePlace.changes, []);

    await live().applyRoutePatch(p.patch);
    assert.equal(resolveLive().find((r) => r.id === "chat").host, "other.example.com", "commit is the preview");
    await live().applyRoutePatch(p.undoPatch);
    assert.equal(live().azureEndpoint, "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai", "Undo restores the endpoint exactly");

    reset({ azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    const unused = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(azureKey), "chat", { azureEndpoint: "https://other.example.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(unused.kind, "instant", "no route uses Azure, so nothing new is sent");
    assert.deepEqual(unused.changes, []);
  });

  // Change-driving (R2-1 staging gap): until Task 3 has synced facts.enterpriseMain, or while
  // Vertex's key presence is still null, enterprise routes resolve `unknown` with host null on
  // both sides. The v2 planner compared null === null (and the fingerprints were equal), so an
  // endpoint, region or location edit was instant and committed without review.
  await t.test("an enterprise recipient edit stages while the graph cannot name the host", () => {
    const unsynced = { facts: { ...azureKey.facts, enterpriseMain: null } };
    reset({ ...azureScope("chatAgent"), azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    const p = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(unsynced), "chat", { azureEndpoint: "https://other.example.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(p.kind, "staged", "an unnamed recipient is never assumed to be the same one");
    assert.deepEqual(p.changes.map((c) => c.id), ["chat"]);
    assert.equal(change(p, "chat").before.host, null);
    assert.equal(change(p, "chat").after.host, null);
    assert.equal(change(p, "chat").after.state.status, "unknown");
    assert.equal(p.blocker, "unknown", "Apply waits until main's facts are synced");
    assert.deepEqual(p.patch, { azureEndpoint: "https://other.example.com/openai" });
    assert.deepEqual(p.undoPatch, { azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(live().azureEndpoint, "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai", "planning commits nothing");

    // A Bedrock region edit, with its coupled model rewrite, stages too.
    reset({ bedrockRegion: "us-east-1", chatAgentMode: "enterprise", chatAgentProvider: "bedrock", chatAgentModel: "us.anthropic.claude-fable-5" });
    const region = planner.planPatch(
      live(),
      ctx({ facts: { credentials: new Map([["bedrock", true]]), enterpriseMain: null } }),
      "chat",
      { bedrockRegion: "eu-west-1" }
    );
    assert.equal(region.kind, "staged");
    assert.equal(region.blocker, "unknown");
    assert.deepEqual(region.patch, { bedrockRegion: "eu-west-1", chatAgentModel: "eu.anthropic.claude-fable-5" });

    // Baseline guards: what was instant stays instant while the facts load.
    reset({ azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    const unused = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(unsynced), "chat", { azureEndpoint: "https://other.example.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(unused.kind, "instant", "no route uses Azure, so nothing is sent whatever the facts");
    assert.deepEqual(unused.changes, []);
    reset(OPENAI_CHAT);
    assert.equal(
      plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "openai", model: "gpt-5.6-sol" }, { facts: { enterpriseMain: null } }).kind,
      "instant",
      "a model change at the same provider and host does not wait for enterprise facts"
    );
    reset({ ...azureScope("chatAgent"), azureEndpoint: "https://myres.openai.azure.com/openai" });
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "local" }, unsynced).kind, "instant", "moving onto the device is instant");
  });

  await t.test("Vertex source edits stage across coupled active routes and Apply/Undo use that exact source", async () => {
    reset({
      chatAgentMode: "enterprise", chatAgentProvider: "vertex", chatAgentModel: "gemini-2.5-flash",
      noteFormattingMode: "enterprise", noteFormattingProvider: "vertex", noteFormattingModel: "gemini-2.5-flash",
      vertexProject: "acme-prod", vertexLocation: "europe-west4", vertexAuthSource: "adc",
    });

    assert.equal(p.kind, "staged");
    assert.deepEqual(p.changes.map((c) => c.id), ["chat", "noteFormatting"]);
    for (const c of p.changes) {
      assert.equal(c.before.host, "europe-west4-aiplatform.googleapis.com", c.id);
      assert.equal(c.after.host, "aiplatform.googleapis.com", c.id);
      assert.deepEqual(c.after.state, { status: "ready" }, c.id);
    }
    assert.equal(p.blocker, null);
    assert.deepEqual(p.patch, { vertexAuthSource: "apiKey" });
    assert.deepEqual(p.undoPatch, { vertexAuthSource: "adc" });
    assert.equal(live().vertexAuthSource, "adc", "planning leaves main/store unchanged");
    await live().applyRoutePatch(p.patch);
    assert.equal(resolveLive().find((r) => r.id === "chat").host, "aiplatform.googleapis.com", "Apply commits the previewed recipient");
    await live().applyRoutePatch(p.undoPatch);
    assert.equal(live().vertexAuthSource, "adc", "Undo restores the committed source");
    assert.equal(resolveLive().find((r) => r.id === "chat").host, "europe-west4-aiplatform.googleapis.com");
  });

  // Change-driving (R2-1): the region's model rewrite lived only in EnterpriseProviderConfig.tsx:115-118.
  await t.test("a Bedrock region change adds the model adjustment to the same patch, and Undo is exact", async () => {
    const bedrockKey = { facts: { credentials: new Map([["bedrock", true]]) } };
    reset({
      bedrockRegion: "us-east-1",
      chatAgentMode: "enterprise",
      chatAgentProvider: "bedrock",
      chatAgentModel: "us.anthropic.claude-fable-5",
      noteFormattingMode: "enterprise",
      noteFormattingProvider: "bedrock",
      noteFormattingModel: "anthropic.claude-3-haiku", // on-demand id: valid in every region
    });
    const before = routeKeys();
    const p = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(bedrockKey), "chat", { bedrockRegion: "eu-west-1" });
    assert.deepEqual(p.patch, { bedrockRegion: "eu-west-1", chatAgentModel: "eu.anthropic.claude-fable-5" });
    assert.deepEqual(p.undoPatch, {
      bedrockRegion: "us-east-1",
      chatAgentModel: "us.anthropic.claude-fable-5",
      noteFormattingModel: "anthropic.claude-3-haiku", // pinned: a re-planned Undo must not rewrite it
    });
    assert.equal(p.kind, "staged");
    const chat = change(p, "chat");
    assert.equal(chat.coupled, false);
    assert.equal(chat.before.host, "bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com");
    assert.equal(chat.after.host, "bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com");
    assert.equal(chat.after.model, "eu.anthropic.claude-fable-5", "the preview shows the adjusted model");
    assert.equal(change(p, "noteFormatting").coupled, true, "the other Bedrock route changes region too");
    assert.equal(change(p, "noteFormatting").after.host, "bedrock-runtime.eu-west-1.amazonaws.com");

    await live().applyRoutePatch(p.patch);
    assert.equal(live().chatAgentModel, "eu.anthropic.claude-fable-5");
    // Task 7's Undo re-plans the undoPatch against the live state.
    const back = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(bedrockKey), "chat", p.undoPatch);
    assert.deepEqual(back.patch, { bedrockRegion: "us-east-1", chatAgentModel: "us.anthropic.claude-fable-5" });
    await live().applyRoutePatch(back.patch);
    assert.deepEqual(routeKeys(), before, "every key restored");

    // A profile id that never matched its region is restored too, not "fixed" by the Undo.
    reset({ bedrockRegion: "us-east-1", chatAgentMode: "enterprise", chatAgentProvider: "bedrock", chatAgentModel: "eu.anthropic.claude-fable-5" });
    const mismatched = routeKeys();
    const forward = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(bedrockKey), "chat", { bedrockRegion: "eu-west-1" });
    assert.deepEqual(forward.patch, { bedrockRegion: "eu-west-1" }, "already an eu.* id");
    await live().applyRoutePatch(forward.patch);
    await live().applyRoutePatch(planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(bedrockKey), "chat", forward.undoPatch).patch);
    assert.deepEqual(routeKeys(), mismatched);

    // Switching to Bedrock picks the profile id for the region the state holds.
    reset({ bedrockRegion: "eu-west-1" });
    assert.equal(plan("chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "bedrock" }, bedrockKey).patch.chatAgentModel, "eu.anthropic.claude-fable-5");
  });


  // Change-driving (I1 follow-up): v1's allowlist refused the enable switches,
  // so the editors wrote them directly and turning a cloud route on sent data unreviewed.
  await t.test("enable switches: turning an off-device route on stages; turning it off is instant", () => {
    const cases = [
      ["useCleanupModel", "dictationCleanup", { cleanupMode: "providers", cleanupProvider: "openai", cleanupModel: "gpt-6-astra" }],
      ["useDictationTranslation", "translation", { translationMode: "providers", translationProvider: "openai", translationModel: "gpt-6-astra" }],
    ];
    for (const [key, id, cloud] of cases) {
      reset({ ...cloud, [key]: false });
      const on = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), id, { [key]: true });
      assert.equal(on.kind, "staged", `${key}: on sends to OpenAI`);
      assert.deepEqual(on.changes.map((c) => c.id), [id]);
      assert.equal(change(on, id).before.state.status, "off");
      assert.equal(change(on, id).after.providerId, "openai");
      assert.deepEqual(on.undoPatch, { [key]: false });
      assert.equal(on.blocker, null);
      const noKey = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx({ facts: { credentials: new Map([["openai", false]]) } }), id, { [key]: true });
      assert.equal(noKey.blocker, "needsKey", `${key}: Apply waits for the key`);

      reset(cloud);
      const off = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), id, { [key]: false });
      assert.equal(off.kind, "instant", `${key}: off sends nothing`);
      assert.equal(change(off, id).after.state.status, "off");

      reset({ [key]: false });
      assert.equal(planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), id, { [key]: true }).kind, "instant", `${key}: an on-device route turns on at once`);
      assert.equal(planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), id, { [key]: false }).kind, "noop");
    }
  });

  // Change-driving (I1 follow-up): the assistant's switches change who receives screenshots.
  await t.test("assistant switches: screen context adds the screenshot; the vision override moves it", async () => {
    const cloudAssistant = { dictationAgentMode: "providers", dictationAgentProvider: "openai", dictationAgentModel: "gpt-6-astra" };
    reset({ ...cloudAssistant, voiceAgentScreenContext: false });
    const screen = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "voiceAssistant", { voiceAgentScreenContext: true });
    assert.equal(screen.kind, "staged");
    assert.doesNotMatch(change(screen, "voiceAssistant").before.sends, /<screenshot>/);
    assert.match(change(screen, "voiceAssistant").after.sends, /<screenshot>/);
    assert.equal(change(screen, "assistantVision").coupled, true, "the vision route turns on with it");

    reset({ ...cloudAssistant, useDictationAgent: false });
    assert.equal(planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "voiceAssistant", { useDictationAgent: true }).kind, "staged");
    reset(cloudAssistant);
    const off = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "voiceAssistant", { useDictationAgent: false });
    assert.equal(off.kind, "instant");
    assert.deepEqual(off.changes.map((c) => [c.id, c.after.state.status]), [["voiceAssistant", "off"], ["assistantVision", "off"]]);

    // The override is not an off switch: either direction can hand screenshots to another provider.
    reset({ ...cloudAssistant, dictationAgentVisionProvider: "anthropic", dictationAgentVisionModel: "claude-fable-5-1" });
    const override = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "assistantVision", { useDictationAgentVisionModel: true });
    assert.equal(override.kind, "staged", "screenshots move to Anthropic");
    assert.equal(change(override, "assistantVision").after.providerId, "anthropic");
    await live().applyRoutePatch(override.patch);
    const follow = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "assistantVision", { useDictationAgentVisionModel: false });
    assert.equal(follow.kind, "staged", "following the assistant again sends screenshots to OpenAI");
    assert.equal(change(follow, "assistantVision").after.providerId, "openai");
  });

  // Change-driving (I1 follow-up): v1 had no Corti host input, so a region switch changed the recipient silently.
  await t.test("the Corti region picks the receiving host, so switching it stages", () => {
    const corti = {
      transcriptionMode: "providers",
      useLocalWhisper: false,
      cloudTranscriptionProvider: "corti",
      cloudTranscriptionModel: "corti-transcribe",
    };
    const cortiKeys = { facts: { credentials: new Map([["corti:speech", true]]) } };
    reset(corti);
    const eu = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(cortiKeys), "dictationStt", { cortiEnvironment: "eu" });
    assert.equal(eu.kind, "staged");
    assert.equal(change(eu, "dictationStt").before.host, "api.us.corti.app");
    assert.equal(change(eu, "dictationStt").after.host, "api.eu.corti.app");
    assert.deepEqual(eu.undoPatch, { cortiEnvironment: "us" });

    const tenant = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(cortiKeys), "dictationStt", { cortiTenant: "acme" });
    assert.equal(tenant.kind, "instant", "the tenant picks an account on the same host");
    assert.deepEqual(tenant.changes, []);

    reset();
    assert.equal(planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "dictationStt", { cortiEnvironment: "eu" }).kind, "instant", "no route uses Corti");

    // Corti text always calls ai.eu.corti.app (Task 1/3's providerHosts["corti:text"]), so the region moves no text route.
    reset({ chatAgentMode: "providers", chatAgentProvider: "corti", chatAgentModel: "corti-chat" });
    const text = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx({ facts: { credentials: new Map([["corti:text", true]]) } }), "chat", { cortiEnvironment: "eu" });
    assert.equal(text.kind, "instant", "a text-only Corti profile keeps its recipient");
    assert.deepEqual(text.changes, []);
  });

  // Change-driving (I1 follow-up): the toggle wrote localStorage directly and added webSearch unreviewed.
  await t.test("provider web search: on adds a payload part and stages; off is instant", async () => {
    const key = "providerSearch:chatIntelligence";
    reset(OPENAI_CHAT);
    const on = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "chat", { [key]: true });
    assert.equal(on.kind, "staged");
    assert.doesNotMatch(change(on, "chat").before.sends, /<webSearch>/);
    assert.match(change(on, "chat").after.sends, /<webSearch>/);
    assert.deepEqual(on.undoPatch, { [key]: false }, "Undo restores the stored preference");

    await live().applyRoutePatch(on.patch);
    assert.equal(storage.getItem("personalWebSearch:chatIntelligence"), "true");
    assert.equal(planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "chat", { [key]: true }).kind, "noop");
    const off = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "chat", { [key]: false });
    assert.equal(off.kind, "instant");
    assert.doesNotMatch(change(off, "chat").after.sends, /<webSearch>/);

    reset({ chatAgentMode: "providers", chatAgentProvider: "groq", chatAgentModel: "openai/gpt-oss-120b" });
    const groq = planner.planPatch(live(), ctx(), "chat", { [key]: true });
    assert.equal(groq.kind, "instant", "Groq has no native search, so nothing new is sent");
    assert.deepEqual(groq.changes, []);
  });

  // Change-driving (I5): the preview must be the state that commit produces.
  await t.test("preview equals the state after applying the patch, and Undo returns to the start", async () => {
    const start = {
      transcriptionMode: "providers",
      useLocalWhisper: false,
      meetingTranscriptionMode: "providers",
      meetingUseLocalWhisper: false,
      chatAgentMode: "providers",
      chatAgentProvider: "groq",
      chatAgentModel: "openai/gpt-oss-120b",
      translationMode: "self-hosted",
      translationRemoteUrl: "http://192.168.1.20:11434/v1",
      translationModel: "llama3",
      dictationAgentMode: "providers",
      dictationAgentProvider: "openai",
      dictationAgentModel: "gpt-6-astra",
      reasoningModelByProvider: { "chatIntelligence:anthropic": "claude-sonnet-5" },
    };
    const targets = [
      ["dictationStt", { mode: "providers", provider: "groq" }],
      ["dictationStt", { mode: "providers", provider: "openai", model: "gpt-4o-transcribe" }],
      ["dictationStt", { mode: "local", provider: "nvidia", model: "parakeet-unified-en-0.6b" }],
      ["uploadStt", { mode: "providers", provider: "groq", model: "whisper-large-v3-turbo" }],
      ["noteRecordingStt", { mode: "providers", provider: "deepgram" }],
      ["chat", { mode: "providers", provider: "anthropic" }],
      ["chat", { mode: "self-hosted", remoteUrl: "http://192.168.1.40:8080/v1", model: "mistral" }],
      ["translation", { mode: "providers", provider: "custom", baseUrl: "http://localhost:1234/v1", model: "m" }],
      ["voiceAssistant", { mode: "local", provider: "qwen", model: QWEN }],
      ["assistantVision", { mode: "providers", provider: "bedrock" }],
      ["dictationCleanup", { mode: "providers", provider: "openai" }],
    ];
    for (const [id, target] of targets) {
      reset(start);
      const before = resolveLive();
      const p = plan(id, target);
      await live().applyRoutePatch(p.patch);
      for (const route of resolveLive()) {
        const c = change(p, route.id);
        const expected = c ? c.after : before.find((r) => r.id === route.id);
        assert.deepEqual(route, expected, `${id} → ${JSON.stringify(target)}: ${route.id}`);
        if (c) assert.deepEqual(c.before, before.find((r) => r.id === route.id));
      }
      await live().applyRoutePatch(p.undoPatch);
      assert.deepEqual(resolveLive(), before, `${id}: Undo returns every route`);
    }
  });
});
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Run the tests to verify they fail**

Run: `npm test -- test/lib/routePlanner.test.js`
Expected: FAIL, because `/lib/routePlanner.ts` does not exist. Every subtest above is change-driving, and the reason is stated on each. The four I1 follow-up subtests (enable switches, assistant switches, Corti region, provider web search) also depend on Step 3's allowlist and on Task 3's builder deriving `providerHosts.corti` from `cortiEnvironment`. The three R2-1 subtests (Azure endpoint staging, coupled-route review, Bedrock region coupling with exact Undo) depend on Step 3's `ROUTE_ENTERPRISE_KEYS`/`planEnterpriseCoupling` and on Tasks 1 and 3 deriving enterprise hosts from `snapshot.enterprise`; the reversed `blockers` assertions (Codex/Bedrock `needsKey`, remote `needsModel`, Azure `needsUrl`) are R2-9/R2-1 change-driving against v2's exemptions. The two R2-1 staging-gap subtests ("an enterprise recipient edit stages while the graph cannot name the host", "a Vertex location edit stages while Vertex's key presence is unknown") fail against the c912d19 planner even once the module exists: with `enterpriseMain: null` or Vertex presence `null` the before and after fingerprints are equal, `changes` is empty and the plan is `instant`. Their baseline-guard lines (unused Azure field, same-host model change, on-device move) pass on both.

- [ ] **Step 8: Implement the planner**

Create `src/lib/routePlanner.ts`:

```ts
import { INFERENCE_SCOPES } from "../config/inferenceScopes";
import { isProviderValidForMode } from "../models/ModelRegistry";
import type { SettingsState } from "../stores/settingsStore";
import type { EnterpriseRouteSettings, InferenceMode, LocalTranscriptionProvider } from "../types/electron";
import { adjustBedrockModelForRegion } from "../utils/bedrockRegions";
import { readProviderSearchPreference, supportsProviderSearch } from "../utils/providerSearch";
import {
  ENTERPRISE_PROVIDER_IDS,
  ROUTE_PATCH_KEY_SET,
  bedrockCoupledModelKeys,
  defaultCloudModel,
  planEnterpriseCoupling,
  planReasoningProviderSwitch,
  planTranscriptionProviderSwitch,
  providerSearchScope,
  resolvedScopeField,
  type SettingsPatch,
} from "./providerSwitchPlans";
import {
  buildRouteSnapshot,
  resolveRoutes,
  routePayloadParts,
  type LlmRouteScope,
  type ResolvedRoute,
  type RouteCopy,
  type RouteFacts,
  type RouteId,
  type RouteSettingsSnapshot,
  type SttContext,
} from "./routes";

// The route planner (SET-R3 B). One simulated patch is the preview, the
// commit and (through undoPatch) the Undo, so they cannot disagree. It lists
// every route among the 11 whose effective result changes, including routes
// coupled by inheritance. Pure: it never writes the store.

export type RouteTarget =
  | { mode: "local"; provider?: string; model?: string }
  | { mode: "providers"; provider: string; model?: string; baseUrl?: string } // enterprise providers map to mode "enterprise"
  | { mode: "self-hosted"; remoteUrl: string; model?: string };

export interface RouteChange {
  id: RouteId;
  before: ResolvedRoute;
  after: ResolvedRoute;
  coupled: boolean; // not the requested route
}

export type ApplyBlocker =
  | "needsKey"
  | "chooseProvider"
  | "needsUrl"
  | "needsModel"
  | "sealed"
  | "unknown"
  | "unsupported";

export interface RoutePlan {
  routeId: RouteId;
  enterpriseBase: EnterpriseRouteSettings; // exact non-secret tuple this preview/review was computed against; Task 7 passes it unchanged to the main CAS
  patch: SettingsPatch;
  undoPatch: SettingsPatch;
  changes: RouteChange[];
  kind: "noop" | "instant" | "staged";
  blocker: ApplyBlocker | null;
}

export interface PlanContext {
  facts: RouteFacts;
  copy: RouteCopy;
  sealed: boolean;
}

// Providers whose setup (Codex sign-in; enterprise endpoint, region, project
// and credentials) happens in the provider editor, which the staged editor
// shows before Apply (R2-9). Copy only ("sign in here first", Task 8): it
// never unblocks Apply.
export const SETUP_AFTER_APPLY: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set(["codex", ...ENTERPRISE_PROVIDER_IDS]);

type Patch = Record<string, unknown>;
type ProvidersTarget = Extract<RouteTarget, { mode: "providers" }>;

const STT_CONTEXT_OF: Partial<Record<RouteId, SttContext>> = {
  dictationStt: "dictation",
  noteRecordingStt: "meeting",
  uploadStt: "upload",
};

const LLM_SCOPE_OF: Partial<Record<RouteId, LlmRouteScope>> = {
  dictationCleanup: "dictationCleanup",
  voiceAssistant: "dictationAgent",
  assistantVision: "dictationAgentVision",
  translation: "dictationTranslation",
  noteFormatting: "noteFormatting",
  chat: "chatIntelligence",
};

interface SttKeys {
  mode: keyof SettingsState;
  useLocal: keyof SettingsState;
  cloudMode: keyof SettingsState;
  localProvider: keyof SettingsState;
  localModel: Record<LocalTranscriptionProvider, keyof SettingsState>;
  cloudProvider: keyof SettingsState;
  cloudModel: keyof SettingsState;
  cloudBaseUrl: keyof SettingsState;
  remoteUrl: keyof SettingsState | null;
  remoteModel: keyof SettingsState | null;
}

// The keys each STT context's mode handler writes (SettingsPage.tsx:526-533,
// MeetingSettings.tsx:87-95, UploadSettings.tsx:68-74).
const STT_KEYS: Record<SttContext, SttKeys> = {
  dictation: {
    mode: "transcriptionMode",
    useLocal: "useLocalWhisper",
    cloudMode: "cloudTranscriptionMode",
    localProvider: "localTranscriptionProvider",
    localModel: { whisper: "whisperModel", nvidia: "parakeetModel", cohere: "cohereModel" },
    cloudProvider: "cloudTranscriptionProvider",
    cloudModel: "cloudTranscriptionModel",
    cloudBaseUrl: "cloudTranscriptionBaseUrl",
    remoteUrl: "remoteTranscriptionUrl",
    remoteModel: "remoteTranscriptionModel",
  },
  meeting: {
    mode: "meetingTranscriptionMode",
    useLocal: "meetingUseLocalWhisper",
    cloudMode: "meetingCloudTranscriptionMode",
    localProvider: "meetingLocalTranscriptionProvider",
    localModel: { whisper: "meetingWhisperModel", nvidia: "meetingParakeetModel", cohere: "meetingCohereModel" },
    cloudProvider: "meetingCloudTranscriptionProvider",
    cloudModel: "meetingCloudTranscriptionModel",
    cloudBaseUrl: "meetingCloudTranscriptionBaseUrl",
    remoteUrl: "meetingRemoteTranscriptionUrl",
    remoteModel: null,
  },
  // Upload has no server of its own. It reads dictation's URL and model
  // (UploadSettings.tsx:132-138), so an upload target never writes them.
  upload: {
    mode: "uploadTranscriptionMode",
    useLocal: "uploadUseLocalWhisper",
    cloudMode: "uploadCloudTranscriptionMode",
    localProvider: "uploadLocalTranscriptionProvider",
    localModel: { whisper: "uploadWhisperModel", nvidia: "uploadParakeetModel", cohere: "uploadCohereModel" },
    cloudProvider: "uploadCloudTranscriptionProvider",
    cloudModel: "uploadCloudTranscriptionModel",
    cloudBaseUrl: "uploadCloudTranscriptionBaseUrl",
    remoteUrl: null,
    remoteModel: null,
  },
};

const merged = (state: SettingsState, patch: Patch) => ({ ...state, ...patch }) as SettingsState;

function sttTargetPatch(state: SettingsState, context: SttContext, target: RouteTarget): Patch {
  const k = STT_KEYS[context];
  const patch: Patch = {
    [k.mode]: target.mode,
    [k.useLocal]: target.mode === "local",
    [k.cloudMode]: "byok",
  };
  if (target.mode === "local") {
    if (target.provider !== undefined) patch[k.localProvider] = target.provider;
    if (target.model !== undefined) {
      const provider = (target.provider ?? state[k.localProvider]) as LocalTranscriptionProvider;
      patch[k.localModel[provider] ?? k.localModel.whisper] = target.model;
    }
    return patch;
  }
  if (target.mode === "providers") {
    if (target.provider) {
      Object.assign(patch, planTranscriptionProviderSwitch(merged(state, patch), context, target.provider));
    } else {
      patch[k.cloudProvider] = "";
    }
    if (target.model !== undefined) patch[k.cloudModel] = target.model;
    if (target.baseUrl !== undefined) patch[k.cloudBaseUrl] = target.baseUrl;
    return patch;
  }
  if (k.remoteUrl) patch[k.remoteUrl] = target.remoteUrl;
  if (k.remoteModel && target.model !== undefined) patch[k.remoteModel] = target.model;
  return patch;
}

function providerPatch(
  state: SettingsState,
  scope: LlmRouteScope,
  target: ProvidersTarget,
  options: { vision: boolean; mode: InferenceMode }
): Patch {
  const keys = INFERENCE_SCOPES[scope].storeKeys as Record<string, string>;
  let patch: Patch;
  if (target.provider) {
    patch = {
      ...planReasoningProviderSwitch(
        state,
        scope,
        target.provider,
        defaultCloudModel(target.provider, { vision: options.vision })
      ),
    };
  } else {
    // "Choose a provider". Like InferenceConfigEditor.tsx:109-112, a model
    // whose provider the new mode cannot use goes with it.
    patch = { [keys.provider]: "" };
    if (!isProviderValidForMode(resolvedScopeField(state, scope, "provider"), options.mode)) {
      patch[keys.model] = "";
    }
  }
  if (target.model !== undefined) {
    patch[keys.model] = target.model;
  } else if (target.provider === "bedrock" && typeof patch[keys.model] === "string") {
    // R2-1: a remembered or default Bedrock profile id follows the region the
    // state holds (bedrockRegions.ts), so switching to Bedrock in eu-west-1 never
    // previews or commits a us.* profile. A caller that stages a region together
    // with a target plans the target against the state with that region applied.
    patch[keys.model] = adjustBedrockModelForRegion(patch[keys.model] as string, state.bedrockRegion || "us-east-1");
  }
  if (target.baseUrl !== undefined && keys.cloudBaseUrl) patch[keys.cloudBaseUrl] = target.baseUrl;
  return patch;
}

function llmTargetPatch(state: SettingsState, scope: LlmRouteScope, target: RouteTarget): Patch {
  const keys = INFERENCE_SCOPES[scope].storeKeys as Record<string, string>;

  if (scope === "dictationAgentVision") {
    if (target.mode !== "providers") {
      throw new Error("Assistant vision runs on a provider: use a providers target");
    }
    // Only the override flag and the vision provider, model and endpoint. Never
    // screen context, never the vision mode (settingsStore.ts:1757-1758).
    const patch: Patch = {
      useDictationAgentVisionModel: true,
      ...providerPatch(state, scope, target, { vision: true, mode: "providers" }),
    };
    // dictationAgentInference.js:72 treats the override as chosen only when
    // its own model is set; a switch that keeps the inherited model must write it.
    const after = merged(state, patch);
    if (!after.dictationAgentVisionModel) {
      patch.dictationAgentVisionModel =
        resolvedScopeField(after, scope, "model") ||
        defaultCloudModel(target.provider, { vision: true });
    }
    return patch;
  }

  const currentMode = state[keys.mode as keyof SettingsState] as InferenceMode;

  if (target.mode === "local") {
    const patch: Patch = { [keys.mode]: "local", [keys.cloudMode]: "byok" };
    if (target.provider !== undefined) {
      const current = resolvedScopeField(state, scope, "provider");
      patch[keys.provider] = target.provider;
      patch[keys.model] =
        target.model ?? (target.provider === current ? resolvedScopeField(state, scope, "model") : "");
      return patch;
    }
    // InferenceConfigEditor.tsx:109-112: a provider the new mode cannot use is cleared with its model.
    if (!isProviderValidForMode(resolvedScopeField(state, scope, "provider"), "local")) {
      patch[keys.provider] = "";
      patch[keys.model] = "";
    }
    if (target.model !== undefined) patch[keys.model] = target.model;
    return patch;
  }

  if (target.mode === "self-hosted") {
    const patch: Patch = {
      [keys.mode]: "self-hosted",
      [keys.cloudMode]: "byok",
      [keys.remoteUrl]: target.remoteUrl,
    };
    // A cloud or local model id means nothing to your server.
    if (target.model !== undefined) patch[keys.model] = target.model;
    else if (currentMode !== "self-hosted") patch[keys.model] = "";
    return patch;
  }

  const mode: InferenceMode = ENTERPRISE_PROVIDER_IDS.has(target.provider) ? "enterprise" : "providers";
  const patch: Patch = { [keys.mode]: mode, [keys.cloudMode]: "byok" };
  return Object.assign(patch, providerPatch(merged(state, patch), scope, target, { vision: false, mode }));
}

function sameValue(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean {
  if ((a && typeof a === "object") || (b && typeof b === "object")) {
    return JSON.stringify(a ?? null) === JSON.stringify(b ?? null);
  }
  return a === b;
}

function fingerprint(route: ResolvedRoute): string {
  return JSON.stringify([route.locality, route.providerId, route.host, route.model, route.sends, route.state]);
}

// The value a patch key holds now. The web-search preference is not a store
// field; its current value is the localStorage preference.
function currentValue(state: SettingsState, key: string): unknown {
  const scope = providerSearchScope(key);
  return scope ? readProviderSearchPreference(scope) : (state as unknown as Patch)[key];
}

// buildRouteSnapshot reads the web-search preference from localStorage, which
// a simulated patch has not written. Apply the patched preference here, with
// the request path's own support rule, so the preview is what commit sends.
function withPatchedSearch(snapshot: RouteSettingsSnapshot, written: Patch): RouteSettingsSnapshot {
  let llm = snapshot.llm;
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(written)) {
    const scope = providerSearchScope(key);
    if (!scope) continue;
    const input = llm[scope];
    llm = {
      ...llm,
      [scope]: {
        ...input,
        providerSearch: value === true && supportsProviderSearch(scope, input.provider, input.mode),
      },
    };
  }
  return llm === snapshot.llm ? snapshot : { ...snapshot, llm };
}

// Instant when nothing new leaves the device: the route is off or ends on the
// device, or it keeps the same recipient (locality, provider and host) and
// its payload did not grow. Turning on a route that leaves the device adds a
// recipient. An off-device recipient the graph cannot name (host null, or
// state `unknown`) is never assumed to be the same one (R2-1 staging gap).
function addsNoRecipientOrPayload(
  change: RouteChange,
  beforeSnapshot: RouteSettingsSnapshot,
  afterSnapshot: RouteSettingsSnapshot
): boolean {
  const { before, after } = change;
  // An off route sends nothing, whatever it is configured to use.
  if (after.state.status === "off") return true;
  if (after.locality === "device") return true;
  if (before.state.status === "off") return false;
  // R2-1 staging gap: until Task 3 syncs facts.enterpriseMain, and while
  // Vertex's key presence is null, enterprise routes resolve `unknown` with
  // host null on both sides, so null === null let an Azure endpoint, Bedrock
  // region or Vertex location edit commit unreviewed. An unnamed recipient is
  // a recipient change: the edit stages, and Apply's `unknown` blocker holds
  // it until the facts load.
  if (before.host === null || after.host === null) return false;
  if (before.state.status === "unknown" || after.state.status === "unknown") return false;
  if (
    after.locality !== before.locality ||
    after.providerId !== before.providerId ||
    after.host !== before.host
  ) {
    return false;
  }
  const had = new Set<string>(routePayloadParts(change.id, beforeSnapshot));
  return routePayloadParts(change.id, afterSnapshot).every((part) => had.has(part));
}

// R2-1 staging gap: the enterprise settings each provider's host is derived
// from (Task 1's enterpriseRequestHost). While a route's recipient is unnamed,
// both fingerprints read `unknown`/null whatever these hold, so a write to one
// of them is listed as a change explicitly; otherwise it would never reach
// addsNoRecipientOrPayload and the empty change list would read as instant.
const ENTERPRISE_RECIPIENT_KEYS: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> = {
  bedrock: ["bedrockRegion"],
  azure: ["azureEndpoint"],
  vertex: ["vertexProject", "vertexLocation", "vertexAuthSource"],
};

function recipientUnnamed(route: ResolvedRoute): boolean {
  return (
    route.locality !== "device" &&
    route.state.status !== "off" &&
    (route.host === null || route.state.status === "unknown")
  );
}

function writesRecipientInput(route: ResolvedRoute, written: Patch): boolean {
  const keys = route.providerId ? ENTERPRISE_RECIPIENT_KEYS[route.providerId] : undefined;
  return keys !== undefined && keys.some((key) => key in written);
}

function unnamedRecipientEdit(before: ResolvedRoute, after: ResolvedRoute, written: Patch): boolean {
  return (
    (recipientUnnamed(before) || recipientUnnamed(after)) &&
    (writesRecipientInput(before, written) || writesRecipientInput(after, written))
  );
}

const BLOCKER_PRIORITY: ApplyBlocker[] = [
  "sealed",
  "unknown",
  "chooseProvider",
  "needsKey",
  "needsUrl",
  "unsupported",
  "needsModel",
];

// R2-9: Apply waits until every changed, enabled, off-device route would run.
// Device routes (on-device changes stay instant) and off routes never block.
// Model choice and provider setup (Codex sign-in, enterprise fields, keys,
// Corti fields) are reachable in the staged editor before Apply, so no
// provider is exempt.
function routeBlocker(route: ResolvedRoute): ApplyBlocker | null {
  if (route.locality === "device") return null;
  const state = route.state;
  switch (state.status) {
    case "ready":
    case "off":
      return null;
    case "unknown":
      return "unknown";
    case "needsUrl":
      return "needsUrl";
    case "unreachable":
      return state.detail === "sealed" ? "sealed" : "unsupported";
    case "needsKey":
      return state.provider === "" ? "chooseProvider" : "needsKey";
    case "needsModel":
      return "needsModel";
    default:
      return "unsupported";
  }
}

export function planPatch(
  state: SettingsState,
  ctx: PlanContext,
  routeId: RouteId,
  patch: SettingsPatch
): RoutePlan {
  // R2-1: coupled writes (a Bedrock region's model rewrite) join the patch
  // before diffing, so the preview, the commit and the undoPatch all carry them.
  const expanded: SettingsPatch = { ...patch, ...planEnterpriseCoupling(state, patch) };
  const written: Patch = {};
  const undo: Patch = {};
  for (const [key, value] of Object.entries(expanded)) {
    if (value === undefined) continue;
    if (!ROUTE_PATCH_KEY_SET.has(key)) throw new Error(`Route patches cannot write ${key}`);
    const now = currentValue(state, key);
    if (sameValue(now, value)) continue;
    written[key] = value;
    undo[key] = now;
  }
  // A region change pins every Bedrock model it could rewrite into the Undo
  // (at its current value), so re-planning undoPatch couples nothing new and
  // restores exactly the starting keys, even a profile id that never matched.
  if ("bedrockRegion" in written) {
    for (const key of bedrockCoupledModelKeys(merged(state, written))) {
      if (!(key in undo)) undo[key as string] = state[key];
    }
  }
  const enterpriseBase: EnterpriseRouteSettings = {
    bedrockRegion: state.bedrockRegion || "us-east-1",
    azureEndpoint: state.azureEndpoint || "",
    vertexProject: state.vertexProject || "",
    vertexLocation: state.vertexLocation || "us-central1",
    vertexAuthSource: state.vertexAuthSource,
  };
  if (Object.keys(written).length === 0) {
    return { routeId, enterpriseBase, patch: {}, undoPatch: {}, changes: [], kind: "noop", blocker: null };
  }

  const beforeSnapshot = buildRouteSnapshot(state, ctx.facts, ctx.copy, ctx.sealed);
  const afterSnapshot = withPatchedSearch(
    buildRouteSnapshot(merged(state, written), ctx.facts, ctx.copy, ctx.sealed),
    written
  );
  const afterById = new Map(resolveRoutes(afterSnapshot).map((route) => [route.id, route]));
  const changes: RouteChange[] = [];
  for (const before of resolveRoutes(beforeSnapshot)) {
    const after = afterById.get(before.id);
    if (!after) continue;
    // R2-1 staging gap: an enterprise field edit on a route whose host is not
    // known yet leaves both fingerprints equal; it is still a recipient edit.
    if (fingerprint(after) !== fingerprint(before) || unnamedRecipientEdit(before, after, written)) {
      changes.push({ id: before.id, before, after, coupled: before.id !== routeId });
    }
  }
  changes.sort((a, b) => Number(a.coupled) - Number(b.coupled));

  const instant = changes.every((change) =>
    addsNoRecipientOrPayload(change, beforeSnapshot, afterSnapshot)
  );
  const found = new Set(changes.map((change) => routeBlocker(change.after)));
  const blocker = BLOCKER_PRIORITY.find((candidate) => found.has(candidate)) ?? null;

  return {
    routeId,
    enterpriseBase,
    patch: written as SettingsPatch,
    undoPatch: undo as SettingsPatch,
    changes,
    kind: instant ? "instant" : "staged",
    blocker,
  };
}

export function planRouteChange(
  state: SettingsState,
  ctx: PlanContext,
  id: RouteId,
  target: RouteTarget
): RoutePlan {
  const context = STT_CONTEXT_OF[id];
  const scope = LLM_SCOPE_OF[id];
  if (!context && !scope) {
    throw new Error(`${id} always runs on this device; it has no destination to change`);
  }
  const patch = context ? sttTargetPatch(state, context, target) : llmTargetPatch(state, scope, target);
  return planPatch(state, ctx, id, patch as SettingsPatch);
}
```

Notes for the implementer:
- `routeBlocker` returns null for `off` routes because their state is `off`, so an off route never blocks (Appendix A: "every non-off changed route"). R2-9 removed both exemptions (Codex/enterprise `needsKey`, size-less `needsModel`): the staged editor exposes the model picker and provider setup before Apply (Tasks 7-9).
- `planEnterpriseCoupling` runs before the key check, so a coupled model key is validated like any other. It skips model keys the patch already writes, so `planPatch(live, ctx, id, plan.undoPatch)` (Task 7's Undo) re-plans exactly the undoPatch. A caller that stages a region together with a provider target plans the target against `{ ...state, ...setup }`, so `providerPatch` picks the profile id for the new region.
- `planEnterpriseCoupling` returns nothing when `bedrockRegion` equals the current region, so re-typing the region is still `noop`.
- R2-1 staging gap. Any changed, enabled, off-device route whose before or after `host` is `null`, or whose before or after state is `unknown`, is a recipient change, so the edit stages and Apply's `unknown` (or `needsUrl`) blocker holds it until it is ready. This subsumes v2's narrower custom-endpoint rule. Because an unsynced enterprise route resolves to the same `unknown`/`null` fingerprint whatever its fields hold, `planPatch` also lists a route as changed when its recipient is unnamed and the patch writes one of its provider's `ENTERPRISE_RECIPIENT_KEYS` (Azure `azureEndpoint`, Bedrock `bedrockRegion`, Vertex `vertexProject`/`vertexLocation`). A field nobody uses still changes no route and stays instant. A model change at a known host, on-device moves and switching a route off are untouched.
- Switch semantics come out of `addsNoRecipientOrPayload` with no switch-specific code: a route that ends `off` is instant; a route that goes from `off` to on and leaves the device is staged (the resolver keeps an off route's locality, provider and host, so without the `before.state` check an enable switch would look like "same recipient"). The vision override is not an off switch: turning it either way can hand screenshots to another provider, and the planner stages that like any other recipient change.
- `providerSearch:<scope>` keys read their current value from localStorage (`currentValue`) so `undoPatch` restores the stored preference, and `withPatchedSearch` puts the patched value into the after-snapshot, gated by `supportsProviderSearch` exactly like `isProviderSearchEnabled`.
- The `state.status === …` comparisons narrow explicitly, because `src/tsconfig.json` is not strict.
- `planPatch` drops keys whose value already matches. Re-selecting where a route already runs is therefore `noop`, and `undoPatch` holds exactly the keys that change, plus (R2-1) after a region change every Bedrock model key at its unchanged value, which pins it against coupling when Task 7 re-plans the Undo. Applying such a pinned key writes the value it already has.
- `undoPatch` holds the raw prior value. For inherited meeting and upload fields, that is `""` (inheritance restored). For the vision flags, it is the prior `useDictationAgentVisionModel` and the prior vision provider and model.
